current_state.next: Recon the daemon-side singleton sites and the delegated recovery-scope choice before any implementation
current_state.state_reason: Two exit criteria need someone other than this host: the container e2e suite must run on Linux or CI, which macOS structurally cannot discharge, and the change still needs code review. Everything satisfiable here is green.

entries.note: The export-root declaration lives at ~/.config/sandboxd/export-roots.json — the third sibling of the config dir the CLI already resolves for config.json and presets/ — rather than in the daemon's state tree, because an operator home is 0750 and no other operator can traverse it, so the OS satisfies the 'writable only by its own operator' constraint instead of an ACL we maintain.

The declared set is read and validated by the operator's own agent, not by the daemon: measured on this host the daemon account is outside the operator's home group and cannot traverse it, so it structurally cannot check that a declared root exists, is a directory, or is readable. The new op carries no fields — the agent derives the path from its own environment.

Operator-declared roots apply only when per-operator gateways are on. The daemon-owned singleton keeps its single administrator-set root, because unioning several operators' declarations into one shared VM would export each operator's real project tree to every other operator's sessions.

Schema is a JSON object with a roots array, not a bare top-level array: an object can grow a field under serde default without breaking files written by an older build, and the on-disk compatibility rules in this tree require exactly that. Validation refuses non-absolute paths, non-canonical components, a root of /, and the comma and equals characters that are syntax at the mount sink.

The spec's phase-5 file table lists the fixed-root constant, its env override and the lexical validator for deletion; they are kept this session because the per-operator gateway switch has not flipped, so deleting them would remove shared workspaces from the only mode that currently runs. They are post-flip cleanups, not part of generalising one root into a set.

The macOS lite shared: create path and the container start-time re-check now share one containment helper over the exported root *set*. Root selection is lexical and unique (nesting is refused at declaration), the component scan runs against the selected root, and an Outside verdict is re-checked against the rest of the set so a symlink crossing between two of the same operator's roots is not an escape.

SharedPathError::OutsideRoot stops being the operator-facing outside-the-export refusal: it is handed one root and the question is now about the whole set. The daemon renders its own refusal naming every exported root, how to add one (mode-dependent: the operator's export-roots.json vs the administrator's env var), and the alternatives the old message carried.

The macOS e2e log in the scratchpad (e2e-full-verify.log) finished 2026-08-23 22:37, before commit 14c502a (Aug 24 04:16) and before any of this session's uncommitted work — it cannot verify the export-root change and must not be read as a green run for it.

The Makefile target that creates the fixed shared root is kept, on the same grounds as the fixed-root constant and its env override: it provisions the daemon-owned gateway's single administrator-set root, which is the mode that currently runs and the one the e2e suite mounts. Its comment now says so, since a per-operator gateway does not use that directory at all. Removal is a post-flip cleanup.

The spec's security-posture 'Known deltas' section states the shared gateway-VM blast radius unconditionally ('all gateway containers share one Docker daemon inside the single gateway Lima VM'), which describes only the daemon-owned mode — per-operator gateways give each operator their own VM and Docker daemon, so the cross-session egress-control compromise it describes does not apply there. Recorded rather than edited into the spec.

The macOS e2e suite drives the daemon-owned gateway in default mode, and conftest deliberately keeps that instance across runs; so it cannot cover per-operator export roots at all, and a kept instance also hides the mount-generation path unless the instance is deleted first.

Relaunched the full macOS e2e after deleting the stale e2e gateway VM so the run exercises gateway creation. Compare its failures against the raw pre-run baseline (85 entries), not the regenerated one.

Cold-creating the macOS gateway VM outstrips the first daemon start's patience, so deleting the kept instance makes every e2e test error at fixture setup. The VM does finish booting afterwards, so the recovery is to let it come up and rerun rather than to widen a timeout.

A cold gateway create in default mode emits exactly one 9p mount, the fixed shared root, matching the pre-change configuration; the export-root list generation is therefore correct on the path that only runs at instance creation.

The policy-persistence restart test fails against a freshly created gateway and passes on an immediate rerun, so a cold gateway produces a spurious egress failure that looks like a policy regression. Judge it on a rerun, not a first run.

Full macOS e2e against the committed work: 85 failed, 78 passed, matching the pre-change baseline as a set once two truncated baseline names and one deleted test are accounted for. The single moved test passed on rerun, so there are no regressions.

log.summary: Implemented GatewayManager: create/stop gateway containers on session networks, nftables injection via nsenter into container netns. decisions: Two-NIC approach: eth0=SLIRP (Lima management), eth1=TAP on Docker bridge (data plane). QMP hot-add via ~/.lima/{vm}/qmp.sock after boot. TAP created on host, attached to session bridge. Guest agent configures eth1 with static IP .3, default route to gateway .2.

Lima q35 machine has no PCIe root port — QMP NIC hot-add fails without it. Fixed with QEMU wrapper script that injects pcie-root-port device arg.
Ubuntu 24.04 uses predictable NIC naming — hot-added NIC is enp1s0 not eth1. Guest script now discovers interface by MAC address.
Gateway deny-all nftables input chain blocks DNATed traffic. Added input-allow ruleset for DNS(53) and Envoy(10000) from VM subnet.

log.title: Docker-style session IDs with prefix matching
log.summary: Replaced UUID session IDs with Docker-style 12-hex-char IDs. Added SessionId newtype with validation, collision retry on insert (PRIMARY KEY constraint, 3 attempts), and Store::resolve_id_prefix. CLI now resolves exact ID → exact name → prefix for every session-arg subcommand. Renamed TAP prefix tap-sb- → tb- so all interface names fit IFNAMSIZ=15 without truncation (bridge sb-{12hex}=15, tap tb-{12hex}=15). 20 Rust files + conftest regex touched; 2 logical commits (08a5ef5 plan, 178b1a2 refactor). Verification: cargo build/clippy clean, 467 unit+integration tests green, full E2E 33/33 in 32:32 (faster than 34:51 baseline).
decisions: Prefix resolution is CLI-only: daemon API keeps exact-ID semantics. CLI resolves prefix→full ID before dispatching. Cleaner boundary, better UX for ambiguity.
SessionId as newtype (struct SessionId(String)) with validation (12 lowercase hex) — not a type alias. Catches accidental misuse at compile time across all call sites.

decisions: Addon composition semantics (rewritten _check_request): all host-matching rules contribute filters; request allowed iff any filter in any matching rule permits (method, path) pair. Deny reasons: 'host not in policy' vs 'no filter matched {method} {path}'

log.title: Deny-logger component and nftables DNAT restructure
log.summary: Deny-logger component + nftables two-table DNAT restructure. 33 commits on feat/m10-s3-deny-logger-dnat-restructure (defd541..0581dd2). Phase 1: TrafficEvent::DenyLogger domain+DTO. Phase 2: sandbox_dnat absorbs VM-egress conditional DNAT; concat sets duplicated across both tables (nft 1.0.6 rejects cross-table set refs); empty-policy flush leaves sandbox_dnat shape intact for fail-closed. Phase 3: sandbox-deny-logger Rust crate (2.86MB release) with TCP SO_ORIGINAL_DST + UDP IP_RECVORIGDSTADDR capture, JSONL emission, rate+conn caps, SIGTERM handling. Phase 4: Dockerfile builder stage + entrypoint supervision + bridge-IP healthcheck ($(hostname -i), NOT 127.0.0.1 - martian drop). Phase 5: parse_deny_logger_line + EventBus integration. Phase 6: gateway.rs component_probe + MONITORED_COMPONENTS adds DenyLogger. Phase 7: DockerHealth enum first-pass with healthcheck.sh fallback; fixes race where transient failures bypassed Docker retries=3 window. Phase 8: 4 integration tests (TCP deny, UDP deny, table inventory, healthcheck cycle). Phase 9: reviewer APPROVE 0 blockers; absorbed I2/I5/N3; deferred I1/I3/I4 as todos #30/31/32. Tests 658->699 base (+41), 703 with SANDBOX_TEST_INTEGRATION=1. All exit gates green: cargo nextest, clippy, fmt, make test-validators (3/3), make docs-build (all internal links valid). Key discoveries: (1) nft 1.0.6 cross-table set refs reject empirically - concat set duplication is mandatory, not a stylistic choice; (2) IP_ORIGDSTADDR does NOT expose pre-DNAT destination for conntrack-DNAT'd UDP (asymmetric vs TCP SO_ORIGINAL_DST) - blocks M10-S4 UDP discovery until conntrack netlink lookup lands (todo #29); (3) deny-logger must bind bridge IP not loopback - route_localnet deliberately not enabled so PREROUTING DNAT redirects to 127.0.0.1 get martian-dropped; (4) spec Part 3 Liveness posture corrected to reflect empirical $(hostname -i) probe. Carry-forward todos for M10-S4+: #29 (UDP pre-DNAT conntrack fix - blocks UDP discovery), #30 (Rust toolchain pin), #31 (ticker panic handling), #32 (monitor refactor).

Cargo 3x post-fix: 0/3 pass. All curl:7 TCP-RST — same original symptom, fix 4d91cf5 is INEFFECTIVE. Fix acts as a ~10s fixed wait via timeout path, BUT cargo still fails — so the race is deeper than filesystem-watch latency. Real race is likely in Envoy cluster DNS resolution (STRICT_DNS endpoints) or nftables enforcement settling. Out of M10-S6 scope.

log.title: User polish & refactor — integration-test mechanism + flaky tcp fix
log.summary: Polish & refactor sweep: integration-test mechanism (nextest profile + integration_* prefix replacing #[ignore]+env-gate), flaky tcp test fix, 14-todo deferred-todo sweep across 10 commit groups (#16,#17,#18,#19,#20,#21,#22,#31,#32,#34,#36,#38,#39,#40), and re-enabling 3 previously skipped E2E fixtures. Per-group dispatch with main-agent verification and CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 to avoid OOM on 8GB host. Final clean-state run: hermetic 951/951, integration 16/16, full E2E 46/46 in 45:44 (zero failures, zero errors, zero skips). All M11-deferred-fix skip decorators removed. Branch m10-s8-polish-sweep tip b6252b4, 10 commits committed (no PR/push per session policy).
decisions: Integration-test mechanism: replace #[ignore] + env-gate helper with nextest profile + integration_* name prefix. Single source of truth in sandboxd/.config/nextest.toml; default profile filters out integration_*, integration profile runs only them.
Drop SANDBOX_TEST_VALIDATORS + SANDBOX_TEST_INTEGRATION entirely. Profile is the sole gate; Makefile test-integration target just adds --profile integration.

Expand M10-S8 scope to include a deferred-todo sweep (#16, #17, #18, #19, #20, #21, #22, #31, #32, #36). Single session, processed sequentially. #36 requires a live VM run (~30+ min); user explicitly waived time concern.

#29 (UDP deny events post-DNAT destination) explicitly deferred out of M10-S8 sweep. User suspicion: UDP path may have broader issues than just the conntrack-netlink lookup; warrants its own dedicated session rather than a point fix here.

Expand M10-S8 scope to also include #34, #38, #39, #40 — the todos blocking currently-skipped E2E tests (test_clone_repo, test_cargo_preset_allows_cargo_fetch, test_github_repo_preset_scopes_to_one_repo, plus the multi-host propagation race that blocks M10-close). New exit criterion: all E2E tests pass and no #[skip]/pytest.mark.skip decorators remain from M11-deferred fixes.

Switched from single-subagent-for-14-todos to per-group dispatch. Each of the 10 commit groups gets its own fresh subagent; main agent verifies each group's commit + test gates and logs findings between dispatches. Reason: single-agent context too polluted across 14 todos; per-group dispatch keeps each subagent focused and gives main agent checkpoints to catch issues early.
Constrain cargo parallelism to CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 in subagent env to mitigate VM OOM (8-parallel link steps were peaking RAM). Per-group E2E gating retained per user direction.

Group 1 (#16): explicit-policy fatal failure committed as 0604be4. Helper fail_explicit_policy_apply takes minimal AppState fields (store/gateway/network/ingestors) instead of &AppState — same trick applied to teardown_session_networking_parts. Lets the hermetic unit test pin the 5xx + state=Error contract without standing up Lima/Docker. Pattern worth reusing for any future helper that the test pyramid wants to drive without full AppState.

Group 2 (#20+#21): listener path hygiene committed as cf54d8b. LISTENER_HOST_ROOT replaced with listener_host_root() resolver — 4-level fallback (SANDBOX_LISTENER_DIR override → XDG_RUNTIME_DIR → HOME/.local/share → /tmp safety net). Fourth level added beyond socket-path's 3-level pattern because listener path is mandatory at session start; HOME-unset CI environments must not panic. Both async distribute call sites wrapped in spawn_blocking; compiled is moved (not cloned) into the closure since neither caller uses it after.

Group 3 (#31+#32): deny-logger hardening committed as 62512fa. #31 picked option (a) — added &mut JoinHandle arm to deny-logger's tokio::select! (matches existing 'task exits → bail' pattern; one more arm reads as natural extension). &mut borrow trick preserves post-select abort + flush_now ordering. #32 helper lives at sandbox-core/src/events/health_transition.rs (peer of lifecycle.rs event builders) and returns a HealthTransition enum, not a pre-built Event — keeps helper session-agnostic, caller maps to lifecycle builder with its own session id.

Protocol change for remaining groups (4-10): drop per-group full make test-e2e gate. Only make test + make test-integration per group + targeted pytest where directly relevant (e.g. Group 6 → test_clone_repo). Final clean-state make test-e2e once after Group 10. Reason: API 529 overloads disrupted Group 4 twice; per-group 40min E2E compounds wall-clock cost when a sweep can take many hours. Full E2E at end still validates the whole branch. Discarded partial Group 4 WIP from failed respawn (M sandboxd/sandbox-core/src/policy.rs, 78 insertions of #18 test-tightening — reproducible by next agent).

Group 4 (#17+#18+#19): PolicyCompiler test hardening committed as b6112ec. #17 → integration_compile_nftables_passes_nft_c in validators.rs (kernel parser as authoritative arbiter, distinct from existing post-DNS-join nft_check). #18 → 5 unit tests tightened with assert_nft_line whole-line equality helper; tightening verified by injecting 'ct original' prefix and watching compile_level1_nftables_allows_dns fail. #19 → integration_apply_policy_through_real_gateway in gateway_integration.rs (full distribute() pipeline with subnet 10.209.7.0/24, asserts nft + Envoy LDS + CoreDNS all healthy).

Group 5 (#22) Option A chosen: assert the warm-restart witnesses the system actually exhibits (listener_added + listener_modified ticks; total_listeners_active = 1 post-rewrite; create_success increments meaningfully) instead of the original 'no drain, no recreate' assertion. Reasoning: #22 is a test-hardening item; Option A meaningfully strengthens over current gateway_status() == Healthy; Option C (filter_chains: populated-policy variant) couples test to compiler internals; B is a product change; D defers entirely. The runtime-vs-comment mismatch is filed as a follow-up todo for separate investigation.
discoveries: Flaky tcp::tests::tcp_respects_concurrency_cap root cause: server's over-cap path does SO_LINGER{0} + drop → kernel surfaces either ECONNREFUSED (backlog overflow) or ECONNRESET (in-flight handshake RST) depending on timing. Client retry arm only matched ECONNREFUSED. Fix: broaden match to accept both kinds as transient over-cap signals.

Latent bug: gateway_integration::test_gateway_nftables_injection_standalone was invoking docker in hermetic make test runs — had no #[ignore] attribute despite touching out-of-process state. Caught during integration_* rename sweep. Now gated by profile + prefix like the other gateway integration tests.

Test classification sweep caught three mislabeled tests: (a) validator_mitmproxy_schema was hermetic (serde_json roundtrip, no external bin) → relocated to sandbox-core::policy unit tests; (b) integration_create_with_npm_preset_ships_source_presets was in-process cargo test → renamed to drop prefix; (c) test_lima_create_and_delete did shell out to limactl create → renamed to integration_lima_create_and_delete. Rule going forward: integration_ prefix means out-of-process state (real container, CLI validator, real VM), nothing else.

E2E venv at tests/e2e/.venv was Python 3.13 on a host now running 3.12; Makefile's .installed marker doesn't track interpreter version so make test-e2e crashed with 'No module named pytest'. Subagent rebuilt out-of-band (rm -rf .venv + python3.12 -m venv + pip install). Will reoccur on any host where Python toolchain changes.

Group 5 found: integration_gateway_lds_listener_and_atomic_rewrite never actually exercises the in-place atomic-update path. Pre-rewrite the bootstrap deny-all listener is rejected by Envoy (filter_chains: [] invalid); the test's first 'rewrite' is a first-add (listener_create_success 0→8). Even a synthetic valid-→valid rewrite drains: listener_modified ticks, total_listeners_draining 0→1, listener_in_place_updated stays 0. Contradicts design comment at sandbox-core/src/policy.rs:1158 claiming filter-chain-only rewrites don't drain. Either the comment is wrong (likely — current emit uses default_filter_chain:, not named filter_chains:) or the compiler emits a non-in-place-eligible shape.

Group 6 (#34) DONE @ e2cf6d2. fail_explicit_repo_clone helper added (mirrors fail_explicit_policy_apply): all 4 warn-and-continue branches now mark session Error + teardown_networking_parts + return 5xx via SandboxError::Internal. Hermetic test pins contract. Cross-group discovery: targeted E2E test_clone_repo fails because clone fires <1s after policy_propagated=true but Envoy listener has not yet flipped to LISTENING — exactly the race #38 fixes. The new fatal-failure code is correct (returns 5xx with full git stderr); the test will go green only after Group 8 (#38) lands. Will use Group 8's targeted-E2E gate to verify test_clone_repo passes.

Group 7 (#39) DONE @ 874a9bb. Option B chosen: CIDR pool (140.82.112.0/20 + 192.30.252.0/22) baked into github-repo preset expansion as Destination::Cidr rules at AssuranceLevel::Http. The CIDR rule routes to mitmproxy via tunneling_config; the existing domain rule does the actual authz via Host header — preserves (host,port) uniqueness. CDN ranges deliberately excluded to keep signed-URL TLS passthrough intact for objects/release-assets. Targeted E2E gate (3 consecutive runs) deferred — blocked on Group 8 (#38) listener-ack race, same dependency Group 6 hit. Both Group 6 (test_clone_repo) and Group 7 (test_github_repo_preset_scopes_to_one_repo) E2Es will be verified after Group 8 lands. Group 7 agent stays alive at id=ae9896fddc93d1598 for resume after #38.

Group 8 (#38) DONE @ 3098b67 (verified: 944/944 hermetic + integration + clean cargo check). Implementation: new sandbox-core/src/lds_ack.rs (519 LoC) with LdsStatsProbe trait + DockerExecLdsProbe prod impl + wait_for_lds_ack(5s deadline, 100ms poll, ignore startup nonzero rejected counter). Wired into dns_propagation_loop on !stable_cache && write_ok. Cross-group impact: (a) test_clone_repo PASSES — Group 6 unblocked. (b) test_github_repo_preset_scopes_to_one_repo still FAILS with new symptom 'actual=-' (no policy_hash on listener) — Group 9 (#40) territory: listener never rewritten, distinct from ack-timing. (c) test_cargo_preset_allows_cargo_fetch still skip-marked — Group 9 owns un-skipping (per M10.md:299; agent's claim that Group 10 owns it was incorrect). Dispatching Group 9 next.

Group 9 (#40) Phase 1 HANDOFF: agent ab36ffa2b3a7869a0 confirmed hypothesis (d) NEW = DNS rotation race in DnsCache::update (cache REPLACES IPs on IpsChanged → gateway and VM see different rotation slots within same TTL → previously-allowed IP evicted from listener prefix_ranges → RST). Hypothesis (a) STRICT_DNS REJECTED (no STRICT_DNS clusters in Envoy config); (c) worker-thread atomicity REJECTED (filter chain for new IP wasn't installed at all). Three independent failure modes: 2.1 test_clone_repo = rotation race (well-defined fix: DnsCache UNION semantics within TTL window); 2.2 test_github_repo_preset = propagation never starts (actual=- whole 60s window — speculative: 6-host preset has unresolvable domain pinning all_domain_rules_resolved=false); 2.3 test_cargo_preset = VM-side getaddrinfo empty (likely /etc/resolv.conf or gateway upstream — separate bug). Test_clone_repo flake confirmed (Group 8 saw lucky pass; Group 9 saw RST). Dispatching fresh agent for Phase 2 with all three sub-tasks; allow multiple commits if needed.

Group 9 (#40) Phase 2 verification HANDOFF: agent's all-three-pass claim was wrong. test_clone_repo PASSES (DnsCache UNION fix works). test_cargo_preset_allows_cargo_fetch FAILS deterministically — curl to static.crates.io (Fastly pool 151.101.x.x) returns CURLE_SSL_CONNECT_ERROR (35) Connection reset by peer. index.crates.io on disjoint IP 146.75.118.137 succeeds at the same time. Asymmetry implicates a lower layer than Envoy listener — nftables set update race during back-to-back DNS batches (2.3s apart) or mitmproxy upstream race. Hermetic 949/949 + integration 16/16 pass. test_github_repo not yet attempted.

Group 9 (#40) Phase 3 DONE @ 9d1dca7. Real root cause: NOT a daemon race — Fastly publishes ≤2s TTL on index/static.crates.io, guest VM systemd-resolved cache expires within test settle window, next curl re-resolves to a different Fastly POP with a disjoint IP set, those IPs not in policy_allow_tcp nft set yet, deny-logger RSTs. Phase 2's daemon-side fixes (DnsCache UNION, filter_chain aggregation, Corefile→127.0.0.11) still real and necessary. Fix mirrors #39: CARGO_FASTLY_CIDR_POOL = [151.101.0.0/16, 146.75.0.0/17] emitted as http_rule_cidr in expand_cargo. crates.io NOT covered (AWS/CloudFront, supernets too broad). Gates: hermetic 951/951 (+2 new pool tests), integration 16/16, cargo 3×consecutive PASS, trio (clone+cargo+github_repo) PASS.

Cargo preset race INVESTIGATION (post-Phase 3): the 9d1dca7 CIDR pool fix is a workaround, not an architectural fix. The race is: CoreDNS plugin writes resolved.json AND answers the VM in WriteMsg interceptor (handler.go:133-156); VM opens TCP to new IP within ~1ms; sandboxd's dns_propagation_loop polls resolved.json every 2s and only then updates nft policy_allow_tcp set. Race window ~2000ms. DnsCache UNION (Phase 2) only preserves previously-seen IPs — doesn't help with first-time-seen rotation IPs. Even an event-driven fast-path (tail coredns.jsonl + signal loop) shrinks but doesn't close the race: docker-exec round-trip is ~20-25ms vs VM TCP setup at ~1ms. The architectural fix is either inline nft from the CoreDNS plugin (option C: cross-language coordination, race-free) or synchronous gating where CoreDNS holds DNS response until sandboxd acks (option D: adds DNS latency). Both are M11-scope changes — out of scope for M10-S8 polish. Recommendation: keep CIDR pool as targeted fix for known CDN supernets (Fastly, GitHub), file explicit M11 follow-up todo for the architectural fix.

log.title: Synchronous DNS-policy gating, workaround removal
log.summary: Synchronous DNS-policy gating delivered end-to-end. Four-commit branch m10-s10-sync-dns-gating: 84d39d2 spec (956 lines, Path D), 268704c implementation (Go plugin + Rust IPC + fail-open semantics), b381590 CIDR-pool removal (-395 LOC, 5 pinning tests deleted), 954be4b docs + closeout. Phase 4 gate 46/46 E2E in 45:52 with cargo Fastly + github-interactive cases passing without their CIDR-pool fallbacks. M10-S8's DNS-rotation workarounds replaced by the gate; todo #55 closed with code.
decisions: M10-S10 Phase 1 (spec) committed at 84d39d2 — synchronous DNS-policy gating chosen (Path D). Per-session UDS at events_host_root/<session-id>/dns-gate.sock bind-mounted into gateway. Length-prefixed JSON 'propagate_and_ack' wire format. Default deadline 1500ms with fail-open + dns_gate_timed_out lifecycle event. Reuses sandboxd helpers wait_for_lds_ack + generate_domain_ip_rules. Keeps dns_propagation_loop as steady-state reconciler.

Phase 2 implementation committed at 268704c. Plugin fail-open releases DNS answer regardless of ack outcome (per spec §6 fail-open). DaemonGateService runs full propagate_dns_changes (listener + nft) + wait_for_lds_ack with ack_deadline = plugin_deadline-150ms (min 100ms). Per-session UDS lives at events_host_root/<sid>/dns-gate.sock and surfaces inside gateway via existing per-session events bind-mount — no new mount machinery required. dns_caches: HashMap<SessionId, Arc<Mutex<DnsCache>>> in AppState gives gate-handler and steady-state dns_propagation_loop shared UNION-merge state.

Phase 3 (CIDR-pool removal) committed at b381590. Removed CARGO_FASTLY_CIDR_POOL + GITHUB_INTERACTIVE_CIDR_POOL constants, http_rule_cidr helper, and 5 pinning tests. Re-baselined shape tests against host-only output. Net -395 LOC in sandbox-cli/src/presets/builtin.rs. Phase 2's synchronous gate is now the sole mechanism preventing the cargo Fastly + github-interactive races.

Phase 5 closeout committed at 954be4b. Updated docs/concepts/networking.md (Fail-closed propagation → Synchronous DNS-policy gating) and docs/guides/troubleshooting.md (L3-first-request now describes dns_gate_timed_out fallback instead of routine race). M10.md closeout paragraph appended summarizing all 4 phases. progress.history.json refreshed. Grep sweep verified clean.
discoveries: Spec author surfaced 6 known gaps for downstream phases: (1) deadline_ms calibration vs measured nft+LDS p99 latency, (2) apply-side correlation when multiple gate requests in flight, (3) pooled vs per-request UDS connections, (4) event ordering between dns_gate_acked and existing propagation events, (5) gate-request signing/auth across IPC boundary, (6) ack cache invalidation when policy churns mid-flight.

Phase 2 verification: 964/964 hermetic + 21/21 integration green (incl. 2 new integration_dns_gate_* tests + 6 new Go gate tests). Bind-mount surface reuse means gateway entrypoint did not need new mount logic — UDS travels through the same per-session events host root that already gets mounted at /var/log/gateway/events/.
Phase 3 verification: 959/959 hermetic + 21/21 integration green after CIDR removal. Hermetic count dropped from 964→959 because 5 CIDR-pool pinning tests were correctly deleted (not regressed).

Phase 4 final E2E: 46/46 passed in 2752.92s (45:52). All M10-S8 workaround coverage now subsumed by the gate. Exit criteria 'ALL tests pass' satisfied.

log.title: Backend abstraction and Lima refactor
log.summary: M11-S1 — Backend abstraction and Lima refactor — landed in 4 phases (1A trait surface, 1B LimaRuntime/LimaTransport, 1C AppState rethread, 1D verification + doc polish). Introduced sandbox_core::backend module with SessionRuntime + GuestTransport traits, RuntimeHandle/RuntimeStatus/Capabilities/SessionSpec/RuntimeStartArgs types, V005 migration for the 'backend' column, and LimaRuntime+LimaTransport impls. AppState now holds Arc<HashMap<BackendKind, Arc<dyn SessionRuntime>>> for handler dispatch alongside Arc<LimaRuntime> for Lima-specific orchestration via .manager(). All 17 handler call sites in main.rs migrated; reconcile() takes &LimaRuntime; cleanup macro and trait dispatch coexist. Lima behavior preserved: 46/46 E2E (45m), 991/991 hermetic, 3/3 Lima integration, clippy/fmt clean, grep sweep clean, kio-reviewer APPROVE.
decisions: BackendKind lives on Capabilities (Capabilities.kind: BackendKind). Lets SessionSpec::validate construct UnsupportedFeature::WorkspaceMode(mode, caps.kind) without an extra parameter. RuntimeHandle is a String newtype with from_session_id and from_name constructors. ExitCode is a pub struct ExitCode(pub i32) newtype. RuntimeStatus mirrors VmStatus plus Creating/Error variants for daemon-level state.

SessionRuntime::create signature deviates from spec sketch: takes (&self, session_id: &SessionId, spec: &SessionSpec) — daemon assigns id before dispatch, mirroring LimaManager::create_vm and the deterministic-handle convention. Documented inline on the trait method. No other trait shape change in 1B.

AppState shape post-1C: runtimes: Arc<HashMap<BackendKind, Arc<dyn SessionRuntime>>> for trait dispatch; lima_runtime: Arc<LimaRuntime> for Lima-specific orchestration via .manager() escape hatch (clone_vm, install_guest_agent, list_vms, vm_status, base_image lifecycle). Helper fns: lima_dyn(&AppState) -> Arc<dyn SessionRuntime>; session_spec_from_config(&SessionConfig) -> SessionSpec. reconcile() takes &LimaRuntime; still Lima-specific (uses VmStatus walks via manager()). clone_vm and install_guest_agent stay Lima-only — provisioning shapes don't generalize cleanly to container backend (M11-S2).
discoveries: Phase 1 rethreading constraint: AppState already owns event_bus, vm_ip_map, ingestors, propagation_states, component_health_state. The refactor moves who *creates and destroys* per-session entries (ingestor spawn at main.rs:2950, event_bus.register_session at 3062, vm_ip_map.bind at 3065, unregister/unbind at 1558/1578) behind the SessionRuntime abstraction — the maps themselves stay on AppState. Hook points must survive the refactor verbatim or Lima E2E breaks.

GuestConnector (sandbox-core/src/guest.rs:202-278) currently takes Arc<LimaManager> to derive the VM name and run 'limactl shell <vm> -- socat - TCP:127.0.0.1:5123'. The S1 refactor splits this: GuestConnector becomes the backend-agnostic JSON-protocol consumer; the raw connect() byte stream becomes GuestTransport::connect() per backend. This is the trickiest seam because it touches the new trait and well-tested existing code.

SessionSpec is new (does not exist today); SessionConfig stays as the persisted blob shape (cpus, memory_mb, disk_gb, hardened, etc., still serialized at sessions.config column). SessionSpec is the request-time validation shape carrying BackendSpecific; mapping from SessionSpec → existing LimaManager call sites happens inside LimaRuntime::create. The persisted 'backend' column is added by V005 separately, alongside the unchanged sessions.config blob.

WorkspaceMode is data-bearing (Shared{host_path}, Clone{repo_url}); cannot derive enumset::EnumSetType. Phase 1A introduced companion WorkspaceModeKind unit-only enum + WorkspaceMode::kind() bridge. Capabilities::workspace_modes is EnumSet<WorkspaceModeKind>; UnsupportedFeature::WorkspaceMode carries (WorkspaceModeKind, BackendKind). Capabilities check kind discriminator, not full mode payload — the right semantic split.

Phase 1B Lima refactor pattern: LimaRuntime wraps Arc<LimaManager> as inner field with pub fn manager() escape hatch. Trait surface (create/start/stop/delete/status/ip/exec_interactive/guest_transport) covers VM lifecycle, but AppState still needs LimaManager-specific methods (clone_vm, check_base_image, build_base_image, install_guest_agent, generate_template) — invoke via runtime.manager(). Phase 1C decision: either grow trait surface to absorb these, or downcast Arc<dyn SessionRuntime> -> Arc<LimaRuntime> for Lima-specific paths. The escape hatch exists by design and should narrow over phases.

Lima integration tests share ~/.lima/ state and collide if run in parallel (limactl delete fails 'open .../sandbox-XXX/lima.yaml: no such file'). Resolved by adding a 'lima' test-group in sandboxd/.config/nextest.toml with max-threads=1 and override targeting test(/^integration_lima/). Future integration_lima_* tests inherit the serialisation; no per-test annotation needed.

Phase 1C deferred work catalogue (set by 1B subagent): (a) trait::start currently uses SessionConfig::default() — Phase 1C must widen signature with RuntimeStartArgs{docker_bridge, mac, config} OR call runtime.manager().start_vm(...) directly via escape hatch. (b) LimaRuntime::ip shells out via 'limactl shell <vm> -- ip -4 -o addr show dev eth1' — Phase 1C should swap for NetworkInfo.vm_ip lookup (already persisted; one less round-trip; works pre-boot). TODO comment left at LimaRuntime::ip impl. (c) LimaRuntime::create is 'create inert VM only' — no clone, no boot, no agent install; the full create→boot→agent flow remains in AppState until Phase 1C decides whether to absorb it onto the trait or keep it on LimaRuntime as Lima-specific inherent methods. (d) GuestConnector still consumes Arc<LimaManager>; Phase 1C may refactor to Arc<dyn GuestTransport>. (e) disk_gb defaulting falls through to SessionConfig::default().disk_gb=20 when SessionSpec::disk_gb is None — Phase 1C may prefer error or daemon-level default upstream.

Phase 1C confirmed: LimaSpec is NOT a separate type. Lima-specific knobs live on BackendSpecific::Lima { hardened, memory_mb, cpus } and SessionSpec.template (Option<String>). The custom Lima YAML template flow now lives in LimaRuntime::create (was inlined in handler before). RuntimeStatus is 5-variant (Running/Stopped/Creating/Error/Unknown); VmStatus is 3-variant. Handlers fold Creating/Error into existing 'leave alone / Unknown' branches for backward compat — Phase 1D may revisit when richer status DTO becomes useful (post-container).

M11-S1 exit criteria fully met. Full E2E suite passed 46/46 in 45:34 against the rethreaded AppState — Lima behavior preserved end-to-end through the Arc<dyn SessionRuntime> dispatch surface. Hermetic 991/991, Lima integration 3/3, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, grep sweep clean (no surviving state.lima refs; Arc<LimaManager> only in expected places: GuestConnector deferred to M11-S2, LimaRuntime internals, comments). kio-reviewer APPROVE with 0 critical and 3 doc-only Issues all fixed in this session.

log.title: Route helper, users.conf, daemon startup validation
log.summary: M11-S2 delivered the privileged route helper and users.conf-driven allocation pool. Phase 2A: shared loader sandbox-core/src/users_conf.rs (UsersConfig/SubnetEntry/Cidr4 types, find_subnet_by_*, allows_uid lookups; 22 unit tests). Phase 2B: new sandbox-route-helper crate (6th workspace member) implementing the spec's eight-step authorization flow (caller uid via getuid, gateway-ip subnet match, allow_users membership, pidfd_open+setns into container netns, getifaddrs subnet enforcement, ip route replace default via gateway, single deny exit code 1 with stderr reasons; three deny-branch integration tests with Docker fixture and CappedHelper RAII). Phase 2C: daemon startup loads users.conf, resolves the daemon's uid → subnet, threads CIDR through NetworkManager::new (replacing with_defaults); resolve_allocation_pool extracted as pure helper with 3 unit tests; explicit eprintln!+match shape in main() to surface SandboxError Display rather than Box<dyn Error> Debug; From<UsersConfigError> for SandboxError mapping with test pinning file-path preservation; three integration_users_conf_startup black-box tests (file missing/malformed/no-matching-subnet). Phase 2D: docs/start/installation.md updated with users.conf section, sandbox-route-helper setcap section (NOT setuid), kernel 5.8+ row, and a one-line callout at top of Run tests pointing at the configuration section (resolves kio-reviewer's docs-ordering blocker). Verification gates: cargo nextest --workspace 1017 passed, make test-integration 30 passed (incl. 6 new tests), make test-e2e 46/46 passed in 50 min, clippy clean, fmt clean, no flakes; kio-reviewer NEEDS CHANGES → APPROVED after the one-line callout. Operator artifact: /etc/sandboxd/users.conf created on the dev VM with {"subnets":[{"cidr":"10.209.0.0/24","allow_users":["olek"]}]} root-owned 0644.
decisions: sandbox-route-helper exit-code policy: single deny exit code 1 across all eight steps; stderr reason text is the load-bearing payload. Rationale: distinct codes per step would invite scripts to take ad-hoc dependencies on internal step numbering. Tests assert on stderr substrings, not exit codes.
discoveries: M11-S2 scoping: NetworkManager already accepts arbitrary base CIDR via new(base, prefix_len) — daemon today calls with_defaults() hardcoded to 10.209.0.0/24; users.conf integration just swaps the call site at sandboxd/src/main.rs ~line 4694. nix 0.29 is in-tree (sandbox-deny-logger dep); use it for pidfd_open/setns/getuid/getpwuid_r in the helper rather than rustix. users.conf loader belongs in sandbox-core, fixed path /etc/sandboxd/users.conf, env-var override SANDBOX_USERS_CONF for tests; pattern follows sandbox-cli/src/presets/user.rs but hard-fail instead of warn-skip.

Phase 2A loader landed: 22 unit tests, full workspace 1013 passing. Public surface: UsersConfig/SubnetEntry/Cidr4 types, find_subnet_by_gateway_ip + find_subnet_by_uid + allows_uid lookups, load_users_config{,_from} loaders. nix features split across crates: sandbox-deny-logger has [net,socket,uio]; sandbox-core now has [user] for User::from_{name,uid}. From<UsersConfigError> for SandboxError DEFERRED — Phase 2C must decide between SandboxError::InvalidArgument-with-formatted-path or a typed extension.

Rust 2024 made std::env::set_var and remove_var unsafe — tests that flip env vars need unsafe blocks with save/restore to avoid leaking into sibling tests. Pattern landed in users_conf.rs tests; reuse for any future env-var tests.

9p filesystem on the cargo target/ directory in this Lima VM does NOT back security.capability xattrs — sudo setcap returns Operation not supported against cargo-built binaries. Workaround: copy binary to /tmp (ext4, real xattr backing) before setcap. Pattern landed in sandbox-route-helper integration tests as CappedHelper RAII struct; reuse for any future setcap-needing test. Use /tmp literally, not std::env::temp_dir() — $TMPDIR could be redirected back to 9p.

nix 0.29 does NOT expose pidfd_open in any feature combination (verified by grepping the registry source). Use libc::syscall(libc::SYS_pidfd_open, pid, 0u32) directly and read errno via *libc::__errno_location(). Wrap in OwnedFd via FromRawFd for RAII close. Bumping nix to a future version that exposes pidfd_open is a small follow-up cleanup.

Box<dyn Error>'s blanket From<E> impl short-circuits the  operator's coercion through SandboxError when used at main()'s top level — operators see Debug repr (FileNotFound("...")) instead of Display message. Workaround: explicit match + eprintln!("sandboxd: {err}") + return Err(err.into()) shape for any UsersConfigError or InvalidArgument coming from startup-validation. Pattern landed in sandboxd/src/main.rs.

NetworkManager::restore_from_infos already errors cleanly on out-of-pool persisted-session allocations (case b per Phase 2C handoff): block_index_for returns None for any subnet outside the configured pool; restore_from_infos maps to SandboxError::Network. No additional code needed for the rollback-with-altered-users.conf path; daemon refuses to start. Error message names offending subnet but not configured pool CIDR — minor enrichment opportunity, not blocking.

M11-S2 verification gates all green on combined M11-S1+S2 working tree: cargo nextest --workspace 1017 passed, make test-integration 30 passed (incl. 6 new M11-S2 tests), full make test-e2e 46/46 passed in 50 min wall-clock, clippy clean, fmt clean, no flakes (incl. previously-flaky github-repo test). kio-reviewer NEEDS CHANGES → blocker fixed (docs ordering callout in installation.md). Working tree remains uncommitted — see todo #65 for disentanglement before merge.

M11-S3 reviewer review-fix triage pattern: when kio-reviewer NEEDS CHANGES findings are mechanical (helper extract + capability narrow + log demote), skip second-pass review. Architectural discovery worth carrying forward (already in current_log + delivery doc): gateway DNAT prerouting in sandbox-core/src/gateway.rs:1462-1486 rewrites every TCP/UDP packet from a session's vm_subnet to that same session's gateway-IP sinks (CoreDNS, Envoy, deny-logger). decisions: M11-S7 ping/cap-drop conflict resolved via path #2 (TCP probe), not path #1 (skip). Replaces ping <gateway_ip> with bash-builtin </dev/tcp/IP/53> reachability probe in test_m3_networking.py's three sites. Rationale: (a) preserves cross-backend reachability coverage that Bundle Y's network-info refactor was building toward, (b) aligns with directional pressure of S7 (DNS-skip→hard-fail, fewer skips not more), (c) modest scope — one helper + 3 call-site swaps. CoreDNS on port 53/TCP is always listening on the gateway so the probe is reliable. The cross-network negative-isolation check in test_concurrent_sessions becomes cleaner with TCP probe (clean fail) than with ping (hangs).
discoveries: Workspace bind target unified to /home/agent/workspace/ on container backend (M11-S7). Both backends now share the same in-session workspace path; capabilities matrix advertises {Shared, Clone} for both. Container Clone uses docker exec git clone reusing fail_explicit_repo_clone error envelope from Lima. The lite Dockerfile's tini/sandbox-guest entrypoint is what makes container side of state.guest.exec work — same TCP-over-SSH protocol as Lima.

Lima injects per-session MITM CA via guest agent into the system trust store (/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/sandbox-ca.crt + update-ca-certificates) — not via a bind mount. Container backend uses a read-only rootfs so it bind-mounts at /etc/ssl/certs/sandbox-ca.pem + env-var trust (CURL_CA_BUNDLE etc., per M11-S6 closeout). Asymmetry is structural: Lima can write trust dirs and rebuild the bundle; container cannot. SessionDto's mounts.ca_bundle_path is None for Lima as a result.

Lite container ping failures (3 of test_m3_networking.py [container] params) are NOT a missing-package gap — they are structural: spec § Hardening line 561-562 forbids ping under --cap-drop=ALL, iputils-ping on Ubuntu 24.04 needs cap_net_raw (inert under cap-drop=ALL), kernel ping_group_range fallback is 65534 65534 inside container, rootless Docker rejects --sysctl net.ipv4.ping_group_range at create time. ping in the e2e suite is a Lima-era L3-reachability proxy that does not survive the lite hardening posture.

Lite Dockerfile is shipped to the daemon via include_str! at sandbox-core/src/backend/container.rs:145, and the cached sandboxd-lite:0.1.0 image tag is keyed off CARGO_PKG_VERSION — bumping the Dockerfile alone does not bust the image cache. Forcing a rebuild requires: (a) cargo build --workspace AND (b) docker rmi sandboxd-lite:0.1.0.

Lite container backend's gateway nftables prerouting (sandbox-core/src/gateway.rs:1462-1486) DNATs every TCP/UDP packet from a session's vm_subnet to the SAME session's gateway IP — CoreDNS, Envoy, or deny-logger sink. The 'ip saddr {vm_subnet}' selector scopes per-session, but because rules match the session's OWN saddr, any outbound TCP/UDP from session A targeting session B's gateway IP gets answered by A's own gateway. Cross-session isolation is therefore invisible at L4 from inside the session — only ICMP (untouched by prerouting) lets a guest observe the actual L3 routing outcome. This is well-justified for production (every byte mediated) but limits what cross-session isolation tests can express via TCP. Container-backend cross-session isolation is best tested at the gateway nftables-integration level, not via e2e.

Rationale: S9's privilege boundary makes production helper ignore SANDBOX_USERS_CONF, but those tests rely on tempfile users.conf via that env var. Pointing the daemon at the test-cap'd helper (which honors the env var) keeps tests independent of /etc/sandboxd/users.conf content while preserving production helper's security boundary.

Privilege-boundary code pattern for capability-bearing helpers: dual entry points in sandbox-core/users_conf — load_users_config (daemon, env-var honored) vs load_users_config_route_helper (helper, env-var only honored when test-env-override Cargo feature is on). Production builds of cap-bearing binaries unconditionally read the canonical config and ignore SANDBOX_USERS_CONF. Codifies 'if a process holds an extra privilege, it must not be redirectable by user-controlled state.' Use this same shape for any future capability-bearing helper or daemon component.

Dev-env Makefile pattern (setup-dev-env): stamp-tracked sub-targets under sandboxd/target/.dev-env-stamps/. Each sub-target does cmp + getcap pre-checks before invoking sudo so a no-op rerun issues zero sudo calls. install-route-helper-test-cap must use --workspace --tests --features sandbox-route-helper/test-env-override to match the binary nextest builds (checksum check). Future host-setup work follows this pattern.
discoveries: make install-route-helper-test-cap had to switch from --release --target-dir route-helper-test to --workspace --tests --features sandbox-route-helper/test-env-override writing to target/debug/. Reason: integration test's checksum check requires the installed binary bit-identical with CARGO_BIN_EXE_sandbox-route-helper, which nextest builds in debug+workspace+tests scope. Any narrower cargo invocation produces a structurally different binary and the test panics 'installed route helper is stale' immediately after a fresh install. Prod (release) and test (debug) binaries don't clobber each other because they live in different profile dirs under the same target/.

Subnet defaults split: NetworkManager in-code default is 10.209.0.0/24 (256 addresses); contrib/users.conf.example dev-install template is 10.209.0.0/20 (4096 addresses). Both work because users.conf overrides the in-code default. Documented in concepts/networking.md and M3.md so future readers reconcile correctly.

Future host-setup must either run on default-hardened Docker or extend the e2e harness to flip --force-rootless-docker. kio-reviewer ran over the diff: 1 Major + 4 Minor + 2 Questions + 2 Nits. Major (in-pool integration test attached container to network being reaped) fixed inline by dropping --network from create_stopped_container helper, all calls now attach to bridge. Minor m-1 (saturating_add defensive intent) and m-4 (IPv6-only parser test) and Q-1 (transitive-ownership scope limitation docstring) fixed inline. Remaining 4 deferred as todos #91-#94: m-2 unique_session_id collision risk (parity with legacy), m-3 missing_ipam test name vs behavior, n-1 module-tag style consistency, n-2 Cidr4::parse #[doc(hidden)]. decisions: Orphan reaper dual-anchor design: two-pass reap_orphans (networks → containers/volumes) with out_of_pool_sids HashSet<SessionId> populated during network pass. Container and volume passes consult the skip set, achieving transitive ownership without coupling to docker-network-inspect calls. The CIDR anchor only protects siblings of out-of-pool networks observed during the network pass — a container/volume whose sandbox-net-{sid} has already been torn down falls through to single-anchor (name-prefix) protection. Acceptable given 12-hex sid randomness; revisit if multi-daemon deployment runbook lands. Documented in orphan_reaper.rs module docstring.
discoveries: Docker integration test convention: test fixtures should attach containers to bridge, NOT the test's custom sandbox-net-{sid} network. Some Docker engine versions (20.x+) register a created-state container as an active endpoint of its custom network, causing 'docker network rm' to fail with 'network has active endpoints'. The legacy integration_orphan_reaper.rs already followed this pattern; new integration_orphan_reaper_cidr.rs aligned via the create_stopped_container(name) helper. Apply this rule to any future Docker-backed integration test that exercises network teardown.

log.title: UDP audit + pre-DNAT deny-event fix
log.summary: Replaced IP_ORIGDSTADDR-only deny-logger UDP path with conntrack netlink lookup; UDP deny events now carry pre-DNAT 5-tuple. Hand-rolled netlink encoding via netlink-sys (published netlink-packet-netfilter v0.2.0 lacks conntrack). Phase 8 test 2 rewritten to assert pre-DNAT; new integration_udp_load_pre_dnat_attribution_holds_under_concurrent_flows exercises 12 concurrent flows. NLM_F_ACK pitfall locked in by comment + unit test (kernel ack-frame leaked into next pipelined recv). NLA_F_NET_BYTEORDER mask added per review (kernel-ABI hardening). Lookup miss → post-DNAT fallback + tracing::warn!. Init failure → hard-fail startup. Audit notes at docs/internal/m12-s1-udp-audit.md surface 3 S2-scope issues (dead allow-path, networking-design.md drifts) and 6 S9 candidates as deferred todos. Tests: 1206 hermetic + 66 integration all green; clippy/fmt clean. Commits: c3bc626 + 08c1d3e.
decisions: M12-S1 conntrack lookup uses hand-rolled netlink encoding via netlink-sys (not netlink-packet-netfilter): published v0.2.0 lacks conntrack support, only nflog. ~250 LOC stable kernel ABI emit/parse with full hermetic test coverage. Cargo.toml comment locks rationale + 'revisit when crates.io ships conntrack' marker.

On conntrack lookup miss (entry GC'd / race), deny-logger falls back to post-DNAT bind_addr + tracing::warn!, not drop. Losing deny attribution is strictly worse than emitting with less-accurate destination. CONNTRACK_LOOKUP_MISSES counter exposed via pub fn (not yet wired to /health). On netlink-socket init failure, deny-logger hard-fails startup so Docker HEALTHCHECK flips unhealthy + sandboxd restarts.

All review findings (1 MAJOR + 2 minors fold-inline) resolved before commit: NLA byte-order mask + comprehensive byte-order tolerance test, Phase 8 docstring rewritten, misleading miss-counter test claim corrected. Reviewer's m3-m6 deferred to M12-S9 as explicit todos.
discoveries: UDP allow-path is structurally dead, not just under-tested: nft DNATs policy_allow_udp to Envoy:10000, but gateway input chain rejects udp dport 10000 and Envoy has no UDP listener. M12-S2 'fully working UDP at transport' is bigger than planned — needs design decision (add Envoy UDP, reshape nft to skip Envoy for UDP, or remove dead path).

No conntrack/netlink crate in workspace today. M12-S1 implementation needs new dependency: rust-native (netlink-packet-netfilter / nfnetlink_conntrack-rs) vs C-linked (nfct via libnetfilter_conntrack). Decision pending implementation phase.

networking-design.md lives at repo root, not docs/internal/. Plan references and docs that point at docs/internal/networking-design.md are stale; future doc-reconciliation work should fix the path or move the file.

NLM_F_ACK on netfilter CT_GET corrupts pipelined lookups: kernel sends successful entry reply followed by separate NLMSG_ERROR(errno=0) ack frame which next lookup's recv() consumes. Fix: drop NLM_F_ACK; on miss kernel sends NLMSG_ERROR(-ENOENT) regardless. Single-flow tests miss this; load tests catch it. Locked in via comment + unit-test assertion.

log.title: Fully working UDP at transport level
log.summary: M12-S2 'Fully working UDP at transport level' complete. Restructured the UDP datapath end-to-end: (a) extracted sandbox-event-emitter shared lib crate; (b) renamed sandbox-deny-logger -> sandbox-nft-deny-logger, replaced conntrack-driven UDP attribution with kernel NFLOG (group 1) + drop, deleted src/conntrack.rs entirely; (c) added new sandbox-nft-allow-logger driven by NFCT NFNLGRP_CONNTRACK_NEW subscription, writing nft-allow.jsonl; (d) extended daemon ingest with strict layer/event pairing parser, DenyLoggerAllow envelope variant, allow_body_dto mapper, EventName::Allow filter; (e) gateway container ships dual binaries with launch-both-then-probe-both pattern (:10003 deny + :10004 allow health), dual-PID process monitor; (f) JSONL filenames flipped to spec-mandated nft-deny.jsonl + nft-allow.jsonl; (g) UDP allow-path skips Envoy entirely (TCP-only proxy); (h) reconciled 5 user-facing docs (networking.md, networking-design.md, network-policies.md, policy-model.md, troubleshooting.md) to silent-drop + five-process model. Test parity: 4 new e2e UDP allow-path tests in test_m4_policy.py (NTP allow, bidirectional echo NEW-only, multi-port-same-host, CIDR-edge), test_m3_networking.py UDP-skip removed and replaced with real deny-event assertion, synthetic-JSONL integration_nft_allow_logger_ingest.rs (2 tests). Verification: 1221 hermetic tests pass, integration profile clean, clippy clean, fmt clean, e2e Lima-backend 5/5 pass. Review verdict APPROVE with 0 blockers / 0 majors / 3 minor citation nits (folded in). Landed as 4 commits c1f069f..0336342 on master (not pushed; awaiting user authorization).
decisions: M12-S2 spec open questions resolved: (1) NFLOG group=1; (2) silent drop, no ICMP unreachable (reconcile networking-design.md:1221 to silent drop); (3) per-source rate cap deferred to S9; (4) delete src/conntrack.rs entirely after UDP-deny moves to NFLOG (TCP-deny uses SO_ORIGINAL_DST, no remaining caller); (5) /health field names preserved through rename, new fields added for allow-logger; (6) JSONL filenames nft-deny.jsonl + nft-allow.jsonl; (7) allow events fire on NFCT_T_NEW only, flow-end deferred.

EventEmitter::open signature changed: now takes layer: &str so each binary can set its own layer tag (deny-logger vs allow-logger). Line enum's layer field is now &'a str (borrow from emitter's owned String) instead of &'static str. JSONL on-disk shape preserved byte-for-byte because callers pass the original literal.

AllowRecord field set identical to DenyRecord (orig_dst_ip, orig_dst_port, protocol, src_ip, src_port). Same envelope, distinguished by event discriminator only ('allow' vs 'deny'). flow_id deferred (Resolution 7 NEW-only — no second event to correlate); forward-compat via Option<T> + #[serde(default)] when needed.

JSONL 'layer' value pinned at 'deny-logger' across the rename — daemon-side ingest parser keys on this string literal. Crate name and binary name both flipped to sandbox-nft-deny-logger but the wire-shape layer tag stays. Allow-logger will use a distinct layer value (TBD in Phase 3, likely 'allow-logger').

Daemon-side ingest layer-tag asymmetry: on-bus DTO layer always 'deny-logger' (single nft-logger family per Decision 5); discriminator is event tag (deny/allow/rate_limited). On-disk JSONL retains producer-specific layer tags ('deny-logger' vs 'allow-logger'); parser enforces layer/event pairing. nft_logger.rs (renamed from deny_logger.rs) handles both producers with parse_5tuple helper.

Allow-logger /health on port :10004 with nfct_socket and allow_events_emitted_60s fields. health::run is now polymorphic with body_builder (deny_logger_body / allow_logger_body); each binary plugs in its own shape. netlink-sys reused for NFCT subscription — netlink-packet-netfilter v0.2.0 doesn't cover conntrack subsystem.

Phase 4 launch pattern: launch-both-then-probe-both. Gateway entrypoint launches sandbox-nft-deny-logger + sandbox-nft-allow-logger in parallel after mitmproxy/Envoy/CoreDNS, then sequential readiness probes (:10003 deny -> :10004 allow). Process-monitor iterates DENY_LOGGER_PID + ALLOW_LOGGER_PID; either exiting takes container down per Decision 4.

Phase 6 doc reconciliation completed across five files (179+/25-): networking.md (five processes, TCP/UDP-split datapath), networking-design.md (UDP subsection rewritten + ICMP-unreachable mandate reconciled to silent drop), network-policies.md (UDP destinations section with NTP/UDP-123 example), policy-model.md (UDP-specific caveats H4 block), troubleshooting.md (UDP traffic section, 4 sub-entries).

Phase 5 e2e test pattern: bash /dev/udp/ for one-shot UDP sends (universal), socat for bidirectional (read-back required). All assertions hit the on-bus DTO (layer='deny-logger' on bus, event tag discriminates allow/deny) — agnostic to on-disk JSONL filename. RFC-5737 TEST-NET-3 (203.0.113.1) used for negative-tuple deny assertions to avoid collision with idle VM traffic. NTP (time.cloudflare.com:123) chosen as bidirectional probe — universally reachable, real protocol response to validate.

M12-S2 commit split landed as 4 commits instead of suggested 6: c1f069f feat(nft-loggers)! collapses lib-extract + deny rework + allow-logger + daemon ingest because file-level interleaving (events/ingest/{nft_logger,watcher,envelope,mod}.rs all carry both deny and allow content). Restructure authorized by spec/plan; resulting commits all compile mid-sequence. Followed by f301c36 gateway, 514fb3e e2e tests, 0336342 docs.
discoveries: NFLOG bind is a three-step handshake on NETLINK_NETFILTER: (1) PF_BIND cmd=3 [NOT 1, that's CMD_BIND], (2) per-group CMD_BIND cmd=1 [WITHOUT this kernel never routes packets to socket], (3) CFG_MODE COPY_PACKET. Locked in nft-deny-logger nflog.rs.

NFLOG recv buffer can pack multiple NFULNL_MSG_PACKET frames in one recvmsg(); parser must drain all of them (parse_all loop), not return after first. Single-msg parse loses all but the first event in a burst — caught only by load-style integration test.

Allow-logger uses synthetic-JSONL integration test approach (no gateway image dep): tests/sandboxd/integration_nft_allow_logger_ingest.rs writes nft-allow.jsonl + asserts ingest dispatch. Mirrors existing events_ingest_integration.rs pattern. Real-binary live e2e covered in Phase 4+5.

Phase 6 docs already written for spec-mandated name.

SIGTERM doesn't promptly kill nft-loggers because spawn_blocking netlink-recv threads aren't woken by tokio cancel. Pre-existing behavior (matches the deny-logger before split). Entrypoint's 10s SIGKILL escalation handles cleanup. Cosmetic; flagged as latent S9 cleanup.

JSONL rename completed across 7 files (5 tracked + 2 untracked from earlier in session). Watcher.rs gained a strengthened negative test asserting legacy 'deny-logger.jsonl' is no longer in KNOWN_FILES — turns the rename into a tested invariant. 2 files (sandbox-nft-deny-logger/src/main.rs and integration_nft_allow_logger_ingest.rs) are untracked-but-modified — Phase 7 commit split must keep these atomic with the tracked rename so it doesn't get split across commits.

Phase 5 first run failed 3/5 m10_s3_end_to_end tests with stale image (old sandbox-deny-logger expecting DNAT-to-:10002 datapath); make gateway-image then re-run flipped to 5/5 green. Worth either: hardening Makefile dep chain (gateway-image stamp triggers integration profile rebuild), or callout in CONTRIBUTING.

Forward-chain invariant changed in M12-S2: pre-S2 'every saddr-accept also has daddr' assumption no longer holds because gateway.rs admits VM-subnet UDP wholesale at FORWARD (PREROUTING NFLOG+drop already filtered denied UDP). test_denied_traffic relaxed to skip the wholesale UDP-accept rule when checking the daddr invariant for TCP-class lines. Live nft list ruleset prints L4 protocol numerically: UDP=17, TCP=6 — e2e regex assertions need numeric form.

Wire-protocol code (NFLOG + NFCT) well-disciplined: NLA flag-bit masking, multi-message recv drain, group=0 rejection at bind, NEW-only NFCT subscription. log.title: Native cp via limactl cp / docker cp
log.summary: Refactored sandbox cp from in-tree base64-chunk byte pump to native dispatch: plan_cp_command(backend, session, direction, host, remote) returning (limactl cp -r ...) or (docker cp ...). Established the dispatch surface M12-S8 will extend with plan_sync_command. Side benefits: directory copy now works (was broken), attributes preserved (mode/sparse), error messages reach operator verbatim, container cp works against stopped sessions. Dropped base64 dep from sandbox-cli. 6 unit + 7 integration tests pin invocations on both backends; full hermetic suite 1237/1237 + clippy clean. Filed two deferred follow-ups: #126 (deprecate dead daemon /upload /download endpoints) and #127 (E2E test_cp_native_attributes for sparse + mode round-trip). Committed as f3fc855.
decisions: M12-S7 cp dispatch shape: parallel free-functions (plan_ssh_command + plan_cp_command), not a trait. Rationale: matches existing backend-keyed dispatch idiom in the CLI; trait object adds no polymorphism we use. M12-S8 sync lands a sibling plan_sync_command on the same surface.
discoveries: Pre-refactor sandbox cp had broken directory-upload (std::fs::read fails on dirs, despite docs/guides/workspaces.md claiming dirs were 'transferred as chunked base64'). Native dispatch fixes this transparently — limactl cp -r and docker cp recurse by default.

limactl cp -r is harmless on plain files (scp ignores -r for non-directories); docker cp recurses by default and rejects unknown flags. Hence asymmetric flag set in plan_cp_command: limactl gets unconditional -r, docker gets none.

decisions: M12-S8: ship 'sandbox sync' as a separate command (not 'sandbox cp --rsync'). Rationale: cp and sync carry distinct semantics (one-shot retransfer vs incremental mirror with --delete); folding both into cp puts two mental models behind one verb. Each command's contract is now obvious from its name.

M12-S8: rsync remote-shell uses 'limactl shell' on Lima and 'docker exec -i' on container — both as the -e arg to rsync. Rejected 'ssh -F ~/.lima/<vm>/ssh.config' because it's an internal Lima artefact. Rejected '-it' for docker exec because TTY corrupts rsync's binary wire protocol.

M12-S8: rsync required (not optional). Provisioned in both base images (Lima cloud-init apt-get baseline + lite Dockerfile). No runtime pre-flight probe — native error from rsync when missing is clearer than a Rust-emitted check. Establishes new contract for session images going forward.
discoveries: bash builtin echo silently consumes -e as 'interpret escapes' flag, corrupting argv recorders. The cp shim happened to never see -e; the sync shim cannot. Use 'printf %s\n' in shim recorders.

Lima base-image content hash automatically picks up generate_base_template() changes — adding a package to the apt baseline transparently triggers a rebuild on next sandbox create via existing staleness-detection. No extra plumbing needed.

After Docker reinstall to rootful (29.4.0, containerd snapshotter), integration_route_helper_denies_when_netns_ip_outside_caller_subnet fails with 'setns failed: EPERM' on Docker container netns. cap'd helper (cap_sys_admin+ep on /usr/local/libexec/sandboxd-test/sandbox-route-helper) cannot setns into root-owned container PIDs even though container userns == host init userns. setns to own pid works; setns to PID 1 (root-owned) also fails. Likely Ubuntu 24.04 unprivileged_userns AppArmor profile or Linux 6.8 hardening wrt cross-uid setns. Pre-existing environmental issue, NOT a code regression: last green test-integration on 6c8b6b6 was under rootless Docker. Other 84/85 integration tests pass (cp/sync dispatch all green after this session's planner fix).

Group C E2E failures were both real upstream issues, not gateway/code regressions. (1) Canonical removed time.ubuntu.com from authoritative DNS — apex returns SOA-only for this name across ns1.canonical.com/8.8.8.8/1.1.1.1; only ntp.ubuntu.com resolves. (2) cloudflare.com publishes HTTPS (TYPE65) at apex, not SVCB (TYPE64); test_svcb_record_without_ech_reaches_vm asked TYPE64, upstream returned NOERROR-zero-answers correctly. Both fixed in 9f07740: drop time.ubuntu.com from UBUNTU_NTP_HOSTS preset (was a 2-host list, now 1-host) and update SVCB test to query TYPE65. SVCB/HTTPS share wire format and stripECHFromRR handles both arms identically, so HTTPS exercises the same code path.

Container backend (--lite) is broken under rootful Docker 29.4.0 — sandbox create fails with 'sandbox-route-helper denied (exit 1): RTNETLINK answers: Operation not permitted' / 'ip route replace failed: exit 2'. Root cause: under rootless Docker the container's netns lives in a child user namespace, so cap_sys_admin in the parent userns implicitly grants cap_net_admin in the child (Linux userns rule); under rootful Docker the netns sits in the init userns directly, so the helper's spawned ip(8) process has no caps and cannot RTM_NEWROUTE. Adding cap_net_admin to the helper file caps doesn't fix it — file caps are dropped at exec, the spawned ip(8) needs ambient caps (PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE) or the helper should issue the netlink op directly. NEW regression from the rootful Docker switch, not from S11 cleanup work. Out of S11 scope; needs follow-up to make container backend rootful-Docker compatible. Container-backend E2E entirely blocked on this; Lima-backend E2E unaffected.

Rootless Docker masked the route-helper bug via userns cap promotion: CAP_SYS_ADMIN in parent userns implicitly grants all caps in child userns when operating on objects in child userns, so a cap-less ip(8) child still succeeded at RTM_NEWROUTE. Rootful Docker has no such promotion.

PR_CAP_AMBIENT_RAISE under setcap requires the helper to first raise CAP_NET_ADMIN from its Permitted to its Inheritable set. File caps =eip put the cap in the FILE's inheritable set, but on exec a thread's Inheritable is taken from the parent's Inheritable (the unprivileged caller's, which is empty). The helper must call caps::raise(Inheritable, NET_ADMIN) before caps::raise(Ambient, NET_ADMIN).

Docker cp can't write to a --read-only container's tmpfs (/tmp) and can't read from it either; it only sees the rootfs overlay. /home/agent (mounted as a Docker volume) is visible to docker cp because volumes are not part of the rootfs. Test paths under /home/agent/ work on both backends; /tmp/ paths only work on Lima.

Route-helper test setns(pidfd, CLONE_NEWNET) under rootful Docker is gated by ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_REALCREDS), which checks BOTH real uid AND real gid of the target task. Production passes --user 1000:1000; the test fixture passed only --user 1000, leaving gid at busybox image default (root/0), so gid mismatch denied setns. Fixed by passing uid:gid in test fixture.

Daemon does not rm -rf the partial dir on clone failure. Manifests as cascading failure of every Lima E2E test downstream of the first failure. Manual fix: rm -rf the broken Lima dir. Lima base image build silently accepts a failed docker install: cc_scripts_per_boot allows Lima provision.system scripts to exit non-zero without aborting cloud-init, so the daemon's 'golden base image build complete' message fires even when docker-ce apt install failed mid-run. Each cloned session VM then re-runs provision.system on its own first boot, hits the same network flakiness, and fails again — this is the upstream cause of the Lima E2E cascade. Committed as 092693d.
discoveries: Lima SLIRP networking surfaces apt EAGAIN ('Could not wait for server fd - select (11: Resource temporarily unavailable)') under concurrent fetches. Acquire::Queue-Mode 'access' alone is insufficient — Pipeline-Depth=0 (forces serial requests within each connection) is the load-bearing fix. With it, base-image apt-baseline succeeds first try in ~85s.

limactl clone is non-atomic: writes disk + cidata.iso BEFORE lima.yaml. Mid-clone interruption leaves a dir with no lima.yaml, which then poisons every subsequent limactl invocation host-wide ('open lima.yaml: no such file or directory'). Cleanup must try 'limactl delete --force' first then fall back to direct 'rm -rf $LIMA_HOME/<vm>' since limactl refuses to operate on the corrupted instance.

Cloud-init's cc_scripts_per_boot does NOT abort the boot when a per-boot script exits non-zero — it logs a warning and proceeds. So 'limactl start' returning success is necessary but NOT sufficient for declaring a base image golden. Must probe in-VM tools post-start (command -v socat git rsync docker) before stamping. Without the probe, downstream cloned VMs re-run the same flaky provisioning at session-create time.

decisions: SANDBOX_BASE_VM_NAME is set on the e2e harness's own os.environ at conftest module-import time (via os.environ.setdefault), not just on the spawned daemon's env. This lets test_golden_image.py read it as a module-level constant before any session-scoped fixture runs, and keeps Popen(env=...) calls simple — children inherit the parent env. Future env-var-driven test config should follow the same pattern.
discoveries: S13's CIDR + base-VM-name isolation does NOT isolate ~/.lima/ itself: neither e2e conftest nor Rust integration tests set LIMA_HOME, so test and production daemons share the global ~/.lima/ directory. Test cleanup operates by name pattern (sandbox-*) over the shared store. Full ~/.lima/ isolation would require per-test LIMA_HOME=<tempdir> on the spawned daemon and integration tests — out of scope for S13.

S13 sub-section (F) — Lima base/session templates clamp eth0 (SLIRP NIC) MTU to 1280 via netplan dropin in a new step=net-tune provision block. Root-caused to libslirp not propagating host-learned PMTU into guest TCP state; surfaced because (A)'s base-VM rename forced a fresh apt-update during base-image build instead of reusing operator's pre-built image. Universal-safe IPv6 floor (RFC 8200 §5); same choice as Cloudflare WARP/Tailscale. Session runtime egress on eth1/gateway-bridge keeps default 1500 — agent workloads unaffected. Commit 83b6cb1.

nextest filter 'not test(/^integration_/)' in sandboxd/.config/nextest.toml only anchors against bare test names — it filters integration tests in tests/ directories but does NOT filter unit tests inside src/ whose qualified name has a module prefix (e.g. 'tcp::tests::integration_foo'). The CLAUDE.md convention works for unit tests too only after the regex is loosened to '(^|::)integration_'. Surfaced when renaming sandbox-nft-deny-logger src/-mod tcp tests; not previously visible because every prior integration_* test lived in tests/.

tests/e2e/conftest.py sandbox_daemon readiness probe was racing the daemon bind/listen window: socket file appears at bind, connect returns ECONNREFUSED until listen. The old socket_path.exists() check returned prematurely, causing intermittent ECONNREFUSED on the first CLI call under load. Fixed in commit b8a123c by replacing the existence poll with an actual AF_UNIX connect probe (FileNotFoundError plus ConnectionRefusedError = keep polling, success = ready, anything else propagates).

Base-image stop step 5 (build_base_image_inner): single graceful limactl stop with 120s budget timed out under e2e suite I/O contention (in-guest systemd shutdown + qcow2 fsync of dirty pagecache exceeds budget). Replaced with graceful-then-force fallback (60s graceful + 60s force, total ceiling unchanged at 120s). Warn! on fallback preserves diagnostic signal — operators correlate recurring fallbacks with host load vs. genuine guest-side regressions. Force-stop is safe for the base image because it is a build artifact (qcow2 flushes via QEMU SIGTERM exit handler; metadata file write at step 6 is what finalizes the build). Commit a02ac9e.

E2E test failures now auto-dump the last 100 lines of sandboxd stderr/stdout to pytest's failure section via pytest_runtest_makereport + autouse fixture in tests/e2e/conftest.py. Removes the manual /tmp/pytest-of-*/sandboxd0/sandboxd.{stderr,stdout}.log step that was previously the first diagnostic move on every flake.

Three e2e test files deliberately SIGKILL the session-scoped sandboxd and Popen a fresh one on the same --socket and --base-dir, reopening the existing stderr/stdout log paths in append mode: test_networking.py:test_daemon_restart_recovery (and its fallback at test_networking.py:1058), test_lite.py (~:755), and test_policy_persistence.py (~:241). The respawned Popen handle is swapped back into sandbox_daemon["process"] (conftest.py:545-552, 574-584). This means a single pytest session can have multiple sandboxd 'sandboxd starting' lines in the same log file — entirely expected, not a crash signal. Future log-tailing diagnostics must take this into account.

The bind→listen race in sandboxd's startup window also affected SIX inline daemon-respawn paths in three e2e tests — the b8a123c fix landed only in the session-scoped fixture, missing test_lite.py:768/878, test_networking.py:981/1069, and test_policy_persistence.py:254/351, all of which polled os.path.exists() instead of attempting a connect(). When any of those tests hit their respawn path, the next test in the suite raced ECONNREFUSED into the bind→listen window. Fixed in 10909e4 by extracting wait_for_daemon_ready(socket_path, proc, timeout) into tests/e2e/conftest.py and routing all seven call sites (the fixture + the six inline ones) through it. Future inline-daemon-respawn code MUST use this helper, not os.path.exists.

End-to-end suite (make test-e2e) now runs to completion under the cumulative S13 fix set (commits up to 10909e4) — confirms the bind→listen race and libslirp PMTU blackhole were the dominant flake sources. Operator-confirmed validation.

RuntimeStartArgs::for_user is populated at ALL four runtime.start() call sites (D1 container, L1/L2 Lima fast/slow paths, D2 backend-dispatched), even though Lima accepts-and-ignores. Uniform population is a defensive invariant: it avoids a regression if a third backend lands or if a runtime.start() site moves across branches. The Container backend errors with SandboxError::Internal if for_user is None AND a route_helper_path is configured — the spec § 6.3 'programming error' contract.
discoveries: axum 0.8 per-connection state pattern: implement custom Listener with Addr = PerConnExt type, use into_make_service_with_connect_info::<Listener::Addr>(), then a from_fn middleware reads ConnectInfo<...> and inserts Extension<...> for handlers. Connected<IncomingStream<'_, L>> trait impl glues the listener's Addr into axum's per-conn plumbing.

log.title: V006 migration, SessionStore per-caller filtering, handler wiring
log.summary: V006 migration (DELETE FROM sessions + 3 NOT NULL columns) lands with a three-pass SessionStore::new restructure to keep V004's orphan-sweep firing before V006's FK cascade. Every SessionStore read/mutation method now requires caller_username and folds 'AND owner_username = ?N' into its WHERE; foreign sessions are 404-indistinguishable from nonexistent (Ok(None)/Err(SessionNotFound)). update_state_forced → update_state_reconcile rename; static-analysis test (update_state_reconcile_allow_list.rs) pins authorized callers exactly + rejects any caller carrying Extension<OperatorIdentity>. Internal-only callers (gateway monitor, orphan reaper, explicit-fail handlers) use *_unfiltered helpers. SessionDto gains owner_username (additive, serde-default). All 12 HTTP handlers + 2 module handlers (events_http, policy_http) extract Extension<OperatorIdentity> and thread operator.name. create_session stamps owner_username; guest_protocol_version=0, guest_binary_version="" placeholders pending M13-S5. Tests: 4 V006 migration tests, 9 SessionStore filter tests, allow-list static-analysis test, foreign-session-404 integration test. 1280/1280 default + 104/104 integration green; clippy + fmt clean. Committed bfad1ad.
decisions: M13-S4 spec 2 structural core complete: V006 migration + orphan scan; per-caller filter on every SessionStore method (5-arg create_session, caller_username on get/list/update_state/delete/policy methods); update_state_reconcile rename with allow-list static-analysis test; 404-on-foreign-id via Ok(None) at storage boundary; SessionDto.owner_username field; events_http/policy_http thread Extension<OperatorIdentity>; 1280 tests pass, clippy + fmt clean.

Internal-only SessionStore callers (gateway monitor, orphan reaper, explicit-fail handlers) bypass per-caller filtering via *_unfiltered helper methods (list_sessions_unfiltered, get_network_info_unfiltered, etc.). These are pub but rustdoc-marked internal-only. The update_state_reconcile_allow_list.rs static-analysis test pins the exact <path>:<fn> set of authorized callers; a secondary check rejects any caller whose signature includes Extension<OperatorIdentity> (HTTP handlers must never use the reconciler escape hatch).
discoveries: V006 migration ordering: 'DELETE FROM sessions' cascades through session_policies via FK, which would drop orphan rows BEFORE V004's orphan-sweep can fire. The fix was a three-pass restructure of SessionStore::new: pass 1 (V001-V003) snapshots pre-V004 rule counts; pass 2 (V004-V005) sweeps orphans BEFORE V006 cascade-deletes them; pass 3 (V006+) applies the rest. Any future migration that adds destructive DELETEs must consider FK-cascade interactions with prior migrations' sweep passes.

Per-caller filter wire shape: SessionDto.owner_username is additive with #[serde(default)] to keep older clients deserializing responses without the field. Foreign-session probes return 404 indistinguishable from nonexistent (read methods Ok(None), mutations Err(SessionNotFound)) — never 403, so attackers cannot enumerate session IDs by probing.

Predicates is_protocol_compatible + can_refresh_in_place per spec § 3.3/3.7. GuestRequest::Version + GuestResponse::VersionResult wire variants; guest-side handler. SessionRuntime::refresh_guest_binary trait method; Container impl (docker stop -t 5 → stage binary → docker cp → drop tempfile), Lima impl (limactl start → copy → sudo mv → sudo chmod → systemctl restart → limactl stop), wrapped in spawn_blocking. GuestProtocolIncompatible → HTTP 409 with load-bearing tokens 'refresh is not viable' and 'recreate the session'. SessionStore::update_guest_versions with per-caller filter. start_session compat gate per § 3.4 decision tree (fast/refresh+stamp/refuse). 5 integration tests (§§ 7.4-7.5) + 6-row predicate unit table (§ 7.3). 1290/1290 default + 109/109 integration green; clippy + fmt clean. Committed 38ce8c1. Two flagged gaps: spec § 3.8.1 docker cp incompatible with --read-only rootfs (todo #141, recommended path b: bind-mount on create); stage_embedded_guest_binary reads disk vs spec § 3.6 include_bytes! (todo #142, M15 transition).
discoveries: Spec 2 § 3.8.1's docker cp refresh mechanism is empirically broken on modern Docker (29.4+ with containerd snapshotter): 'docker cp' into a --read-only container rootfs is REJECTED by dockerd with 'container rootfs is marked read-only', regardless of destination path. The lite image (images/lite/Dockerfile) ships /usr/local/bin/sandbox-guest baked into a read-only rootfs — production refresh would fail. M13-S5 integration tests pass via a workaround Dockerfile declaring VOLUME [/usr/local/bin]. Three resolution paths exist: (a) add VOLUME directive to production lite Dockerfile (accept volume-orphan lifecycle); (b) bind-mount host-side sandbox-guest into the container at create time + refresh becomes host-side file replace + recreate (cleanest, agent recommended); (c) docker commit per session (heavy). Requires spec amendment to § 3.8.1.

M13-S5 stage_embedded_guest_binary reads sandbox-guest from disk via lima::guest_agent_path() (sibling-of-daemon lookup), not via Spec 2 § 3.6's prescribed include_bytes! embedding. Works in dev where daemon and guest co-build in target/debug/; production binary distribution (Spec 4 / M15 release-and-install) requires the switch to compile-time include_bytes! plus a build.rs that builds sandbox-guest first. The const SANDBOX_GUEST_VERSION is already wired via build.rs reading sandbox-guest/Cargo.toml — that's the half that landed.
