Reference test test_update_fresh_install_to_next_version (using real bumped binary since 4b521f7) also fails at HEAD with the same error — confirming this is a production bug, not migration-caused. test_update_rollback.py had an unsound assertion: pre_sessions_sha snapshotted AFTER daemon start, compared to post_rollback sha — but SQLite WAL legitimately mutates the .db file between daemon-start and daemon-stop-for-backup via checkpointing. Correct invariant is post_rollback_sha == manifest_recorded_sha (the backup's captured sha). Fix in flight via subagent (Option A). Real production correctness question — 'is sandbox update's backup logically consistent w.r.t. concurrent daemon writes' — is M16-S4 review territory; daemon should be stopped or WAL-checkpointed before backup; investigate in S4.

Rollback test invariant fix landed at 0292713 (compares post-rollback sha against manifest_recorded_sha, the backup's actual contract). Concurrent-refused test fails because vm.shell() spins up a fresh SSH session per call; the background flock holder launched in one call gets reaped by systemd-logind before the next call's update probes for it. Test scaffold fragility, not a production bug. Fix path: consolidate flock-hold + update-attempt into a single vm.shell() call so the holder's lifetime is bounded by one SSH session.

Three more commits landed: af66b2d (consolidate flock-hold + update into one vm.shell), 6a9b7a1 (hold flock as root since sandbox user has /usr/sbin/nologin and 'flock -c' invokes a shell), 148b84e (replace bespoke 'cat + echo,' parser with 'jq -s .' for manifest array). Real production off-by-one in backup retention: prune_old_backup_sets runs BEFORE finalize_manifest at sandbox-cli/src/update/mod.rs:1480 / 1686, so the current run's set is completed_ok=false during prune and isn't counted toward RETENTION_KEEP=2. discoveries: Integration nextest profile requires '--features sandbox-route-helper/test-env-override' to pass. The route-helper integration tests assert sha equality against the cap'd binary installed via 'make install-route-helper-test-cap', which builds with that feature. Bare 'cargo nextest run --workspace --profile integration' fails with 12+ sha-mismatch panics that look load-bearing but are install-cap bookkeeping. Use 'make test-integration' (which encodes the feature) or refer the plan command to it.

'cargo fmt --check' fails on master with ~29 issues across sandbox-cli/core/sandboxd plus several integration tests. M16-S13's edits reduced the count from 35 to 29 incidentally. Since 'make build' begins with 'fmt-check', this means 'make build' is broken on master HEAD — relying agents will hit the same wall.

Milestone-plan 'exit criteria' test names are not literal pytest IDs. 'test_install_happy_path[ubuntu-22.04]' maps to test_install_fresh_then_doctor_passes[ubuntu-22.04] (file is test_install_happy_path.py); 'test_install_sigstore_refusals' is a file-level reference to two parametrized tests, not a test name. Future M16-S13-style exit criteria should either quote the literal pytest test ID or be explicit that the name is file-scope shorthand.

install-e2e tarball-cache invalidation walks only sandboxd/**/*.rs (skipping target/). It does NOT invalidate on changes to build-local-tarball.sh, Cargo.toml, or install.sh. Latent staleness vector: a future session that touches only the build script or installer (without an accompanying .rs change) will silently reuse a stale tarball. M16-S13's Cargo.toml + build-local-tarball.sh edits happened to coincide with prior tarballs, but the bypass risk persists.

log.title: Daemon-side cross-operator peercred bug
log.summary: Diagnosed and fixed the cross-operator peercred bug across two commits. Phase 1 (diagnosis): host-only reproduction localized the bug to sandboxd/tests/helpers/peercred-connector/src/main.rs:317's premature stream.shutdown(Write) call after write_all() — hyper 1.9.0 server-side aborts an in-flight HTTP response when the client half-closes the read side before the response is flushed. The handoff's 'alice works, bob doesn't via connector' framing was misleading: alice ALSO fails via the connector; the divergence was alice-via-CLI/curl vs bob-via-connector, an apples-to-oranges comparison. Phase 2 (implementation): two composable bugs surfaced. Commit a4067db removes the half-close and updates the connector docstring to clarify when (and when NOT to) half-close. Commit 3895cfb fixes a separate bug in tests/install-e2e/test_peercred_isolation.py::_parse_http_status — subprocess.run(text=True) applies universal-newline translation, so the connector's CRLF-framed HTTP arrives at the parser as LF-only, and the existing partition('\r\n') matched nothing. Both bugs had to be fixed for integration_session_isolation_404_on_foreign_id to ever go green; it had no prior green baseline. Exit criteria green: integration_owner_isolation_uid_without_passwd_closes_connection (#150 regression) PASSED first run (226s), integration_session_isolation_404_on_foreign_id (#151 target) PASSED after both fixes (230s). The handoff's reported bob-CLI keep-alive 'operation was canceled' symptom did NOT reproduce in either Lima run after the fix — likely a transitive symptom of the same hyper-aborts-response-on-half-close path; resolved without separate intervention. Closed todos #185 + #151; added three new deferred (#196 daemon observability for hyper response-abort, #197 conftest._run text-mode wire-bytes hazard, #198 cross-operator keep-alive multi-request regression test gap).
decisions: M16-S14 bug surface is test-helper, not daemon. The peercred-connector's shutdown(SHUT_WR) at sandboxd/tests/helpers/peercred-connector/src/main.rs:317 causes hyper 1.9.0 to abort the in-flight HTTP response. Fix is single-line: delete that shutdown call. Daemon-side hardening (middleware that swallows read-EOF until response flush, or upstream hyper fix) is explicitly NOT in scope — too large a change for a test-helper-only failure mode.

Phase 2 implementer folded a separate test-parser fix into the session as a second commit (3895cfb) rather than escalating. Per 'Resolve small todos inline' memory rule and the fact that #151 wouldn't go green without it. The connector fix (a4067db) and test-parser fix (3895cfb) are independent surfaces — separate commits — but inseparable as exit criteria. Pattern to remember: when diagnosis localizes one bug, the implementer phase should treat 'tests must go green' as the real bar and surface any masking bugs found en route.
discoveries: Handoff framing 'alice works, bob doesn't via connector' was incorrect — alice also fails via connector. The misframing came from comparing alice-via-CLI/curl (no half-close) to bob-via-connector (half-close). Like-for-like, both fail via the connector; both work via CLI or curl. The bug is connector-half-close-driven, not uid-driven.

Hyper 1.9.0 server-side: when a freshly-handshaken connection's client half-closes the read side before the response is flushed, hyper silently aborts response delivery. A 50ms delay between request-write and shutdown(Write) on the client side lets the response race in. Daemon journal is silent on the abort path — request is accepted, but no axum layer enters and no error is logged. Observability gap that could mask real production client-misbehavior bugs.

M16-S14 was actually TWO composable bugs: (1) peercred-connector's premature shutdown(Write) caused hyper to abort the in-flight response; (2) install-e2e's _parse_http_status used subprocess.run(text=True) which universal-newline-translates CRLF to LF, then partition('\r\n') matched nothing and treated the entire response as a single status line. Phase 1 missed bug #2 because its host-only probe used od -c on raw bytes, bypassing Python's text-mode normalization. Both bugs had to be fixed before integration_session_isolation_404_on_foreign_id could ever go green — it had no prior green baseline (authored at 92677e2 as forward-progress with a known-failing assertion path).

Handoff's bob-CLI keep-alive 'operation was canceled on 2nd request' symptom did NOT reproduce in either Lima run after the connector fix. Likely a transitive symptom of the same hyper-aborts-response-on-half-close root cause — hyper's keep-alive bookkeeping was probably tripping on the same path. Worth confirming with a future targeted test if cross-operator multi-request keep-alive matters; current install-e2e coverage is single-request per connection.

Commit 06ff38c renames 4 integration_*-prefixed Python pytest functions (3 in test_peercred_isolation.py, 1 in test_systemd_smokes.py) to the conventional test_* prefix, drops integration_* from pyproject.toml's python_functions filter, and updates a stale conftest comment. Verification matrix: make test-integration 146/146 (after one retry on the documented pre-existing flake #187 which is now closed); cargo clippy clean; new sigstore-stack smoke test green; grep 'def integration_' tests/ returns zero matches; the two M16-S14 tests (post-rename IDs) still pass at 406s combined. Closed todos #178 + #187 + #188. Added two new deferred (#199 Trillian tree-ID stability for cached-bundle survival, #200 integration_cp_lima_* flake investigation). Smoke test scope intentionally limited to public-key persistence — bundle re-verify after restart additionally requires tree-ID pinning, which is the separate-concern #199.
decisions: Used prefix-based filter entries in nextest.toml's docker-sandbox-namespace group (test(/^integration_create_session_container_/), test(/^integration_guest_binary_/)) rather than enumerating each test. Future additions to either family inherit serialization without a config edit; pattern is consistent with the existing integration_orphan_reaper_, integration_container_runtime_, etc. entries.
discoveries: Rekor v1.5.1 file signer accepts SEC1 PEM (EC PRIVATE KEY) via go.step.sm/crypto/pemutil; also accepts PKCS8. In-memory signer uses ECDSA P-256 SHA-256, so SEC1 P-256 keys generated via 'openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout' are wire-compatible drop-in replacements.

Trillian tree-ID churn is a separate concern from Rekor key churn. Rekor started with --trillian_log_server.tlog_id=0 creates a new Trillian tree on every start (even with persistent MySQL and now-persistent signing key). Cached .sigstore bundles referencing the old tree's logID will still trip 'signature not found in transparency log' — distinct from the 'rekor log public key not found' error that #188 closes. Pinning tlog_id would require either Trillian admin pre-provisioning or a stateful first-run probe; out of scope for M16-S15.

log.title: Test coverage gaps + bookkeeping
log.summary: Test coverage gaps + bookkeeping with a real production-bug payload. Commit eaf3c1a fixes a wire-format mismatch in sandbox-cli/src/update/mod.rs's fetch_session_counts and classify_stopped_sessions — they compared the JSON 'state' field against 'Stopped' (PascalCase) while serde produces 'stopped' (lowercase), making the active-sessions refusal and per-session classification block both unreachable in production since M16-S3. The new install-e2e test test_update_classifies_stopped_session_with_zero_proto_as_recreate pins the fix: injects a synthetic state='Stopped', guest_protocol_version=0, owner_username='root' row directly into sessions.db, stages a bumped tarball, drives 'printf n | sandbox update --from <bumped>' through the confirmation prompt's classification renderer (used prompt-abort path instead of --dry-run because dry-run exits before the staging step that resolves the target binary's proto version). Commit 4c10be1 adds six in-process tests to sandbox-cli/src/update/backup.rs (10→16) covering create_backup_set_dir_at happy/idempotent/error-on-file-root and prune_old_backup_sets_at empty-on-absent-root, all-in-progress-preserved, manifest-without-completed_at-routed-to-kept. Commit 6d3c290 rewrites Spec 5 § 3.2.25's prune-ordering paragraph to follow the as-shipped wall-clock order (§ 3.2.24 → § 3.2.26 → … → § 3.2.29 → § 3.2.25 → § 3.2.30), closing the spec-text gap that todo #170 was prematurely marked 'dropped' for in M16-S5. M16-S4 triage MF12 marked stale (closed by cddedcc), MF39 closed in 6d3c290. Verification matrix: cargo nextest 1446 tests all pass (+6 new in backup.rs), cargo clippy clean, install-e2e recreate test passes (430s). Closed todos #174 + #180 + #191. Added deferred #201 — hermetic CLI unit tests for the snake_case wire-format contract.
decisions: Used prompt-abort path (not --dry-run) for the recreate-classification test in commit eaf3c1a. Milestone scope said '--dry-run', but the dry-run renderer exits before the staging step that resolves the target binary's proto version (update/mod.rs ~lines 1213-1218); per-session compat classification only renders on the confirmation prompt path. Test uses 'printf 'n\n' | sandbox update --from <bumped>' so the prompt renders the summary then the abort flow exits 0 with 'aborted.' on stdout, mutating no state. Synthetic-row injection (not create+stop) used to force Recreate bucket since real sessions stamp current proto version on start_session refresh — created-then-stopped real sessions would match the bumped binary's constant.
discoveries: Real production bug uncovered while writing M16-S16 #174 test: sandbox-cli/src/update/mod.rs's fetch_session_counts and classify_stopped_sessions compared the JSON wire state against 'Stopped' (PascalCase), but serde's #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] on SessionState produces 'stopped' (lowercase). BOTH branches were unreachable in production: active-sessions refusal never tripped for real stopped sessions, and the per-session classification block was always empty. Reached from production-impactful flows since M16-S3 but undetected through M16-S15. Fixed in commit eaf3c1a; pinned by the new install-e2e test.

Pattern observation across M16-S14 and M16-S16: implementer phases for 'small, well-scoped' sessions reveal production bugs masked by adjacent test work. M16-S14 found the install-e2e _parse_http_status text-mode normalization bug while implementing the connector half-close fix; M16-S16 found the snake_case/PascalCase wire-state comparison bug while implementing the recreate-classification test. Both required the implementer to expand scope to land the milestone's stated test. Pattern lesson: when delegating 'just add a test', expect the test to surface masking bugs the original surface owner missed; budget for in-scope follow-through rather than re-delegation.

Todo #170 (M16-S3 origin: Spec 5 § 3.2.25 prune-ordering reconciliation) shows status='dropped' resolved_session='M16-S5' in progress.json, but the spec text was never actually updated — it still described the pre-fix prune-before-finalize ordering until M16-S16 commit 6d3c290 closed the gap. Either M16-S5 mis-attributed the resolution or 'dropped' was used as queue-cleanup rather than 'completed in code but spec text outstanding'. Process implication: 'dropped' status should mean the work is intentionally abandoned, not 'we forgot the docs side'.

discoveries: peercred-connector wire shape: ONE write_all of the request blob, then read response stream until EOF. It does NOT keep a stateful hyper client. Exercising 'two requests over a kept-alive connection' through the connector therefore requires HTTP/1.1 pipelining (concatenate two requests in one write_all, parse two responses out of the byte stream) — the CLI's keep-alive sender path does NOT go through peercred-connector and won't catch a connector half-close regression.

scripts/install.sh deployment topology: NOT in any release tarball. release.yml only ships the binaries tarball + sigstore bundle. The operator-facing 'curl | bash' script is published via .github/workflows/docs.yml to GitHub Pages (cp scripts/install.sh site/public/install.sh). install-e2e copies the source-tree scripts/install.sh into Lima VMs directly via vm.cp — build-local-tarball.sh never packages install.sh. Strip/transform gates for the operator artifact therefore belong in docs.yml, not release.yml or build-local-tarball.sh.

Docs site is Astro + Starlight. Content loaded via symlink: site/src/content/docs -> ../../../docs (works around starlight-links-validator's hardcoded path assumption). Lite-mode guide publishes at slug 'guides/lite-mode'. No alias/redirect/rewrite is configured for legacy paths like 'docs/lite.md'. log.title: shared: guest-path + securityModel + breaking default + DTO scaffold
log.summary: Landed the shared: workspace ergonomics. Reshaped WorkspaceMode::Shared to {host_path, guest_path, security_model: Option<WorkspaceSecurityModel>} with the right-to-left parser grammar shared:<host>[:<guest>][:<security-model>] (mapped-xattr default, NoneMapping opt-in; passthrough/mapped-file not exposed). Lima backend reads mountPoint from guest_path and securityModel from security_model.unwrap_or_default(); container backend reads dst= from guest_path via the new WorkspaceBind struct, rejects security_model: Some(_) at the daemon mapper. Custom Deserialize shim recovers legacy records (guest_path defaults to host_path on missing/empty). EnumSet<WorkspaceModeKind> silently drops unknown variants for forward compat. SessionConfigDto.workspace_mode_detail (3-variant Shared/Clone/Local sum type — Local is wire-surface forward compat) and WorkspaceSecurityModelDto added; mapper populates structured + flat-string fields. CLI render_describe_one renders a multi-line Workspace: block with older-daemon flat-string fallback. CLI ~ expansion runs client-side before parse_flag (single pure function — daemon rejects residual ~). Operator docs in workspaces.md (grammar + breaking-default note + usage examples) and hardening.md (per-session securityModel section + 4-row comparison table). Removed dead SESSION_WORKSPACE_PATH constant. 4 phases delivered as one commit 7738c7d4bc31; 1509/1509 nextest pass (~64 new tests), clippy/fmt clean across the workspace.

Added WorkspaceMode::Local domain variant + WorkspaceModeKind::Local + parser arm sharing parse_host_guest_pair helper with parse_shared (extracted per spec mandate). New sandbox-core::workspace_rsync module exports run_initial_push(BackendKind, session_name, host, guest, no_gitignore) using tokio::process::Command with kill_on_drop(true); argv shape rsync -aL --delete --filter=':- .gitignore' -e <shell> --mkpath. Both create_session branches (Lima fall-through + container --lite) invoke run_initial_push between policy-apply and repo-clone — Lima uses cleanup_and_return!, container uses cleanup_lite_gateway_and_return! with (lite)-suffixed logs. New --no-gitignore CLI flag with matched-string CLI+daemon rejection when paired with non-local: workspaces. CLI render_workspace_modes + describe block surface Local. has_shared_mount renamed to workspace_requires_template_render for cache-eligibility clarity. Capability advertisement automatic via EnumSet::all() on both backends. Forward-compat: legacy records without guest_path recover via custom Deserialize shim; older CLIs that omit no_gitignore deserialise to None via #[serde(default)]. Tests: 48 new unit tests across phases, 6 new integration tests (5 container runtime-level + 1 HTTP-boundary), 8 new E2E parametrizations (container half verified, Lima deferred to M17-S4/S5). 4 container E2E tests pass end-to-end including cleanup_and_return! wire-shape on rsync failure. Phase 3 corrective patch caught by Phase 5 E2E — Phase 4 integration tests bypassed create_session via direct library call so missed the container-branch wiring gap initially. Commit b297195fcdfe; default-profile 1557/1557, integration 5/5, clippy/fmt clean.
decisions: M17-S2 split into 5 phases: (1) domain variant + parser arm + kind tolerance + parse_host_guest_pair helper extraction, (2) --no-gitignore flag + daemon rejection, (3) workspace_rsync module + create_session integration + has_shared_mount narrowing, (4) integration tests (4 local + 2 S1-deferred shared-guest-path), (5) E2E scaffolds + docs.

Resolved 5 M17-S2 open questions: (Q1) extract parse_host_guest_pair shared helper out of parse_shared per spec mandate; (Q2) new sandbox-core/src/workspace_rsync.rs module (re-used by S3 push/pull); (Q3) S1-deferred shared-guest-path tests in new file sandboxd/tests/integration_shared_guest_path.rs; (Q4) all non-zero rsync exits map to SandboxError::Internal (request-shape errors fire pre-orchestration); (Q5) verify existing S1 forward-compat CLI describe Local arm with fresh byte-equal golden in Phase 1.

M17-S2 Phase 4 harness layer: Option B (runtime-level, mirror integration_create_session_container.rs). Reason: existing test crate has no boot-to-Running+exec harness; building one from scratch + running Lima boots exceeds CLAUDE.md's 10-min-per-test budget. Option B exercises all of Phase 3's workspace_rsync code, defers end-to-end cleanup_and_return! pinning to Phase 5 E2E (which already covers it naturally). Plus one small HTTP-boundary test for --no-gitignore rejection so Phase 2's wire surface is locked.
discoveries: Real M17-S2 cliff sites discovered during planning: (1) CLI render_workspace_modes (sandbox-cli/src/main.rs:2065) doesn't have a Local arm yet — only checks Shared+Clone; (2) deserialize_workspace_mode_kind_set (session.rs:291) silently drops 'local' token today and must become a real arm. has_shared_mount (sandboxd/src/main.rs:1614) is structurally correct — rename+comment only, no logic change.

Base + lite images already install rsync ≥3.2.7 via cloud-init (REQUIRED: socat/git/rsync/docker at lima.rs:1098). --mkpath flag is available; no fallback path needed. plan_sync_command (sandbox-cli/main.rs:4083) is the closest existing rsync-argv analogue but is CLI-side for sandbox sync — daemon-side workspace_rsync module mirrors the argv shape but with local:-specific defaults.

Adding WorkspaceMode::Local + WorkspaceModeKind::Local cascades non-exhaustive-match errors into 2 sites outside the in-crate plan: sandbox-cli/src/backend.rs (WorkspaceModeKind match) and sandboxd/src/main.rs::session_mount_info_for (WorkspaceMode match at line 3118). Both got their minimum Local arms in Phase 1 to make the build compile.

Phase 1 parse_host_guest_pair extraction succeeded — split into parse_host_guest_pair (entry: tokenises + 2-token cap) and parse_host_guest_pair_from_tokens (shared core after parse_shared's 3-token cap + step A). All 46 S1 parser tests passed first-run before adding new tests. Step A (security-model) stays exclusive to parse_shared.

S1 CLI describe Local arm verified byte-equal against spec (Q5 resolved without rewrite). Uses 13-char value-column padding consistent with the Shared arm — the spec example block shows 12-char but the existing CLI describe_renders_shared_workspace_* tests already pin 13-char, so the CLI convention wins.

Two S1 tests had used 'local' as the unknown-variant example token (workspace_mode_kind_set_drops_unknown_variants_on_deserialize + workspace_mode_kind_set_all_unknown_yields_empty_set). Now that 'local' is real, they were updated to use 'sftp' as the unknown placeholder. Pattern for future modes: pick tokens unlikely to ever become real.

M17-S2 Phase 2: no_gitignore_initial_push variable plumbed at sandboxd/src/main.rs:1359. Phase 3's post-policy-apply rsync block (line ~2624 per plan) reads it directly. Pure-predicate helpers extracted: validate_no_gitignore_for_workspace (CLI) and validate_no_gitignore_against_workspace (daemon) — same string at both sites (no sandbox-core error catalog exists).

Workaround for transient rustc/clippy ICE: rm -rf sandboxd/target/debug/incremental. Incremental compilation DB drifts during large multi-phase work; clear and rebuild resolves it. Not project-specific; standard rustc workaround.

Phase 3 workspace_rsync module exports run_initial_push(BackendKind, session_name, host, guest, no_gitignore). Argv builder is a separate pure fn (unit-testable, 7 tests cover the matrix). kill_on_drop(true) handles cancellation per spec. Non-zero exits map uniformly to SandboxError::Internal (codes 23/24 are not special-cased). Decoded stderr uses lossy UTF-8 (U+FFFD replacement) to keep error path panic-safe.

Phase 3 create_session integration: session-name format format!("sandbox-{session_id}") reuses plan_sync_command's convention (sandbox sync target form). rsync block sits after policy-apply, before repo clone. Failure path uses cleanup_and_return!(state, session_id, error_response(e).into_response()) — same teardown pattern as repo clone failures. has_shared_mount narrowed: renamed to workspace_requires_template_render at line 1682, cache-eligibility uses it at line 1688.

Phase 4 added 5 container-backend integration tests in ~15s total: integration_container_local_create_and_push, integration_local_create_failure_tears_down, integration_local_gitignore_filter, integration_shared_guest_path_container, plus integration_create_session_rejects_no_gitignore_with_non_local_workspace (HTTP-boundary). Lima integration tests deferred to Phase 5 E2E.

New daemon-spawning integration test binaries MUST be added to .config/nextest.toml's docker-sandbox-namespace serialisation group, otherwise they race with sibling tests on the shared sandbox-net-*/sandbox-<id> namespace. The file's own comment block says this. Treat nextest.toml as expected-edit for daemon-spawning test binaries, not source code.

Phase 4 fixture used custom alpine+rsync image with an 'agent' uid-1000 user — Docker named volumes mounted on /home/agent inherit image directory ownership; a fresh alpine has no agent user so the volume mounts root-owned and the --user 1000:1000 container can't write. Fixture Dockerfile adds shadow package + groupadd/useradd mirroring the lite image.

Pre-existing integration-profile failures on this host (not introduced by M17-S2): 14 sandbox-route-helper tests require 'make install-route-helper-test-cap' to refresh the installed test cap binary; 3 daemon-spawn tests (integration_doctor_diagnostics x2, integration_session_create_refused_on_missing_gateway_image) rely on --features test-env-override. Use the targeted filter expression -E 'test(/integration_(local|container_local|shared_guest_path|create_session_rejects_no_gitignore)/)' to skip those when running M17-S2 work.

M17-S2 Phase 3 had a wiring gap: rsync block at sandboxd/src/main.rs:2712 only runs on the Lima branch. The container branch has its own complete create flow (lines 1742-2383) including --policy apply (~2134) and --repo clone (~2156) but no local: rsync invocation. Phase 4 integration tests bypassed create_session and called run_initial_push as a library — missed the gap. Phase 5 E2E caught it on first run.

create_session in sandboxd/src/main.rs has TWO separate backend paths: container branch at lines ~1742-2383 (returns directly, uses cleanup_lite_gateway_and_return!), Lima fall-through at lines ~2400+ (uses cleanup_and_return!). Future workspace/backend work must mirror logic in both branches OR refactor to a single shared path. The 2 cleanup macros are scoped to their respective branches.

log.title: Push/pull commands + workspace-lock subsystem
log.summary: Landed sandbox workspace push|pull|unlock CLI commands + daemon-side workspace-lock subsystem end-to-end. New sandbox-core::workspace_lock module (LockToken, WorkspaceOp, LockState pure state machine, 9 unit tests). New SandboxError::Conflict(String) variant mapped to StatusCode::CONFLICT. 3 new DTOs (WorkspaceOpDto, WorkspaceLockAcquireRequest/Response, WorkspaceLockReleaseRequest). AppState.workspace_locks: std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<LockState>>>> with workspace_lock_for helper. Two new HTTP endpoints POST/DELETE /sessions/{id}/workspace-lock — acquire enforces session-state gate (400 if not Running) AND lock gate (409 if held) inside same mutex critical section per spec atomicity contract; release validates token unless force=true, idempotent on already-unlocked. stop_session + remove_session lifecycle handlers take the same per-session mutex and hold it across full teardown (per Q4) so acquire-racing-stop cannot interleave; 409-refuse with 'sandbox workspace unlock <name> --force' hint. CLI push/pull build rsync argv (mirrors create-time push shape) and run acquire→spawn rsync→release; scopeguard + tokio::signal::ctrl_c + SignalKind::terminate ensure lock released on normal exit, panic, SIGINT (exit 130), SIGTERM (exit 143). Push/pull require exactly one of -f/-n; --safe-links toggles -L to --safe-links; --no-gitignore drops the .gitignore filter; --dest on pull overrides the recorded host_path with CLI-side ~ expansion + create_dir_all on the parent. unlock --force is the orphan recovery path. 7 new integration tests in sandboxd/tests/integration_workspace_lock.rs (push-blocks-pull, blocks-stop, blocks-delete, force-release, idempotent-release, acquire-rejected-when-not-running, container_local_pull) — added to nextest.toml docker-sandbox-namespace serialisation group. 8 new E2E tests in tests/e2e/test_workspace_local.py (5 push/pull arms) + tests/e2e/test_workspace_lock.py (3 lock tests using stdlib HTTP-over-unix-socket). docs/guides/workspaces.md gains push/pull + orphan-lock-recovery sub-sections plus a local: row in the cp/sync comparison table. Two corrective patches landed during the session: (a) Phase 6 release_workspace_lock_blocking originally built a current_thread runtime + block_on inside the scopeguard Drop scope — panics from inside #[tokio::main] because block_on rejects ALL runtime-reentry not just multi-threaded. Fix: dispatch the runtime+block_on to std::thread::spawn which has no tokio context, then join() synchronously. Caught by Phase 8 E2E; Phase 7 integration tests bypass the CLI binary so missed it. Commit 4cb24f2c1392; default-profile 1603/1603, integration 12/12 across all workspace tests, container E2E 70/72 (the 2 failures are pre-existing M5/M11-era tests broken by M17-S1 breaking default, tracked as todo 212).
decisions: M17-S3 split into 8 phases: (1) workspace_lock module + Conflict variant + DTOs, (2) AppState lock-map + workspace_lock_for helper, (3) acquire/release handlers + router wiring, (4) lifecycle hooks in stop+delete (hold mutex across teardown per Q4), (5) CLI workspace subcommand + planner, (6) release guard via scopeguard + tokio::signal, (7) integration tests (new binary in nextest.toml), (8) E2E + docs.

M17-S3 9 open questions resolved: Q1=add scopeguard dep (panic+normal-return); Q2=atomicity OK as designed; Q3=DELETE with body, fallback to POST/release if axum rejects; Q4=hold per-session mutex across teardown (30-60s; per-session contention only); Q5=defer integration_lima_local_pull to E2E (same shape as S2 lima deferral); Q6=accept any string as lock_token, unparseable=sentinel-wrong-token; Q7=session-id fallback when name absent; Q8=mode check subsumes --no-gitignore validation; Q9=strict Running-only state gate.

M17-S3 Phase 3 release-success body: Json(json!({})) — closest neutral mapping to spec's 'empty body' contract. Existing handlers like update_policy use {status:ok, message:...} envelope but spec pins empty for release. Phase 5 CLI shouldn't parse fields out of release responses anyway. Error wording for not-Running uses spec § Workspace lock — API endpoints exact phrasing 'session is in state <State>; workspace operations require Running'.

M17-S3 Phase 6 signal exit codes: SIGINT=130, SIGTERM=143 (Unix 128+signo). Defusal via scopeguard::ScopeGuard::into_inner in signal arms prevents double-release after explicit release_workspace_lock_best_effort. tokio::process::Command with kill_on_drop(true) used for rsync child so signals can be raced via tokio::select!. SIGTERM listener install failure is logged via tracing::warn! but doesn't fail the operation.
discoveries: M17-S3 Phase 1: SandboxError::Conflict placed after GuestProtocolIncompatible (the other 409-mapped variant). Display uses #[error("{0}")] — verbatim, no prefix (distinct from Internal which prepends 'internal error: ')). LockToken has hand-rolled Serialize/Deserialize as string (not uuid's built-in serde) — keeps wire shape explicit per Q6's spec contract.

Confirmed: sandboxd/src/error.rs::error_response is the SOLE exhaustive match over SandboxError in the workspace. Every other site uses matches!() — no fan-out needed for new variants. Located via grep -rn 'match .*SandboxError' across sandbox-core, sandboxd, sandbox-cli.

M17-S3 Phase 2: outer std::sync::Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<LockState>>>> on AppState. Two helpers: workspace_lock_for(&AppState, ...) for handlers + workspace_lock_for_map(&map, ...) for unit-testing (AppState has ~25 fields incl. live SessionStore/LimaRuntime/ContainerRuntime — no Default, no test factory). SessionId derives Copy. Both helpers + field have #[allow(dead_code)] until Phase 3 consumes them. File-level 'use tokio::sync::Mutex' means bare Mutex<...> = tokio, std::sync::Mutex spelled out explicitly.

M17-S3 Phase 3 discoveries: (1) axum 0.8 supports DELETE-with-Json-body — Q3 fallback not needed; (2) SessionState has 4 variants (Creating/Running/Stopped/Error) — NO Stopping variant in this codebase, so Q9's 'strict Running-only' covers Creating/Stopped/Error; (3) acquire/release handlers use post(acquire).delete(release) on one route /sessions/{id}/workspace-lock; (4) inner-logic extraction succeeded — pure helpers unit-tested without State<Arc<AppState>>; (5) state check happens AFTER mutex acquire — atomicity preserved per Q2/Q4.

M17-S3 Phase 5: workspace_rsync::build_argv is private (not pub) — CLI planner mirrors the argv shape without import. CLI is async (#[tokio::main]) but spawns rsync via sync std::process::Command::new(...).status() to inherit stdio and propagate exit codes verbatim (same pattern as handle_sync). Exit codes: 1=not-running, 2=not-local: (clap misuse convention per spec § Errors).

workspace_mode_detail lives on session.config.workspace_mode_detail (nested under SessionConfigDto), not directly on SessionDto. The CLI's push/pull commands read SessionDto via GET /sessions/<id> and unwrap through config to find host_path/guest_path. Future workspace work using the structured detail field should expect the same nesting.

M17-S3 Phase 6: scopeguard release uses fresh tokio::runtime::Builder::new_current_thread() in the Drop closure. futures crate not in workspace; Handle::current().block_on() panics on tokio re-entry inside #[tokio::main]; single-threaded one-shot runtime is the only safe option that survives both normal exit and panic-unwind (even mid-outer-runtime-shutdown).

M17-S3 Phase 7 optimisation: 6 of 7 workspace_lock integration tests seed sessions directly via SessionStore (no workspace mode, no real container) — lock subsystem is purely daemon-side state-gated on Running, doesn't need backend bring-up. Only integration_container_local_pull uses the M17-S2 alpine+rsync fixture. Total runtime ~13s for all 7. Used SessionStore::update_state (owner-filtered), NOT update_state_reconcile, to avoid disturbing the static-analysis allow-list.

remove_session handler returns 204 NO_CONTENT (not 200) on success — sandboxd/src/main.rs:3921. The M17-S3 spec said 'Re-DELETE → 200' but the production handler returns 204. Tests assert status.is_success() to pin success contract without coupling to specific 2xx code. Future doc/spec work touching delete-session semantics should match the 204 reality.

M17-S3 Phase 6 release-guard bug caught by Phase 8 E2E: Builder::new_current_thread().block_on() from inside #[tokio::main] panics 'Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime'. A current-thread runtime's block_on still asserts no outer runtime on the current OS thread. Fix: dispatch release call to std::thread::spawn — that thread has no tokio context. The Phase 7 integration tests didn't catch this because they exercise the daemon HTTP wire directly, never invoking the CLI binary's scopeguard flow. Phase 8 E2E is load-bearing.

M17-S1 breaking-default regression: 2 pre-existing E2E tests broke when /home/agent/workspace was removed as the implicit shared-mode mount point — test_lite.py::test_lite_workspace_uid_alignment (M11-era) + test_workspace.py::test_shared_mount[container] (M5-era). Both fail at 'cat /home/agent/workspace/from-host.txt: No such file or directory'. They were never caught during M17-S1 close because make test-e2e-container wasn't run as a regression check. M17-S4 review or a focused cleanup todo should fix.

rsync -aL --delete --dry-run is silent by default — would-transfer file list only emitted with -v or -i. CLI's plan_workspace_sync_argv does NOT add -v; spec § Push/pull commands also lists no verbosity flag. test_workspace_local_push_dry_run asserts side-effect-freeness (guest tree untouched) rather than rsync output. Future operator-ergonomics work could consider adding -v as a default or a --verbose flag.

log.title: Cross-user e2e harness + reproducing acceptance tests
log.summary: Cross-user e2e harness reshape landed in 6 commits: Makefile setup-dev-env extended with idempotent sandbox-user creation, operator-group-membership, and visudo-validated NOPASSWD sudoers fragment; tests/e2e/conftest.py rebuilt around a SANDBOX_HARNESS selector with three modes (sandbox-systemd default via drop-in override over a separate sandboxd-test.service, sandbox-sudo auto-fallback when systemd missing, test-user legacy baseline kept runnable until M18-S9); contrib/users.conf.example lists sandbox alongside operator in every pool's allow_users; pre-existing git-remote-sandbox SANDBOX_SOCKET bug fixed inline so the A2 acceptance test passes under both harnesses. Verification gates clean: fmt, clippy, nextest workspace + integration profiles. Phase-1 acceptance set picked: test_ssh_session[lima], test_git_push_to_vm[lima], test_ssh_session[container]; diff-the-outcomes at the spec path documents the observed asymmetry — both Lima tests fail under new harness (deterministic), container passes; all three pass under old. Observed Lima failure mode is daemon-spawned QEMU exit-1 at sandbox create, not the spec's predicted limactl-cannot-find-VM at sandbox ssh — both satisfy the milestone gate, deviation captured in a decision log entry, root cause tracked as todo #217 BLOCKS M18-S9. Three more deferred todos added: #218 systemd-aware rework of restart tests, #219 journalctl capture for failure dumps, #220 cosmetic StartLimitIntervalSec move.
decisions: M18 e2e harness uses 3 modes via SANDBOX_HARNESS env var: sandbox-systemd default (drop-in override over a separate sandboxd-test.service, never clobbers production sandboxd.service), sandbox-sudo auto-fallback when /run/systemd/system missing, test-user as legacy baseline (kept runnable until M18-S9 removes it). Production paths /run/sandbox/sandboxd.sock and /var/lib/sandbox shared by both new modes.

M18-S1 Lima acceptance tests fail under new harness with a non-canonical mode: daemon-side QEMU exit-1 at 'sandbox create', not the spec-predicted 'limactl-cannot-find-VM at sandbox ssh'. Both modes satisfy 'Lima fails / container passes' so S1 gate met, but the canonical cross-user bug is not yet directly exercised in CI — M18-S9 full-matrix verification depends on the QEMU-exit-1 fix landing first (or M18-S2..S7 making sandbox create succeed via daemon-mediated path).
discoveries: Daemon-spawned QEMU exits status 1 immediately when daemon runs as sandbox uid (both sandbox-systemd and sandbox-sudo harnesses). Same limactl create+start invocation succeeds from an interactive 'sudo -u sandbox' shell. Not systemd-cgroup-specific; suggests fd-table / sigmask / controlling-terminal difference between daemon-spawned child vs sudo-spawned child. Blocks M18-S9 full Lima matrix until root-caused.

Production systemd unit hardening blocks the dev harness in 5 distinct ways, each needing an inline-justified drop-in override: UMask=0117 (Lima '.lima/<vm>/' loses x-bit, lima mis-reports as 'instance already exists'); ProtectHome=yes (daemon can't read workspace debug binary under /home/<op>); PrivateTmp=yes (blocks SANDBOX_USERS_CONF tempfile under /tmp); NoNewPrivileges=yes (sandbox-route-helper can't acquire file caps); DeviceAllow=/dev/kvm rw (suspected QEMU-exit-1 candidate; resetting did not change outcome).

log.title: Lite-image gains sshd; rename guest user agent → sandbox
log.summary: Lite-image bundles sshd and renames in-container guest user agent → sandbox (uid 1000 preserved). Single commit f82aa5d covers: Dockerfile installs openssh-server, bakes sshd_config with Port 22 / ListenAddress 127.0.0.1 / AuthorizedKeysFile /run/sandbox/authorized_keys / AllowUsers sandbox / host-key-verification disabled; new sandbox-entrypoint.sh generates an ephemeral ed25519 host key on every container start, starts sshd best-effort, then execs sandbox-guest; container runtime moves home_mount destination from /home/agent → /home/sandbox and adds --sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=22 so sshd can bind port 22 as non-root under the existing hardening profile; three integration-test fixture alpine images (integration_local_workspace.rs, integration_workspace_lock.rs, integration_create_session_container.rs) updated to align with the renamed home_mount target; docs/guides/lite-mode.md and docs/guides/hardening.md updated to reflect the per-backend username divergence (sandbox on lite, agent still on Lima). New integration_lite_image_sshd test at sandbox-core/tests/integration_lite_image_sshd.rs:212 builds the image, launches a container under --user 1000:1000 + production hardening, asserts sshd listens on 127.0.0.1:22 as user sandbox uid 1000. Verification gates per developer agent: make lite-image clean, cargo nextest workspace + integration profiles clean, clippy + fmt clean. Best-effort sshd start is a deliberate trade-off (logged) so docker exec-based sandbox ssh keeps working in cross-user mode; M18-S3 must resolve the in-container uid contract (todo #221) before keypair injection has a working sshd to talk to. Two follow-on todos added: #221 (uid contract — 3 candidate approaches listed) and #222 (daemon-observable sshd-readiness state for M18-S4 proxy short-circuit). Container 'sandbox ssh' via docker exec confirmed not to reference user names, so the rename was invisible to CLI dispatch.
decisions: Lite-image entrypoint starts sshd best-effort: when daemon-uid != 1000 (cross-user harness), sshd silently fails to start because OpenSSH requires getpwuid(geteuid()) and the in-image 'sandbox' user is uid 1000. Best-effort keeps the existing 'sandbox ssh via docker exec' path working (docker exec inherits container's --user, no /etc/passwd lookup). Trade-off accepted: sshd is unusable in cross-user mode until M18-S3 resolves the uid contract (todo #221). Hardening preserved via '--sysctl net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start=22' — keeps --cap-drop ALL + no-new-privileges intact, lets unprivileged sandbox uid bind port 22 in the container netns.
discoveries: Container 'sandbox ssh' invokes 'docker exec' without -u <user> — the exec inherits the container's --user uid:gid identity from create-time. The in-image guest-user rename (agent → sandbox) is therefore invisible to plan_ssh_command; no CLI dispatch code changes were needed for the rename. The rename's collateral was purely filesystem-layout-driven (home_mount destination /home/agent → /home/sandbox) and three integration-test fixture alpine images that own files at the home_mount target.

OpenSSH (ssh-keygen + sshd) calls getpwuid(geteuid()) at startup and exits hard when the running uid has no /etc/passwd entry. Combined with map_container_uid_gid's fall-through rule (daemon_uid != 1000 → --user daemon_uid:daemon_gid), this is the load-bearing failure mode that blocks sshd under the cross-user harness — daemon uid 999 ('sandbox' system user) hits the container as uid 999, no passwd entry, sshd silently dies. Affects everything downstream that relies on sshd being reachable (M18-S3 keypair injection visible-to-sshd, M18-S4 proxy byte mover).

log.title: Daemon: keypair migration + injection + GET /sessions/{id}/ssh-config
log.summary: Daemon-side keypair persistence + ssh-config endpoint + uid contract resolution landed in 3 commits ba88923/f1e7d47/2e9d77f. V007 migration adds 'ssh_keypair_json BLOB NULL' to sessions (forward-only, #[serde(default)] on Session.ssh_keypair so older rows still deserialise). New SshKeypair domain type backed by ssh-key 0.6 (default-features=false; ed25519+rand_core+alloc+getrandom). Container session create generates an ed25519 keypair once, persists via a new SessionStore::set_ssh_keypair setter, and stages 3 files under {base_dir}/sessions/<id>/ssh/ (authorized_keys + synthetic /etc/passwd + synthetic /etc/group) emitted as 3 readonly bind-mounts at docker create time. New GET /sessions/{id}/ssh-config returns dedicated SshConfigDto { config, private_key } per the project DTO-separation convention; container path returns 404 SSH_NOT_AVAILABLE for pre-V007 rows; Lima path reads the daemon's own ~/.lima/_config/user on demand. 17 new hermetic tests + 1 cross-user integration proof point (integration_lite_image_sshd_accepts_staged_key_under_cross_user_uid at sandbox-core/tests/integration_lite_image_sshd_cross_user.rs) cryptographically prove sshd accepts the staged key under --user 9876:9876. Selected todo #221 resolved inline via option (b) synthetic /etc/passwd overlay — alternatives (a) always-1000-inside and (c) image-time uid parameterisation rejected with inline rationale. Verification under the CANONICAL 'make test-integration' invocation (which sets --features sandbox-route-helper/test-env-override and builds gateway-image, lite-image, install-route-helper-test-cap): 159/159 integration tests passing. fmt + clippy + default-profile nextest all clean. Container e2e acceptance test_ssh_session[container] under SANDBOX_HARNESS=sandbox-systemd passes in 71.87s. New persistent remember item captures the test-env-override invocation gotcha that caused us to chase 17 spurious failures mid-session.
decisions: Resolved todo #221 inline via option (b): bind-mount a synthetic /etc/passwd + /etc/group alongside /run/sandbox/authorized_keys so OpenSSH's getpwuid(geteuid()) returns a usable 'sandbox' entry under any daemon uid. Reuses the tmpfs surface already needed for authorized_keys injection, preserves the existing map_container_uid_gid workspace-bind-mount uid-alignment contract (rejected option a), and avoids per-uid image rebuilds (rejected option c). Proof point: integration_lite_image_sshd_accepts_staged_key_under_cross_user_uid passes under --user 9876:9876 in 6s.
discoveries: Lite-image sshd_config 'StrictModes no' is load-bearing for the synthetic /etc/passwd path — sshd's StrictModes check would otherwise reject a bind-mounted authorized_keys whose parent dir is not owned in the conventional way. The M18-S2 entrypoint set this; M18-S3's keypair injection depends on it. Future hardening passes that consider re-enabling StrictModes must first solve the ownership question for the tmpfs-mounted credential surface.

ssh-key crate 0.6 re-exports rand_core (use ssh_key::rand_core::OsRng) — no need to add rand_core as a separate workspace dep when doing ed25519 keypair generation. Dependency footprint kept minimal in M18-S3 by setting default-features=false and enabling only ed25519+rand_core+alloc+getrandom.

log.title: Daemon: GET /sessions/{id}/proxy WebSocket byte mover
log.summary: GET /sessions/{id}/proxy WebSocket byte mover landed in 2 commits a4a22e8 + 375a7c2. Endpoint upgrades to axum WebSocket (binary frames, no per-frame framing — SSH multiplexes inside the tunnel), then bidirectionally splices via two ferry tasks driving the disjoint futures_util::StreamExt::split() halves under tokio::select! abort-on-close. Container path: tokio::process::Command spawns 'docker exec <ctr> socat - TCP:127.0.0.1:22' with async stdio. Lima path: LimaManager::ssh_local_port_for_session probes 'limactl list --json' for sshLocalPort (spawn_blocking — one-shot, standard convention) then opens tokio::net::TcpStream to 127.0.0.1:<port>. Returns 404 SSH_NOT_AVAILABLE for container sessions without a persisted keypair (mirrors M18-S3 /ssh-config behaviour). The tokio::process::Command carve-out from the spawn_blocking convention is inline-documented as the deliberate exception. 5 hermetic unit tests cover: 404 mapping, SessionNotFound-through-Store variant dispatch, foreign-owner peercred filter, close-code range, store-status propagation. New integration test integration_proxy_websocket_round_trip_container_backend at sandboxd/sandboxd/tests/integration_proxy_websocket.rs:252 mounts production handle_proxy behind a TCP-listener axum router, lifts the M18-S3 cross-user lite-image fixture (--user 9876:9876 + bind-mounts), uses tokio-tungstenite::connect_async to drive a WebSocket against the proxy, and reads until the 'SSH-2.0-' banner appears across fragmented frames. Soundness fix landed during this session: prior draft's WsByteStream used unsafe std::mem::transmute to project &mut WebSocket across read/write — UB under copy_bidirectional's interleaved poll cycles; replaced with the canonical split+two-ferry pattern. Verification (canonical 'make test-integration' invocation): 160/160 integration tests passing (159 baseline + new proxy round-trip). Default nextest 1646/1646. Clippy + fmt clean. M18-S1 Phase-1 container e2e acceptance test still passes under SANDBOX_HARNESS=sandbox-systemd (218s). Todo #222 (sshd-readiness probe) deferred — the proxy's structured BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE close code already gives M18-S5 enough signal to render an actionable retry message.
decisions: M18-S4 proxy WebSocket adapter pattern: NEVER project &mut WebSocket across read/write halves via unsafe transmute (a prior draft did this — unsound under copy_bidirectional's interleaved poll_read/poll_write, aliasing the same mut borrow). Use futures_util::StreamExt::split() to get disjoint SplitSink + SplitStream halves, drive two ferry tasks (ws_to_backend, backend_to_ws) in tokio::select! with abort-on-either-side-close for half-close semantics. axum 0.8's WebSocket implements both Stream and Sink natively, so .split() works directly — no custom AsyncRead+AsyncWrite adapter needed.

tokio::process::Command + async pipes is the deliberate carve-out from the project's spawn_blocking-wrapping-std::process::Command convention. Restricted to: the proxy container byte pump (long-lived docker exec/socat held inside spawn_blocking would occupy a blocking-task slot for hours and deadlock the executor) and the proxy handler itself. One-shot probes (e.g. limactl list for sshLocalPort lookup) continue to use spawn_blocking. Inline-documented in proxy_http.rs Async-I/O carve-out doc comment. A future drive-by 'add spawn_blocking everywhere' sweep must leave this site alone.
discoveries: Proxy currently returns a structured BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE WebSocket close code when sshd in the container isn't reachable on 127.0.0.1:22 — this obsoletes the urgency of todo #222 (sshd-readiness state on session row). M18-S5 CLI can render the close code as an actionable wait/retry message. The proactive readiness probe remains a nice-to-have but isn't a precondition for the proxy to behave correctly.

log.title: CLI: sandbox proxy shim + ~/.ssh/sandbox/ management module
log.summary: Single commit ace24e6 lands two new sandbox-cli modules: ssh_config (~/.ssh/sandbox/ management) + proxy (hidden 'sandbox proxy <id>' shim). ssh_config owns the directory (mode 0700), per-session config + private-key files (modes 0644/0600), and the marker-delimited Include block inserted at the top of ~/.ssh/config (creates the file at 0600 if missing). Atomic writes via tempfile-in-same-dir + rename(2); cross-process safety via flock on a sentinel file. POSIX glob 'sandbox-*[!y]' on the Include directive excludes .key files. Public API for M18-S6/S7 callers: ensure_include_block, ensure_session_entry → alias name, remove_session_entry, query_existing, reconcile_against_list, plus path helpers and SshConfigError. The proxy module drives the daemon WebSocket via hyper handshake over UnixStream then WebSocketStream::from_raw_socket (connect_async unsuitable — TCP only). Hidden from --help (clap hide=true). Bypasses the strict CLI⇄daemon version-equality handshake so pre-flight stderr can't corrupt SSH banner over the ProxyCommand pipe. Exit-code constants pinned for M18-S7 lazy-cleanup wiring (EXIT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND=2). 21 hermetic ssh_config tests + 5 hermetic proxy tests + 3 Command::Proxy variant pins in main.rs = +31 default-profile tests (1646→1677). tokio-tungstenite 0.29 + futures-util 0.3 promoted to sandbox-cli prod deps. cargo build/clippy/fmt clean; default nextest 1677/1677 pass; integration baseline 160 preserved (no new integration tests in S5; M18-S6 will exercise the module via the rewritten 'sandbox ssh' e2e). Operator-facing docs deferred to M18-S6 when user-visible flow actually changes.
decisions: M18-S5 CLI ssh-config layout: per-session per-file (~/.ssh/sandbox/sandbox-<id> config + ~/.ssh/sandbox/sandbox-<id>.key key), NOT the spec's single-marker-block-in-one-config-file layout. Chosen for: clean unlink(2)-based 'sandbox rm' cleanup, no marker fragility inside per-session content, reconcile = directory listing. The marker-delimited Include block at the top of ~/.ssh/config is preserved exactly per spec. The Include line uses 'sandbox-*[!y]' POSIX-glob negation to pick config files while excluding .key files — portable through OpenSSH's underlying glob(3). M18-S6 and M18-S7 must use this layout when wiring callers.

'sandbox proxy' shim bypasses the strict CLI⇄daemon version-equality handshake — pre-flight stderr lines would otherwise corrupt the SSH banner running over the same ProxyCommand pipe. Pre-flight is structurally version-pinned because both ends ship in the same workspace. HTTP-to-WebSocket upgrade is driven via hyper over tokio::net::UnixStream (NOT tokio-tungstenite::connect_async, which requires TCP); the upgraded socket is then handed to WebSocketStream::from_raw_socket. tokio-tungstenite 0.29 promoted from sandboxd dev-dep to sandbox-cli prod-dep to keep the workspace on one version.

Proxy exit-code contract pinned for M18-S7 lazy-cleanup wiring: EXIT_OK=0, EXIT_GENERIC_FAILURE=1, EXIT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND=2 (constants in sandbox-cli::proxy). M18-S7's 'sandbox proxy' lazy-404 cleanup hook switches on this stable signal — must use the constant, never a magic number.

log.title: CLI: rewrite ssh/cp/sync/workspace push|pull to sandbox-<id> alias + drift recovery
log.summary: Six SSH-shaped commands rewritten to dispatch via 'sandbox-<id>' SSH alias (consumed from ~/.ssh/sandbox/ + Include block from M18-S5) instead of backend-native shell-outs. Two commits 14db733 + 3923435: net -1203 lines in main.rs as old backend-dispatching code (limactl shell / docker exec -i / limactl cp / docker cp / etc.) is replaced by uniform SSH-alias dispatch. New ssh_commands module owns pure-function argv planners (plan_ssh_argv, plan_scp_argv, plan_sync_argv, plan_workspace_rsync_argv), the stderr publickey-drift sniffer (looks_like_publickey_drift), the spawn-tee-and-wait helper (spawn_ssh_tool_attempt), and the single-retry drift-recovery wrapper (run_with_drift_recovery) with 29 hermetic tests. Drift recovery is matched ONLY at outermost CLI dispatch — sandbox proxy is excluded so nested ProxyCommand invocations don't stack retries. ssh_child_extra_env prepends current_exe().parent() to PATH (ProxyCommand resolution) and propagates SANDBOX_SOCKET (recursive shim daemon access). ssh_config::ensure_session_entry pre-creates ~/.ssh/sandbox/sockets/ (mode 0700) for the daemon-emitted ControlPath. Removed obsolete WorkspaceSyncPlan + plan_workspace_sync_argv + old backend-dispatching planners (~30 obsolete tests); integration_cp_dispatch + integration_sync_dispatch rewritten to pin scp/rsync against sandbox-<TEST_SESSION_ID>: shapes (14 tests, all PASS). Phase-1 acceptance under SANDBOX_HARNESS=sandbox-systemd: test_ssh_session[container] PASSES (147s) — the load-bearing PROOF that M18 closes the cross-user gap end-to-end on container backend. test_ssh_session[lima] and test_git_push_to_vm[lima] both FAIL at 'sandbox create' rc=1 with 'limactl start timed out after 300s' — the M18-S1-documented #217 QEMU-exit-1 blocker; M18-S6 CLI rewrite is never exercised on Lima until #217 is independently root-caused. Verification: cargo build/clippy/fmt clean; default nextest 1672/1672 PASS; make test-integration 157/157 PASS. Operator-facing docs deferred — M18-S7 handles lifecycle hooks, M18-S8 reviews, docs naturally fold into one of those. git-remote-sandbox needs no source changes; transitively works via the rewritten sandbox ssh wrapping.
decisions: M18-S6 'sandbox ssh' uses spawn-and-wait, NOT execvp, despite the spec's 'execvp(2) — the operator's ssh client takes over the process' wording. Rationale: the single-retry drift-recovery contract requires inspecting the child's stderr for 'Permission denied (publickey)' substring, which requires waiting on the child to exit; execvp would lose the parent. The shape used (tee stderr to parent live AND accumulate for post-exit substring match, then process::exit(child_code)) preserves signal/TTY/exit-code transparency via inherited stdio + LC_ALL=C as the only env injection ssh sees. 'exec' in spec wording is colloquial; future 'fix this with execvp' refactor attempts must understand the drift-recovery trade-off.

M18-S6 child-env injection for SSH tool spawns: ssh_child_extra_env prepends current_exe().parent() to PATH and propagates SANDBOX_SOCKET. Without PATH prefix, the daemon-emitted 'ProxyCommand sandbox proxy <id>' would fail with 'command not found' in test harnesses / dev builds / multi-version hosts where 'sandbox' isn't on PATH. Without SANDBOX_SOCKET propagation, the recursive 'sandbox proxy' invocation can't reach the same daemon socket the parent CLI was invoked against. ssh_config::ensure_session_entry also pre-creates ~/.ssh/sandbox/sockets/ (mode 0700) so the daemon-emitted ControlPath has its parent dir — OpenSSH creates the socket file but not the parent.
discoveries: M18-S6 PROOF POINT: tests/e2e/test_guest_agent.py::test_ssh_session[container] PASSES end-to-end under SANDBOX_HARNESS=sandbox-systemd (147s). CLI (operator uid) fetches ssh-config from daemon (sandbox uid), writes ~/.ssh/sandbox/sandbox-<id> + key, execs 'ssh sandbox-<id>' which tunnels through the daemon's /proxy WebSocket to the in-container sshd via the bind-mounted authorized_keys + synthetic /etc/passwd. Closes the cross-user CLI bug for the container backend. Lima backend remains blocked by todo #217 (daemon-spawned QEMU exit-1) — the CLI rewrite is correct but is never exercised on Lima because no Lima session can be created under the new harness.

Both rm and proxy cleanup use _at(home, id) testable seam — hermetic tests drive inner Result<()>-returning variants against tempdir, bypassing process::exit. 10 new hermetic unit tests (rm happy/daemon-failure/404, ls reconcile happy/silent-on-/home/olek.guest-unset/redirected-/home/olek.guest, proxy lazy-404 happy+key-removed/non-404-leaves-intact, _at helper direct, build_request dispatch bypass). 3 new container-backend E2E tests at tests/e2e/test_cli_lifecycle_hooks.py — all PASS under SANDBOX_HARNESS=sandbox-systemd. M18-S4 integration_proxy_websocket_round_trip_container_backend flagged as FLAKY (pre-existing race; container exits before sshd banner observed) — tracked as new todo for M18-S8 e2e-test-quality review track. Pre-existing fmt drift carved into separate style(cli) commit so the M18-S7 feature commit is focused. Operator-facing docs deferred to M18-S8/S9 per the original session brief.
decisions: M18-S7 testability pattern: rm and proxy lazy-cleanup paths use a '_at(home, id)' testable seam where the outer function reads /home/olek.guest via resolve_home() and the _at variant takes an explicit home Path. Outer wraps inner Result<()>-returning logic + process::exit; tests drive the inner _at variant directly against a tempdir, bypassing process::exit. Future cleanup-hook additions should follow this shape — the alternative (mutating /home/olek.guest with a serial mutex) works but is brittle when tests need their own scope.
discoveries: M18-S7 confirmed lifecycle hooks behave correctly end-to-end on container backend under SANDBOX_HARNESS=sandbox-systemd: rm cleanup (147s), ls reconcile after out-of-band DELETE (passes), ls --no-reconcile keeps stale entries (passes). Phase-1 test_ssh_session[container] still passes (177s) — no regression. New e2e file tests/e2e/test_cli_lifecycle_hooks.py with 3 container-backend tests. integration_proxy_websocket_round_trip_container_backend (the M18-S4 round-trip test) is FLAKY — container exits before sshd banner observation; passed on retry — track as M18-S8 e2e-test-quality review focus.

log.title: Spec-delivery verification: full e2e matrix + claim-to-code map
log.summary: Spec-delivery verification: claim-to-code map shipped at 613d2f0 (128 claims / 117 (a) shipped / 6 (b) out-of-scope / 5 (c) tracked-todo / 0 blockers). Full e2e matrix completed: 70 failed / 74 passed. Five root causes triaged in .tasks/handoffs/m18-s8-triage.md. Real architectural gap is Cause B — container starts as daemon uid 999 against image /home/sandbox owned by uid 1000, so interactive shells fail 'cd ~'. M18 cross-user contract is half-shipped without uid alignment between operator, runtime process, and in-runtime /home/olek.guest. Deep architectural Q&A with user concluded: do NOT defer this; the correct fix is the supervisor-fork-as-operator pattern via a dedicated sandbox-spawn-helper setcap CAP_SETUID+ep binary, mirroring sandbox-route-helper precedent. Daemon stays uncapped. M18 extended from 144 to 147 sessions: S10 (implement spawn-helper architecture: helper binary + daemon spawn paths + Lima cloud-init usermod + container --user operator + entrypoint chown + synthetic /etc/passwd with operator uid + Cause A fixture cleanup + Cause C limactl-as-sandbox test helper + spec amendment + full matrix re-run), S11 (review pass with explicit workspace-documentation review — confirm docs surface explains mapped-xattr semantics, spawn-helper privilege model, in-VM uid mapping, container --user uid handling, operator setup), S12 (rewrite delivery artifact to absorb S10/S11 outcomes before M18 closure). shared: 9p stays default cross-user — passthrough swap rejected since mapped-xattr behaves correctly once QEMU runs as operator uid. The (143/144 complete) figure adjusts to (144/147) on close — three sessions added below the current one to keep M18 in flight.
decisions: Plan changed: M18 extended by 3 sessions: S10 spawn-helper architecture (supervisor-fork-as-operator for QEMU cross-user 9p shared access — sandbox-spawn-helper setcap CAP_SETUID binary mirroring sandbox-route-helper precedent, daemon stays uncapped, container backend gets --user operator_uid + entrypoint chown, Lima gets cloud-init usermod for in-VM uid mapping, synthetic /etc/passwd per session), S11 review + workspace-docs pass (does the docs surface explain mapped-xattr semantics, single-user-only shared mode restriction if we go that route, spawn-helper privilege model, in-VM uid mapping, container --user uid handling, operator setup model), S12 rewrite delivery artifact to absorb S10/S11 outcomes before M18 closure (total sessions: 144 → 147)

M18 close path: supervisor-fork-as-operator pattern via a dedicated sandbox-spawn-helper setcap CAP_SETUID+ep binary mirroring the sandbox-route-helper precedent. Daemon stays uncapped (uid 999, no AmbientCapabilities). Per-session spawn: daemon execs helper with (operator_uid, runtime_argv); helper validates caller is sandbox-group member, validates operator_uid resolves to a local user, calls setresuid(operator_uid), drops capabilities (capset empty sets), execve's the runtime tool. Resulting QEMU/Docker invocation runs as operator. Drivers: (i) 9p shared mode needs QEMU at operator uid for host DAC checks AND for correct in-VM ownership via mapped-xattr (back-propagated host writes are operator-owned, not uid 999); (ii) daemon stays uncapped — privileged surface is ~50-100 line auditable binary; (iii) same helper covers Lima QEMU spawn and container backend cross-user staging. Container backend gets --user operator_uid:operator_gid + entrypoint chown -R; Lima cloud-init does usermod -u operator_uid sandbox + chown -R /home/agent. Synthetic /etc/passwd uses operator uid. shared: 9p stays default cross-user (no passthrough swap needed).
discoveries: Full e2e matrix outcome (M18-S9 verification): 70 failed / 74 passed. Five root causes identified. Cause A: hard-coded /home/agent ↔ /home/sandbox literals in test fixtures (~40 occurrences across 7 files) — fixture bug, not daemon regression. Verdict: A safer (zero race window); B probably viable per source but hinges on un-verifiable OpenSSH client behavior under transient IdentityFile EACCES with live mux. Two independent LIMA_HOMEs are fully independent Lima installs — this validates the user's per-user LIMA_HOME proposal: base in /var/lib/sandbox/.lima-base/ (daemon-owned), sessions in /var/lib/sandbox/.lima-<operator-uid>/ (operator-owned). ROOT CAUSE of cross-user Lima SSH hang (an S13 bug, commit b415d87): the per-operator LIMA_HOME setfacl (u:op:rwx,d:u:op:rwx) leaves a DEFAULT GROUP+OTHER ACL that propagates read bits into the operator SSH key _config/user, so it lands 0644 (-rw-r--r--+) regardless of umask. OpenSSH StrictKeyfileMode rejects the group/world-readable private key -> hostagent never authenticates -> 600s 'waiting for ssh' timeout -> base-image build fails. The 0f4eeab/3b3cf32 churn band-aided the same vector. Lead decision: fix at the ACL level in ensure_operator_lima_home (daemon/sandbox-core) — NOT cap_chown (spec Non-goal), NOT a timeout bump. Zero BOTH default-group and default-other in the ACL so files in the tree are operator-private 0600; operator access stays via the named-user default entry; daemon (dir owner, uid 999) and operator (named-user) both retain access, everyone else denied; daemon never reads the key directly (goes through helper). Keep helper umask 0o077 as defense-in-depth. Must be grounded in actual getfacl output + verified empirically (key 0600 op-owned, SSH up <600s) before the matrix.

Deeper root cause: OpenSSH ignores POSIX ACLs and reads st_mode. When _config/user inherits the default named-user ACL entry (default:user:op:rwx) from the per-operator LIMA_HOME, the kernel maintains an ACL MASK, and ls/stat show that mask in the GROUP bits. So the key reads 0640 (g+r) and ssh StrictKeyfileMode rejects it ('bad permissions') -> hostagent never auths -> 600s ssh-wait hang. Zeroing d:g::/d:o:: is insufficient while a named-user entry forces mask>=r. Fix direction: the operator OWNS everything it creates via the helper pivot (owner bits suffice); it only needs to TRAVERSE the daemon-created top dir. So use a NON-default u:op:rwx on the top LIMA_HOME dir for traversal and DROP the default named-user propagation (d:u:op), so child files (incl the SSH key) carry no named-user ACL, no mask, and land plain 0600. Verify no daemon-owned (uid 999) files live below the top dir that the operator must read; if any do, handle those narrowly. cap_chown remains a Non-goal; helper runs AS operator so it can chmod operator-owned files without it.

log.title: AgentBrokerExecutor and login-session execution routing
log.summary: Completed the operator-execution seam on macOS. GuestSocat hands the raw stream to the caller via a PrefixedStream that preserves bytes buffered after the StreamOpen frame, then the agent reconnects. Degenerate path: op_uid==daemon_uid (gateway infra + single-uid foreground dev) runs limactl directly with the SAME qemu-wrapper + hardening env the routed/agent handle_start path uses — review confirmed field-by-field, NO egress gap. Wire-protocol types moved to a macOS-gated sandbox-agent library the daemon depends on only on macOS; Linux stays on SetuidHelperExecutor unchanged (verified: full workspace builds on Linux, sandbox-core lima tests 97/97 green on Linux). log.title: socket_vmnet pool and the vmnet launchd daemon set
log.summary: Landed the macOS socket_vmnet pool + vmnet launchd daemon set — the isolated per-session L2 segments the macOS egress model depends on. Bring-up portability+prompt-friendliness fix (commit afeaf1f): BSD-install create-parents (GNU -D is unportable), a no-sudo idempotent fast-path (world-readable plist + launchctl print), dropped -k in the readiness wait, and a 60s vmnet.framework first-start wait. Independent reviews approved both rounds (Phase A: 2 blockers + 3 should-fixes all fixed; bring-up: Linux-path safety of the shared canonical-binary.sh confirmed). Verification: macOS hermetic 0 new failures (+8 tests); Linux invariance confirmed by container build (VmnetSlot/NetworkInfo compile unconditionally; pool is macOS-gated). ALL live exit criteria PROVEN on this host: 8 daemons up, slot-0..7.sock under /var/run/sandbox/vmnet/ all CONNECTED by an _sandbox member, /Library/sandboxd ancestry root-owned, integration_vmnet_inter_slot_l2_isolation PASS, positive ancestry assertion PASS, idempotent re-run issues no sudo, no networks.yaml ever written. The live L2-DATAPATH regression (ARP across distinct identifiers) was reviewed and legitimately deferred to M20-S6's egress E2E (no lighter mechanism before VMs boot at M20-S4); S1 ships the structural precondition. Follow-ups parked as todos #240 (CI cross-language UUID-equivalence guard) and #241 (sync spec VmnetPool struct to include session_count).
decisions: M20-S1 split into Phase A (delegate now, no sudo): VmnetPool + /29 allocation + NetworkInfo.vmnet_slot + io.sandboxd.vmnet.<n> plist generation + slot->socket map + daemon startup ancestry/ownership assertion logic + make setup-dev-env Darwin RECIPE + all pure-logic/fixture tests incl. the L2-isolation regression test code. Phase B (block for user): live bring-up via sudo (stage socket_vmnet to /Library/sandboxd, bootstrap launchd daemons) + executing the live inter-slot L2 isolation regression + live ancestry-assertion check — a system-package+sudo change the standing constraint says to block on. Phase B depends on Phase A's plists/recipe (sequential).

Accepted (after independent review): the live inter-slot L2 datapath regression (two slots, same-subnet ARP/datapath across distinct vmnet-network-identifiers must fail) is deferred from M20-S1 to M20-S6's egress E2E. No lighter mechanism is feasible at S1 — socket_vmnet's unix socket is QEMU's length-prefixed datagram framing (not a raw tap), needs the daemons bootstrapped + _sandbox membership + QEMU, and no sandbox VM boots until M20-S4. discoveries: macOS dev host state for the arc: socket_vmnet 1.2.2 installed via Homebrew (/opt/homebrew/Cellar/.../bin) but NOT staged to /Library/sandboxd nor launchd-activated; _sandbox group pre-exists as macOS system group GID 60 (Seatbelt/Sandbox framework) so no creation needed; /var/run/sandbox and /var/lib/sandboxd absent; Lima 2.1.2 (meets floor).
