VmnetPool is the macOS counterpart to the Linux SubnetAllocator (sandbox-core network.rs): claimed-slot HashSet + max_slots + session->(_slot,NetworkInfo) map, mirroring the established pattern. NetworkInfo gains vmnet_slot: Option<VmnetSlot> with serde(default) — NO DB migration (network_info persists as a single serialized blob, not discrete columns).

First real run of 'make setup-dev-env' on macOS surfaced a BSD-install portability bug: install-guest-prod (installs /usr/local/libexec/sandboxd/sandbox-guest) fails because macOS BSD 'install' has no GNU 'install -D' auto-create-parent; the target dir isn't created first. The Darwin bring-up (an M20-S1 deliverable) needs a portability + Linux-only-target-gating pass to run end-to-end on macOS. (Rust/cargo now installed on host by user, so cargo build steps work.)

Darwin setup-dev-env bring-up bug root cause: scripts/dev/canonical-binary.sh used 'install -D' (GNU: create-parents; BSD/macOS: DESTDIR prefix, does NOT create parents) so installing sandbox-guest to a non-existent /usr/local/libexec/sandboxd/ failed. Fix: 'sudo mkdir -p $(dirname)' + plain 'install' — portable + idempotent, Linux path unaffected. Audit: other Darwin targets already BSD-clean (stat -f, install -d, dscl/dseditgroup/launchctl); all Linux-only setcap/useradd/visudo steps correctly absent from the Darwin path.

Darwin 'make setup-dev-env' now completes clean + idempotent; all M20-S1 LIVE exit criteria pass on this host (8 io.sandboxd.vmnet daemons up, sockets slot-0..7.sock root:_sandbox srwxrwx--- under /var/run/sandbox/vmnet/ all CONNECTED by an _sandbox member, /Library/sandboxd ancestry root-owned, integration_vmnet_inter_slot_l2_isolation PASS, positive ancestry assertion PASS). Beyond the install -D fix, 3 more bring-up fixes were needed: socket-existence check must use 'sudo test -S' (the 0750 vmnet dir blocks non-_sandbox traversal so the bare check always returned false); vmnet.framework first-start needs a 60s (not 10s) wait; daemon-wait loop restructured. Uncommitted: scripts/dev/canonical-binary.sh + Makefile.

Passwordless sudo MASKS sudo-prompt-convention regressions: the bring-up's 'sudo -k test -S' (added to traverse the 0750 vmnet dir) ran silently here but would prompt a non-passwordless user on every poll iteration (up to 30x) and on the idempotent no-op path — violating the 'no-op => no prompt' convention. Lesson: verify prompt-friendliness by INSPECTING whether the no-op path invokes sudo at all, not by observing absence of a prompt on this (passwordless) host. canonical-binary.sh install -D fix confirmed Linux-safe by review.

log.title: Gateway Lima instance: template, lifecycle, NIC discovery, egress plumbing
log.summary: Landed the persistent, daemon-owned macOS gateway Lima instance — the only sanctioned egress uplink for every macOS session. Round 1 (cfff692): GatewayLimaManager generates the sandboxd-gateway Lima template (vmType qemu, N socket_vmnet NICs from the VmnetPool slot->socket map, forwarded Docker socket, provisioning = docker.io install + MTU-clamp/IPv6-disable/no-DHCP hardening), drives lifecycle (create/start + two-phase docker-info readiness), discovers limaN NICs by name (non-fatal count mismatch -> use discovered count; full resize deferred to M21-S3), ensures the shared sandboxd-egress NAT bridge, and applies the baseline default-drop egress nft on the management NIC. Daemon-owned -> all limactl via the degenerate direct path (no agent). Round 2 (acf4965): live-boot fixes (template written outside LIMA_HOME then removed, two-phase readiness widened for cloud-init, printf-over-heredoc netplan, UID>=500 docker-group, shared env-sanitization helpers, nft idempotency) AND the egress BLOCKER fix — the eth0 OUTPUT chain is now a tight port allow-list (DNS 53 + 443 + 80) with default-drop instead of a blanket ct-state-new accept, bounding the VM-host-namespace blast radius; re-originated container traffic flows via the untouched FORWARD chain (Docker NAT). PROVEN LIVE on this host: sandboxd-gateway boots, forwarded Docker socket reachable, limaN discovery works on real ip-json, sandboxd-egress created, policy applies idempotently; DNS+HTTPS work from the VM host-ns while a container still egresses via FORWARD; integration_gateway_lima 6/6 PASS. Both rounds reviewed (the live-boot review caught+fixed the egress over-relaxation, with a negative regression test added). Verified: macOS hermetic 0 new failures (gateway_lima unit tests + 6 integration), Linux invariant by construction (module fully macOS-gated). Deferred per spec: gateway-image docker-load (M22-S5), crash recovery (M21-S1), pool-resize rebuild (M21-S3); ensure_ready wiring into the live startup ordering is M20-S5. Durable macOS topology docs deferred to a consolidated arc-end pass (todo). NOTE: the live bring-up twice tripped the 600s subagent stream-watchdog on long silent ops — mitigated by timeout-wrapping every command + reusing the running VM.
decisions: M20-S2 design: new macOS-gated GatewayLimaManager (sandbox-core) owns the persistent daemon-owned 'sandboxd-gateway' Lima instance under the daemon LIMA_HOME — vmType qemu, N socket_vmnet NICs sourced from the VmnetPool slot->socket map, forwarded Docker socket at {{.Dir}}/gateway-docker.sock, provision installs docker.io from Ubuntu packages + MTU-clamp eth0=1280 + IPv6-disable + no-DHCP netplan. limactl ops route via the degenerate op_uid==daemon_uid run_limactl_direct path (daemon-owned, NO agent). NIC discovery: 'limactl shell ... ip -json link' maps limaN->slot (exclude eth0). Egress: idempotent 'sandboxd-egress' docker bridge + baseline default-drop eth0 nft (allow established/related re-originated + DNS; gateway VM is NEVER restrict=on). Resolved: NIC-count!=max_slots is NON-FATAL in S2 (log + use discovered count; full pool-resize=M21-S3); slot->NIC map cached in GatewayLimaManager. Implementing in 2 rounds: code+hermetic+integration-scaffold first (reviewed), then live gateway-VM bring-up (single-uid dev path) to satisfy the live exit criteria.

M20-S2 baseline eth0 egress nft policy reviewed SOUND: genuine default-drop, allows only established/related (re-originated upstream) + DNS, no blanket accept, gateway VM correctly never restrict=on — satisfies the spec MUST (the defense-in-depth egress bound for the shared gateway). Round 1 review: 0 blockers, 5 should-fixes being fixed (nft re-application idempotency missing delete-table; #[ignore] on integration tests vs the integration_ prefix convention; milestone tags in comments; docker cmds need env sanitization like run_limactl_direct; dedup run_gateway_shell env-sanitize).

M20-S2 live-boot review: BLOCKER — the baseline eth0 egress policy was over-relaxed during live bring-up to a blanket 'ct state new accept' on the OUTPUT chain (allows ALL new VM-host-namespace outbound), violating the spec MUST. Correct design (reviewer-confirmed): re-originated container traffic flows via the FORWARD chain (Docker NAT), so the OUTPUT chain is exactly the VM-host-namespace blast-radius surface and must be a TIGHT port allow-list (DNS 53 udp/tcp + 443/80 for registry/apt), default-drop — NOT blanket new-accept. Non-nft live-boot fixes (template path, two-phase readiness, env sanitization, printf-over-heredoc, idempotency) are sound. Fixing via a fresh developer (prior implementer stalled twice on the 600s stream watchdog).

M20-S2 egress BLOCKER fixed + LIVE-verified: baseline eth0 OUTPUT chain is now a tight port allow-list (DNS 53 udp/tcp + 443 + 80) with default-drop, no FORWARD chain (Docker NAT untouched), idempotent. Proven on the running sandboxd-gateway VM: policy applies, DNS resolves, HTTPS reaches upstream from the VM host-ns (allow-listed), a throwaway container still egresses via the FORWARD path, integration 6/6 pass. This satisfies the M20-S2 egress exit criterion (allow only re-originated + DNS/essentials, default-drop, bound the compromised-component blast radius, gateway never restrict=on) — live, not just structurally. Added a negative unit test (does_not_have_blanket_new_accept) to lock it in.
discoveries: Live gateway bring-up revealed the baseline eth0 nft policy is INCOMPLETE: it sets the FORWARD chain to policy=drop with NO ACCEPT for the re-originated forward path (sandboxd-egress bridge -> eth0), so Docker container traffic can't egress. Re-originated upstream from gateway components traverses the VM's FORWARD chain (bridge->eth0 + SNAT/MASQUERADE), not just OUTPUT — so the baseline must ACCEPT that forward path (and established/related return) while staying default-drop, AND must coexist with Docker's own iptables FORWARD/MASQUERADE rules. The static review approved the OUTPUT structure but the FORWARD/Docker-iptables interaction only surfaced on a live boot. (Round 2 dev stalled on a no-timeout command mid-debug at this finding; recovering.)

log.title: Sandbox VM template + the narrow restrict=on qemu-wrapper
log.summary: Landed the macOS sandbox VM template + the narrow restrict=on qemu-wrapper — per-VM egress enforcement at the QEMU/slirp layer (commit d202513). Wrapper: reuses the Linux in-place rewrite (splices restrict=on into the management 'user' netdev, preserves hostfwd, idempotent), genuinely FAIL-CLOSED (aborts on 0 or >1 user netdev or unconfirmed restrict=on; the only paths to exec qemu without restrict=on are the intentional provisioning bypass + Lima probe passthrough — confirmed by static review + present exit-1 guards). macOS deltas: firmware staging (share->/opt/homebrew/share symlink so Lima's qemu-dir-relative firmware resolution finds edk2), HVF-via-exec (execs the entitled Homebrew qemu), a marker file recording the rewritten netdev (fallback for M20-S6 post-boot QMP verification), no bridge NIC. Gated to sandbox VMs ONLY — never the gateway. Template: vmType qemu emitted EXPLICITLY (the headline BLOCKER — Lima defaults to VZ on macOS, which cannot attach socket_vmnet and would VOID egress; review caught the original omit-vmType design before any live boot), per-session socket_vmnet NIC + static-IP cloud-init (B+4 of the /29, route via B+3), 9p+securityModel, operator-uid-alignment (elided at default uid), seccomp/cgroup wrapper gated off, shared image-URL consts. The per-operator agent validator was STRENGTHENED to REQUIRE vmType==qemu (reject absent + vz + non-qemu) so a daemon-authored template can never silently fall back to VZ. Generated template round-trips through the validator; fixtures updated to real rendered output. Spec append-vs-rewrite wording corrected. Shape-only/hermetic (first live HVF boot is M20-S4, egress proof M20-S6). Review: 2 blockers (the vmType hole, same root cause) fixed. Independent full-hermetic verification via background bash (subagents repeatedly stalled on silent cargo runs at the 600s watchdog) caught 4 dev-MISLABELED test bugs (3 wrapper-test shell-string mismatches + 1 naive-grep template-shape test) — all fixed, production code was correct. Verified: macOS fmt/clippy clean, 11 known failures/0 new, Linux clippy -D warnings clean apart from the known statvfs #239.
decisions: M20-S3 design: the macOS sandbox-VM restrict=on qemu-wrapper REUSES the existing Linux in-place rewrite (lima.rs already splices restrict=on into the -netdev user, token, skipping any existing restrict=, idempotent — the spec's 'Linux only appends' wording is INACCURATE and gets corrected in-branch). Genuine macOS deltas: (a) firmware-path staging so Lima's qemu-dir-relative firmware resolution finds edk2-aarch64-code.fd (/opt/homebrew/share/qemu/...), (b) HVF-via-exec (wrapper execs the entitled Homebrew qemu; the com.apple.security.hypervisor entitlement is re-acquired across exec), (c) a marker file recording the rewritten netdev for M20-S6 FALLBACK verification (S6 prefers live QMP query-netdev), (d) no bridge NIC. Wrapper gated by INSTANCE KIND at the daemon call site — sandbox VMs pass --qemu-wrapper, the gateway never does. Template gen is largely platform-independent (qemu vmType already; add the socket_vmnet NIC + 9p securityModel; seccomp/cgroup wrapper gated off; operator-uid-alignment cloud-init elided at uid 1000). S3 is SHAPE-only/hermetic — first live HVF boot is M20-S4, egress proof is M20-S6. Exit also requires round-tripping the rendered template through M19-S4's validate_lima_yaml_shape and UPDATING its fixtures to the real output.

M20-S3 BLOCKER (core-promise): the macOS sandbox VM template omitted vmType, relying on a WRONG assumption (a stale M19-S4 validator comment claimed Lima defaults to qemu) — but Lima defaults to VZ on macOS, and VZ can't attach socket_vmnet, so a sandbox VM would boot under vz and VOID egress control. Coordinated fix: (1) change sandbox-agent validate_lima_yaml_shape from 'reject all vmType' to 'REQUIRE vmType==qemu' (reject vz AND absent) — this STRENGTHENS the egress invariant the agent enforces; (2) emit vmType: qemu in generate_template_macos; (3) update round-trip fixtures + the wrong comment. Every template flowing through the agent validator (sandbox session + base-image build if applicable) must emit vmType: qemu so the new requirement doesn't break another flow; the gateway bypasses the validator (unaffected). Also S1: extract the duplicated Ubuntu image URLs to shared consts. The wrapper itself is genuinely fail-closed (reviewer found no fail-open path); IP arithmetic + cross-platform safety confirmed sound. Caught at the shape stage before any live boot — exactly where it should be.

log.title: macOS session lifecycle (create/start/stop/rm) + vmnet_slot schema
log.summary: Wired the macOS session lifecycle end-to-end. Round 1 (906fb3a): building blocks — macos_session setup/teardown_macos_gateway (private macvlan + hardened two-NIC gateway container in the gateway VM via the forwarded Docker socket; deny-all->health->DNAT; idempotent reverse teardown + slot release), verify_restrict_on (FAILS CLOSED — a missing/wrong wrapper marker returns Err so the caller tears down + releases the slot + never marks Running), check_host_ip_forwarding_disabled; GatewayManager parameterized with an optional Docker socket (Linux byte-for-behavior unchanged); NetworkInfo.vmnet_slot DTO + sandbox-inspect rendering. Round 2 (b507570): hooked the create/start/stop/rm request handlers (cfg-gated macOS parallel paths, Linux unchanged) to the building blocks with the happens-before ordering (slot->persist->limactl create->gateway-before-VM->wrapped limactl start with SANDBOX_RESTRICT_MARKER injected->verify_restrict_on->mark Running; rollback+slot-release on any failure; start resumes on a fresh non-sticky slot via rewrite_vm_network_slot); the marker env is injected in run_limactl_direct; added a DirectLimaExecutor test harness (single-uid degenerate execution path) + 4 macOS-lifecycle integration tests. LIVE FINDING (captured forward): a full sandbox-VM boot is gated on two explicitly-deferred prerequisites — the macOS operator-LIMA_HOME path without Linux setfacl (#236/M21) and the gateway-image load into the gateway VM (M22-S5); discovered by running the live test. So the 2 no-prerequisite live tests (partial-create rollback, vmnet_slot accounting) PASS; the 2 boot/image-dependent tests guard-skip with clear messages until M20-S6's minimal-e2e bring-up provides those slices (todo #243). M20-S4's exit criteria are met WITHOUT a full live boot (they require slot accounting, naming, rollback-no-leak, vmnet_slot round-trip, gateway-container hardening assertions, inspect rendering, green suites, review, happens-before documented — the 'first HVF boot' was M20-S3's scope-note framing, now consolidated to M20-S6). Verified: macOS fmt/clippy(0 warn)/hermetic (11 known, 0 new), Linux clippy clean apart from #239, integration_macos suite 4 green. Reviews: R1 found 1 blocker (restrict-verify soft-warn -> made hard-err) + 4 should-fix (macvlan_mode=private, real hardening assertions, per-component health wait, container pre-cleanup) all fixed; my own verification caught an edition-2024 unsafe-extern, libc-in-test (->nix), 10 clippy warnings, and the prereq-gated tests. PROCESS NOTE: subagents repeatedly tripped the 600s stream watchdog on silent cargo runs — resolved by running ALL builds/tests via background bash + zero-cargo subagent edits.
decisions: M20-S4 design (2 rounds: code+hermetic, then first live HVF boot). Create/start/stop/rm mirror Linux but the macOS deltas are: claim a vmnet slot (not a /28); create the macvlan 'sandbox-net-<id>' INSIDE the gateway VM via its forwarded Docker socket with parent = the slot's limaN NIC (from GatewayLimaManager.nic_map); run the hardened gateway container 'sandbox-gw-<id>' in the gateway VM with two NICs (sandboxd-egress + the macvlan at B+3); deny-all -> health -> DNAT; wrapped 'limactl start' with  injected; then the restrict-verify gate; partial-create rollback releases the slot. HAPPENS-BEFORE (load-bearing): slot -> db -> macvlan -> gateway-container -> deny-all -> health -> DNAT -> [only now] VM start -> verify -> Running. NetworkInfo.vmnet_slot already exists (M20-S1); S4 adds the 'sandbox inspect' 3-line rendering. Restrict-verify gate: S4 wires the call + failure->teardown+release-slot; the check is marker-based-via-broker (or a flagged stub) at S4, upgraded to authoritative QMP at S6. Reuse gateway.rs create_gateway/inject_deny_all/inject_dnat + NetworkManager.create_network by PARAMETERIZING the Docker socket (forwarded socket on macOS). Assert gateway-container hardening (no --privileged, --read-only, exactly NET_ADMIN, no in-VM docker-socket mount) + net.inet.ip{,6}.forwarding==0 re-check at create. macvlan per-slot isolation = distinct limaN parent (verified live R2).

M20-S4 live first-HVF-boot is gated on TWO explicitly-deferred prerequisites, discovered by running the live test: (1) ensure_operator_lima_home uses Linux setfacl -> 'failed to spawn setfacl' on macOS = todo #236 (macOS per-operator LIMA_HOME port, deferred M21); (2) the gateway container needs the sandbox-gateway:<ver> image loaded into the gateway VM = deferred M22-S5 (gateway-image docker load). Neither is an M20-S4 bug. M20-S4's actual exit criteria do NOT require a full live boot (they require slot-accounting/naming/rollback/round-trip + hardening assertions + green suites + review — the 'first HVF boot' was M20-S3's scope-note framing). DECISION: M20-S4 delivers the complete create/start/stop/rm wiring + building blocks + the 2 no-prerequisite live tests (rollback + pool accounting PASS); the 2 prerequisite-blocked live tests (create_start_stop_rm, gateway_side_lifecycle) are GUARDED to skip-with-clear-message when their prerequisite is absent. The FULL live boot + egress proof consolidate at M20-S6, which is designed to bring up the minimal macOS e2e (incl. the minimal #236 + gateway-image slices). NOT pulling M21/M22-S5 forward into S4.
discoveries: M20-S4 R1 verified: hermetic 0 new failures (11 known), Linux clippy clean apart from #239, all 13 macos_session unit tests pass. The restrict-verify marker CHECK is already real (confirms restrict=on, errors on wrong content) — B1 is narrow: only the MISSING-marker branch is wrongly soft (warn+Ok), must become Err so the caller tears down + releases + does not mark Running. Fixing B1 + 4 should-fix (macvlan_mode=private; real gateway-hardening assertions; per-component wait_for_components made public; docker rm -f pre-cleanup) + 2 nit + 2 clippy (too_many_args on setup_macos_gateway; dead_code on macOS AppState vmnet_pool/gateway_lima_manager, consumed by the create-handler wiring next round).

log.title: macOS daemon startup sequence + reconcile
log.summary: Wired the macOS daemon startup sequence + reconcile (commit 4f66825). The 8-step boot (cfg-gated; Linux byte-unchanged): prereq checks — a HARD assertion that host IP forwarding is off on BOTH net.inet.ip.forwarding + net.inet6.ip6.forwarding (corrected the IPv6 key from the WRONG net.inet.ip6.forwarding which is unknown-oid on macOS; absent/unknown sysctl treated defensively as off, symmetric v4+v6), the staged socket_vmnet root-owned-ancestry assertion, the launchd vmnet slot sockets reachable; pool init; gateway ensure_ready (HARD FAIL — the only sanctioned egress uplink); session load; the TWO-HALVES reconcile; pool-state restore (restore_from_infos); accept. Reconcile split: 6a (remove gateway container+macvlan + RELEASE slot for every non-running session + orphaned containers) runs UNCONDITIONALLY — reclaims a logged-out operator's leftover state without waiting for re-login; 6b (VM-side liveness) runs only for operators whose agent is checked in (gated via connected_uids). Startup slot-leak release. #244 (IP-forwarding re-checked at create vs a runtime VPN flip) DONE. PROVEN LIVE: the daemon refuses to start with the actionable forwarding error when host IP-forwarding is on (integration test PASSES with forwarding flipped on; forwarding safely restored to 0). Reconcile-split + slot-leak release are unit-tested (review APPROVED); the full live daemon-start reconcile of a real stopped session shares M20-S4's deferred prereqs (#236 setfacl, gateway image), consolidated to M20-S6. Verified: macOS fmt/clippy-0/hermetic (1953 pass, 11 known, 0 new) + Linux clippy clean apart from #239. Review APPROVE (0 blockers). DISCOVERIES: IPv6-forwarding-sysctl key was a real egress-prereq correctness bug (fixed + spec corrected); users.conf IS legitimately needed on macOS (lite/container backend /28 allocation) — the daemon-start test fixture was wrong (schema_version->_schema_version, uid->username) + needed broker-socket/base-dir/XDG test seams to run as a non-_sandbox user. PROCESS: subagents kept stalling on silent cargo runs (a review too) — all builds/tests + the live forwarding-flip via background bash; subagents do edit-only.
decisions: M20-S5 design (mostly WIRING — restore_from_infos, ensure_ready, check_host_ip_forwarding_disabled all exist; M20-S5 calls them in the 8-step startup). Resolutions: (1) gateway ensure_ready failure at startup = HARD FAIL (mandatory egress infra); NIC-count mismatch within stays non-fatal (M21-S3). (2) Reconcile split: add AgentRegistry::is_agent_checked_in(uid)->bool; step 6a (gateway-side cleanup: remove gateway container+macvlan + RELEASE slot for every NON-running session + orphaned containers) runs UNCONDITIONALLY (no agent); step 6b (VM-side liveness reconcile) is AGENT-GATED on is_agent_checked_in. (3) Startup slot-leak release: stopped/nonexistent sessions hold no slot. (4) Pool restore via restore_from_infos(running sessions). (5) #244: call check_host_ip_forwarding_disabled at BOTH startup (hard assert, refuse-start with actionable error) AND create (re-check vs runtime VPN flip). TESTABILITY: unit-test the reconcile-split LOGIC with a constructed/mock is_agent_checked_in (6a unconditional; 6b gated) + slot-leak release + the prereq checks (incl. the corrected IPv6 sysctl); live daemon-start + the IP-forwarding-refuse test via background bash; full live cross-user 6b deferred (no agent on this single-uid host -> M20-S6+). Deferred per plan: live failure recovery (gateway-crash poll/agent respawn) M21-S1/S2; pool resize M21-S3.

M20-S5 review: APPROVE, 0 blockers. Reconcile split CONFIRMED correct (6a unconditional gateway-teardown + slot-release for every non-running session, zero agent dependency, no stranded logged-out-operator state; 6b agent-gated via connected_uids, cold-start no-op). IP-forwarding egress-prereq assertion sound (net.inet.ip.forwarding + net.inet6.ip6.forwarding, unknown-oid-as-off, startup hard-fail + create re-check #244). 2 should-fixes: (1) reviewer flagged connected_uids dead_code on Linux — NON-ISSUE, contradicted by the actual Linux clippy -D-warnings run (clean apart from #239; broker.rs is macOS-gated, not compiled on Linux); skipping. (2) IPv4 forwarding check lacks the empty/unknown-oid defensive treatment the IPv6 path has — minor asymmetry on the egress-prereq check; fixing for symmetry/robustness (one-line). Static gate v2 GREEN: fmt/build/clippy-0-warn/hermetic-11known-0new/Linux-clean-apart-from-#239.
discoveries: EGRESS-PREREQ BUG found in M20-S5 recon: check_host_ip_forwarding_disabled (and the spec) check 'net.inet.ip6.forwarding', which returns 'unknown oid' on macOS — the correct macOS IPv6-forwarding sysctl is 'net.inet6.ip6.forwarding' (inet6, not inet). So the IPv6 half of the egress-prereq assertion is currently broken (would error/refuse-start on the wrong key). Fix: use net.inet6.ip6.forwarding; treat an absent/unknown-oid sysctl defensively as off (0); correct the spec wording (git add -f). IPv4 key net.inet.ip.forwarding is correct (==0 on this host).

M20-S5 live IP-forwarding-refuse test FAILED (exit criterion not yet met): the daemon refused to start but on users.conf parsing ('unknown field schema_version, expected _schema_version') BEFORE reaching the IP-forwarding check. users.conf is the Linux per-uid /28-allocation config; macOS uses the vmnet pool + max_macos_sessions, so the macOS startup arguably should NOT require/validate users.conf at all. Either (a) the macOS startup is wrongly running the shared Linux users.conf validation -> cfg-gate it off on macOS (cleaner), or (b) macOS genuinely needs that config and the TEST FIXTURE just has a wrong field name (schema_version vs _schema_version). Symmetry fix itself verified green (fmt/clippy-0/15 scoped pass). Host forwarding flipped on->test->RESTORED to 0 safely.

M20-S5 daemon-start test progress: users.conf fixture fixed (daemon passes it now), but fails earlier at step 1 — binding /var/run/sandbox/broker.sock = Permission denied. /var/run/sandbox is _sandbox:_sandbox 0750, so a GROUP member (olek) can traverse but not WRITE; only the _sandbox USER (prod daemon) can create the socket. The test runs as olek. Need the M19-S3 SANDBOX_BROKER_SOCKET test-env-override seam (+ other prod-path seams: daemon base dir, etc.) pointed at temp paths, AND the integration run built with the test-env-override feature (bare 'cargo nextest --profile integration' omits it — per the standing remember-item). The broker bind (step 1) precedes the IP-forwarding check (step 2f), so the seam must let the daemon bind a temp broker socket to reach the forwarding check. NOTE: the IP-forwarding CHECK itself is already unit-tested green; this is about the end-to-end daemon-start test's environment.

So I will: (1) implement everything; (2) PROVE the egress regression LIVE on this Apple-Silicon dev host (boot a real sandbox VM, delete the gateway default route, confirm slirp eth0 still can't egress — the core promise); (3) land the build-macos CI-lane YAML so the literal 'in CI' confirmation runs on the user's push; (4) the post-boot restrict-verify negative test + the hardening review locally. CORE PROMISE PROVEN LIVE on Apple-Silicon macOS. On a real booted sandbox VM (HVF-accelerated, restrict=on confirmed on eth0 in the qemu cmdline + marker; gateway VM correctly NOT restricted), as ROOT in the guest I deleted the gateway default route and forced default via the slirp eth0 (192.168.5.2). discoveries: M20-S6 D1 architecture: QMP-preferred restrict=on verification lives in the agent (handler.rs query_restrict_on_via_qmp), reached via a new LimaOp::RestrictOnVerify executor seam. A new GatewayLimaManager-style verify_restrict_on METHOD (lima.rs) supersedes the old macos_session.rs marker-stub free function; main.rs create+start flows now call manager.verify_restrict_on and rollback on failure (old stub import removed, stub+its tests now dead). QMP semantics: Ok(Some)=confirmed, Ok(None)=QMP unavailable→marker fallback, Err=QMP reachable but restrict unconfirmed. Marker is fallback ONLY (operator-owned; threat model is guest-adversary, not malicious operator, so marker fallback is acceptable).

Todo 238 recharacterized: the two event-ingest tests (deny_logger_jsonl_appears_on_bus, ingest_traffic_events_stamp_session_and_reach_bus) fail CONSISTENTLY on macOS in true isolation (both timeout no-event-within-5s), not just under parallel load as previously thought. Root cause: SessionIngestor uses an inotify-based file watcher (Linux primitive); on macOS the watcher does not deliver the appended JSONL within the deadline. deny_logger_jsonl_appears_on_bus is also misclassified (no integration_ prefix so it runs in the hermetic default profile). Pre-existing, unrelated to M20-S6 (event-ingestion code untouched). Proper fix (macOS watcher path or reclassify) belongs in a test-hygiene/macOS session, not the egress milestone.

LIVE first-light: daemon full 8-step macOS startup works end-to-end and is listening. Proven LIVE: D3 gateway image load from staged tarball (sandbox-gateway:0.1.10 loaded into gateway VM); D2 per-operator LIMA_HOME provisioned on macOS with no setfacl; socket_vmnet ancestry assertion; all 8 vmnet slot sockets reachable; gateway eth0 baseline nft applied. Pre-existing sandboxd-gateway instance has only 2 NICs (created earlier with fewer slots) vs max_slots 8 - non-fatal, enough for one session.

LIVE first-light BLOCKER: the gateway image cannot run on arm64. networking/gateway/Dockerfile line 104 hardcodes the mitmproxy download to linux-x86_64 (and ARG TARGETARCH=amd64), so mitmdump is an amd64 binary that fails with Exec-format-error inside the arm64 gateway Lima VM. The entrypoint then loops retrying mitmproxy and never starts Envoy, so session create fails at the gateway health gate. Everything else in the image is multi-arch (Envoy official image, CoreDNS golang build, nft-loggers rust build, debian base). Fix: derive the mitmproxy arch from TARGETARCH (amd64 to x86_64, arm64 to aarch64). This is a prerequisite for the macOS full backend to boot at all.

LIVE blocker 3 (macOS gateway Envoy never starts): arm64 mitmproxy now runs, but the entrypoint then waits for the Envoy LISTENER file (/etc/envoy/listeners/listener.yaml) which setup_macos_gateway never seeds. The Linux path seeds the initial deny-all listener (PolicyCompiler::compile_initial_envoy_listener) via a bind-mounted host dir; on macOS bind-mounts into the gateway VM are unavailable (build_macos_gateway_docker_args has an explicit REVISIT-in-M20-S6 marker). setup_macos_gateway DOES write the bootstrap via docker exec but omits the listener. Fix: seed the initial listener into the container via docker exec (mirror the bootstrap write) using LISTENER_FILE_IN_CONTAINER. Dynamic LDS policy updates on macOS (AtomicListenerWriter uses the host bind-mount) remain a separate follow-up.

LIVE findings 4+5 (reconcile/rollback): (4) macOS create rollback leaves a SESSION RECORD in sessions.db (not just the VM) when create fails after the record is written. (5) On daemon restart, the macOS reconcile/restore validates the leaked lima sessions vmnet-slot subnet 10.209.128.0/29 (correct vmnet base 10.209.128.0/24) against base range 10.209.0.0/24 (the users.conf lite subnet) and ABORTS startup with a not-a-valid-block error. So a single leaked lima session record bricks daemon startup. The restore path is using the wrong base (lite users.conf subnet) to validate vmnet slots. Pre-existing M20-S4 (rollback store-record) + M20-S5 (reconcile base) bugs surfaced by first-light. Workaround for the proof: clear sessions.db (no real sessions).

LIVE finding 6 root cause: macOS sandbox VM first-boot exceeds Lima 5-min limactl-start timeout because systemd-networkd-wait-online blocks ~2min (full default timeout) waiting for the restricted eth0 (and lima0) to reach routable/online (snapd.seeded 40s + pollinate 10s add more). VM boots fine (HVF confirmed, accel=hvf) and reaches Running AFTER the timeout, so create times out and rolls back. Fix: mark eth0 and lima0 optional:true in the macOS template netplan so networkd-wait-online does not gate boot (does NOT change addressing/restrict/MTU). M20-S3 template gap. The other 3 first-light bugs (rollback VM leak, rollback session-record leak, reconcile vmnet-base brick) are failure-path robustness - deferred as follow-ups; none compromise egress.

log.title: Gateway and socket_vmnet failure handling
log.summary: M21-S1 gateway and socket_vmnet failure handling complete. Implemented the gateway-Lima crash recovery story: GatewayLimaManager recovery primitives (probe_docker_health, force_stop_instance, restart_instance_for_recovery with a 90s readiness budget that re-establishes the egress fabric), a 10s gateway_lima_monitor triggering after 3 consecutive failed probes, and an idempotent recover_gateway_lima orchestrator that tags sessions Degraded then Recovering, force-restarts the gateway instance, and re-creates each per-session gateway container in bounded parallel - marking only sessions that fail recovery as Error while others continue, and never restarting a sandbox VM. Added a transient networking_status DTO field (in-memory only, no migration), a gateway_recovering latch so the per-session monitor stands down during whole-instance recovery, a macOS-aware per-session gateway_monitor behind a gateway_for_probes accessor (Linux byte-identical), and broker-checkin-driven runtime slot-leak reclamation via reconcile_operator_vms. Absorbed deferred items 247 (rollback now deletes the VM and the session record) and 248 (reconcile restore partitions macOS vmnet rows away from the lite subnet allocator that was bricking startup). Verified on macOS and Linux (clippy -D warnings); hermetic suite 1962 passed with only 3 known pre-existing environmental failures. Code review APPROVED, 0 blockers; minor findings polished in-session. Tests: integration recovery-primitive plus hermetic slot-reclamation, plus macos-marked e2e orchestrator tests. Commits 1a83cbd, 8c9791f, 5a4bc98, e911577. Tracked follow-ups: orchestrator state machine is e2e-only (253), live e2e gated on first-boot-timeout (249), e2e harness model needs macOS verification (254).
decisions: networking_status is a transient health field living only on SessionDto plus an in-memory AppState map (HashMap SessionId to status); never persisted, no SQLite migration. It is a session-level field parallel to gateway_status, NOT a field on SessionNetworkInfo.

Gateway-crash recovery never restarts a sandbox VM; it only re-creates the per-session gateway container over the forwarded gateway-Lima docker socket. This keeps recovery independent of operator-agent availability and works for logged-out operators. Review must assert no limactl start of a sandbox VM on the recovery path.

Two monitors coexist: a new gateway-Lima instance monitor (10s) and the existing per-session gateway monitor (30s). Instance-monitor-wins: a daemon-wide gateway-recovering flag (like sessions_stopping) gates the per-session monitor so it does not thrash per-session re-creates while the whole instance is down.

M21-S1 absorbs todos 247 (rollback VM-delete plus record cleanup) and 248 (reconcile restore validating macOS vmnet slots against the lite-pool base, which bricks startup). Deferred: 249 (first-boot timeout, template concern, may gate live macOS e2e so sequence first if needed) and 246 (macOS event-ingest watcher portability). CLI/doctor/diagnostics rendering of networking_status is explicitly M21-S5 per the milestone plan.

Broker check-in to slot-reclaim wiring uses a non-blocking try_send over a capacity-32 mpsc channel (on_admit_tx) feeding a task that calls reconcile_operator_vms. Best-effort: a full channel drops the trigger, which is fine since startup reconcile and the next check-in re-cover. Avoids blocking the broker admit loop on a slow reconcile.

recover_gateway_lima and the monitors live in main.rs (bin crate), unreachable from sandbox-core test harness, so the orchestrator state machine is only e2e-validated (gated on 249). Exit criteria accept e2e coverage + review, so this is acceptable for M21-S1. Hermetic orchestrator testing would require extracting the core loop into sandbox-core with injectable deps; tracked as a follow-up, not blocking.
discoveries: The per-session gateway_monitor in main.rs is spawned cross-platform but is Linux-only in behavior: it uses state.gateway (system docker socket) and state.network (SubnetAllocator) with zero cfg branches, so on macOS it targets the wrong socket. Making it macOS-aware via an AppState gateway_for_probes accessor is part of this session.

Todo 248 brick root cause: main.rs startup calls network.restore_from_infos over ALL persisted network rows including macOS lima slots, and SubnetAllocator validates each subnet against the users.conf lite base, so a 10.209.128.x/29 vmnet slot fails block validation and aborts daemon startup. Fix: cfg-gated partition so only vmnet_slot.is_none rows go to the lite restorer; VmnetPool.restore_from_infos (correct base) owns the slot rows.

Pass 1 regressed the hermetic test test_update_state_reconcile_caller_whitelist. M20 baseline had exactly 3 known hermetic failures (237 BSD-tar peek_manifest, 238 deny_logger and ingest_traffic event-infra). The 4th failure is new, almost certainly from extracting reconcile_operator_vms (a new caller of update_state_reconcile) or the rollback delete_session change. Sub-agent mischaracterized it as pre-existing. Fixing root cause before accepting Pass 1; must preserve the caller-whitelist security intent.

The update_state_reconcile allow-list scanner finds the nearest enclosing fn by scanning backward for the fn keyword, so an inline RAII Drop guard near an update_state_reconcile call gets mis-attributed to fn drop. Keep such guard structs at module scope. Relevant whenever adding callers.

log.title: Per-operator agent failure modes and fast user switching
log.summary: M21-S2 per-operator agent failure modes and fast user switching complete. Found most spec in-scope behavior already implemented (M19/M20/M21-S1): generation-guarded last-writer-wins eviction, 60s agent-initiated heartbeat liveness, actionable agent-unavailable error, full lite-mode bypass, on_admit-to-reconcile_operator_vms wiring; guest transport re-establishes passively (fresh-per-RPC) and the SSH proxy does not ride the broker. Genuine new work was small: fixed a race where the broker fired the check-in reconcile trigger before registering the new connection (now register-then-notify, so reconcile never observes a being-evicted connection); split reconcile dead-VM handling by trigger so a fresh-check-in/login-scoped dead VM is marked Stopped/resumable while startup keeps Error (spec line 919); added a heartbeat-timeout test seam; documented the login-scoped lifetime at the reconcile site. Audited and confirmed agent-initiated-only heartbeat, last-writer-wins within the peercred trust domain, and kernel-level guest-stream sever on eviction. Tests: mandatory multi-uid no-cross-operator-leakage, eviction severing the prior guest stream, switched-away-not-failed, agent-absent error contract, heartbeat-drop detection. Verified macOS (build/clippy/nextest 1966 passed) and Linux (clippy -D warnings); broker integration tests pass. Code review APPROVED; interim security review PASSED on all five eviction/stale-uid/last-writer-wins/isolation/cross-operator-reconcile paths.
decisions: D1 (real race from M21-S1): broker fires on_admit try_send BEFORE registry.register, so the per-checkin reconcile can observe a being-evicted connection. Fix: move the on_admit send to AFTER register.

D2 (spec vs code): agent-crash reconcile currently marks dead VMs Error, but spec says stopped/resumable for the login-scoped/crash case. Decision: split reconcile_operator_vms by call-site - fresh-check-in/login-scoped marks dead VMs Stopped (resumable per spec), startup 6b keeps Error (unchanged). Implementer must verify against exact spec wording and CLARIFY if it differs.

M21-S2 confirmations: D3 accept agent-initiated-only heartbeat (no daemon PING); D4 last-writer-wins exactly as spec'd, no prefer-genuine-agent tie-break (same-uid = same trust domain); D5 GuestSocat severed-then-reconnected satisfied passively (fresh-per-RPC + generation-guard eviction), security review verifies no in-flight stream survives eviction; D6 hermetic broker tests via test feature incl mandatory multi-uid isolation driving the registry directly, reconcile/switched-away wiring e2e-only/opportunistic; R3 add a test seam for the 60s heartbeat timeout.
discoveries: M21-S2 is largely already implemented in landed code (M19/M20 + M21-S1): broker last-writer-wins eviction (generation-counter guarded), 60s heartbeat liveness, actionable agent-unavailable error, full lite-mode bypass, on_admit to reconcile_operator_vms wiring, and passive fresh-per-RPC guest transport. The SSH proxy does not ride the broker. Genuine new code is small: the D1 race fix, the D2 state-split, an R3 heartbeat test seam, plus tests and the interim security review. Guard against over-building.

Verification footgun: the integration broker tests set SANDBOX_BROKER_TEST_HEARTBEAT_MS themselves (in-test set_var). Do NOT export that env globally when running the broker tests - a global 100ms heartbeat forces eviction mid-test on integration_eviction_severs_guest_socat and panics with BrokenPipe. Run the broker integration tests with no global heartbeat env; each manages its own.

log.title: Pool resize handling
log.summary: M21-S3 pool resize handling complete. Made the daemon the single authority on a config-vs-actual gateway NIC-count mismatch via a pure decide_pool_resize function (4 arms: NoChange, WarnRunningSessions, RefuseNeedsPrivilegedRegen, Rebuild) in sandbox-core, exhaustively unit-tested (20 hermetic tests across decision arms + daemon-set observation). Wired pool size to SANDBOX_MAX_MACOS_SESSIONS (1..=32, default 8); reordered startup so effective_n is derived before VmnetPool is sized; added idempotent delete_instance for stop-delete-recreate rebuild; made NIC discovery defer to the handler rather than hard-fail. Always-start guarantee upheld (non-rebuild arms keep the gateway; rebuild only when no sessions + daemon set matches N; no existing hard-fail softened). Daemon observes the root-owned socket_vmnet daemon set without privilege (plist + live-socket counts). Verified macOS (build/clippy/nextest 1986 passed, +20 new tests, only 3 known pre-existing failures) and Linux (clippy -D warnings). Code review APPROVED, 0 blockers; polish applied (conditional resize guidance, observe doc, removed plan-label comments, manual_range_contains clippy fix). Live rebuild-execution integration/e2e deferred to M22-S2 (needs sudo vmnet regen); decision authority hermetically tested.
decisions: M21-S3 decisions D1-D3: D1 wire max_macos_sessions via env SANDBOX_MAX_MACOS_SESSIONS default 8 (mirrors SANDBOX_BASE_VM_NAME; production sets it in the daemon launchd plist next to the vmnet daemon set). D2 derive effective_n from the resize decision EARLY (config-N + discovered gateway NIC count + daemon-set-N + running-count from store) and size VmnetPool to effective_n - reorder startup accordingly. D3 daemon-set-matches-N = N world-readable plists present AND N slot-sockets live (both).

M21-S3 decisions D4/O1/O2: D4 the always-start guarantee is met by the non-rebuild arms (no-op/warn/refuse keep the gateway intact); rebuild attempted only when safe (no sessions + daemon-set==N); on rebuild failure follow EXISTING gateway-failure behavior, do NOT add new degradation semantics this session (out of scope, adjacent to M21-S1) - just confirm no mismatch arm aborts startup. O1 add idempotent delete_instance() to GatewayLimaManager for stop-delete-recreate. O2 warn/refuse guidance references make setup-dev-env DARWIN_VMNET_SLOTS=N as the current privileged vmnet pool setup; M22-S2 installer supersedes.

M21-S3 test coverage: the 4 exit-criteria behaviors (rebuild-when-safe, warn-with-running-sessions, refuse-when-daemon-set-mismatch, always-start) are covered hermetically at the decision-authority level via decide_pool_resize unit tests. The LIVE rebuild execution (delete+recreate gateway) is bin-crate wiring + needs the M22-S2 sudo vmnet regen, so true end-to-end rebuild tests are gated on M22-S2 - consistent with the hermetic-core + gated-e2e pattern from M21-S1/S2.
discoveries: M21-S3 mostly restructuring: the spec's warn-and-continue NIC-mismatch behavior already exists inline in GatewayLimaManager ensure_ready and is already non-fatal (daemon already starts on mismatch today). New work: a pure decide_pool_resize predicate in sandbox-core (4 arms: NoChange, WarnRunningSessions, RefuseNeedsPrivilegedRegen, Rebuild), wiring config-N, a startup reorder, delete_instance, and the rebuild/refuse arms. max_macos_sessions is currently a hardcoded 8 (DEFAULT_MAX_MACOS_SESSIONS), not config-wired.

log.title: Lite-mode container backend on macOS
log.summary: macOS lite (container) backend live first-light COMPLETE. test_lite_macos.py = 8 passed / 1 skipped (local:, deferred to S6) on a FRESH gateway VM with zero manual patches; core promise (absolute egress block) proven live (direct-IP + DNS egress all blocked, route via per-session gateway). Live first-light found+fixed ~14 bugs across the lite path, all committed (aece2f8): create-dispatch order (macOS Container early-return moved above generic host network/CA/VM setup); per-session CA+SSH staged into the gateway VM (limactl copy to /tmp/sandbox-lite/<id>, bound from VM paths) + image-baked arm64 guest (skip host overlay); gateway mitmproxy-CA written via write_file_to_gateway_container (was ignored); restart-path gateway recreate via setup_macos_lite_gateway; container resources clamped to the gateway VM (2cpu/1536MiB); socket-awareness sweep (delete_network_on_socket, sshd-probe, SSH proxy, local-rsync, gateway-status all -H on macOS); gateway template fixes (docker.socket.d SocketMode=0666 drop-in — fixed ensure_ready 300s docker-forward timeout; route-helper temp-copy+sudo-install; 9p top-level mountType); lite-image baked with a linux/aarch64 sandbox-guest cross-build (Makefile build-guest-linux-aarch64; Darwin host build was a Mach-O -> Exec format error); local: push wired into create_session_macos_lite. e2e harness (#254 substantially resolved for lite): conftest macOS-import-safe + autouse fixtures no longer force the cross-user-daemon skip; test file fixed to the real CLI contract (inspect=JSON array, lowercase states, ps-parse). Verification GREEN: macOS suite 8/1 fresh, Linux clippy 1.88.0 --workspace -D clean (canonical gate; only colima binary-LINK OOMs, known), macOS clippy clean, fmt clean. DEFERRED to new M21-S6: egress allow-policy + DNS distribution (host-docker-bound on macOS, milestone-sized; only deny-all works), local: under openrsync, --repo/--boot-cmd, full-backend gateway-CA+restore socket-awareness, Makefile stage-uid #260. Toolchain note: default cargo=Homebrew 1.96; pinned/e2e-fixture=rustup 1.88.0 — use rustup for macOS builds.
decisions: M21-S4 decisions D1-D5: D1a gateway VM provisioning installs the cap'd sandbox-route-helper (mirror host install) - this session owns it, implementer checks if already present. D1b degenerate single-VM-user route-helper gate inside the gateway VM; helper acts per-session on the container netns by PID; operator isolation stays at container/session level; CLARIFY if VM model differs. D2 new create_session_macos_lite branch. D3 additive ContainerRuntime::with_macos_socket (Linux byte-identical). D5 reuse NetworkManager allocator with socket-aware docker emit.

M21-S4 decisions D6-D8: D6 (correctness) EXTEND pool restore to re-count lite sessions toward session_count, else the pool over-admits after a daemon restart. D7 add SANDBOX_LITE_SHARED_ROOT env knob for the install-time 9p mounts root; validate per-session shared: paths are under it; wire the stanza into generate_template_macos. D8 pure host-to-VM path translation function, hermetically tested. 241: spec VmnetPool struct snippet is stale, impl authoritative (session_count + lite tokens already present) - low-priority spec doc-fix only.

M21-S4 live-E2E harness model RESOLVED (todo 254/259): use the OPERATOR single-uid model — daemon_lima_home = /var/lib/sandboxd/501/501/lima (operator_lima_home(getuid)), reuse the operator-owned sandboxd-gateway, NOT a sandbox-test cross-user daemon (heavyweight macOS system change overlapping M22-S8). De-risk with a manual sandbox-CLI first-light before pytest. The running gateway VM predates the new lite template (no 9p mounts stanza, no /etc/sudoers.d/sandbox-route-helper, no route-helper, no lite image in-VM) and ensure_ready REUSES a Running instance as-is (never re-provisions), so the gateway VM must be DELETED + recreated by the daemon to pick up the new template — the same migration concern real upgraders hit.

M21-S4 macOS lite file-provisioning MECHANISM decided = VM-staged single-file binds (NOT docker cp). Spiked in the live gateway VM: docker cp to a --read-only container rootfs path FAILS ('container rootfs is marked read-only'), and cp to /run tmpfs ALSO fails (container runs as non-root --user, /run is root-owned, can't mkdir). The container runs as --user <operator-uid> (container.rs effective_container_user) so the synthetic /etc/passwd+/etc/group are REQUIRED (can't skip). Binds are the only mechanism that works with --read-only + non-root user + single-file targets (and matches Linux byte-for-byte). Design: stage cert.pem + ssh{authorized_keys,passwd,group} into a per-session OPERATOR-WRITABLE VM dir (limactl copy into the Lima user's home; root-in-VM reads it for the bind), bind each :ro to its Linux dst; SKIP the guest -v overlay (image-baked, version-matched); write the gateway mitmproxy CA pair via write_file_to_gateway_container (fix the ignored _ca_dir). Cleanup the per-session VM dir on delete.

M21-S4 CORE PROMISE PROVEN LIVE on the macOS LITE backend (first-light headline). A lite session reached Running with the guest agent connected; the in-VM sandbox-route-helper correctly repointed the container default route at the per-session gateway (default via 10.209.0.34), resolv.conf points at the gateway, and ALL egress is BLOCKED by the deny-all gateway: direct-IP HTTP 1.1.1.1:80 and HTTPS 8.8.8.8:443 both 'Couldn't connect to server', DNS example.com 'Could not resolve host'. Gateway container Up(healthy). 'sandbox exec' works (guest-agent transport socket-aware). This validates the lite-on-macOS data plane end to end (after fixing: dispatch order, gateway socket/route-helper/9p template, CA+SSH VM file-staging, gateway mitmproxy CA, and the arm64 guest cross-build for the lite image).

M21-S4 scope decision: 3 further gaps found by first-light. (G1) create_session_macos_lite returns after mark-Running with NO post-Running provisioning, so local: rsync (and --repo clone, initial --policy) is never invoked -> e2e test 8 (local:) fails. Will FIX G1 (wire local: workspace push) to pass the suite. (G2) policy distribution + DNS propagation are NOT socket-aware on macOS lite (PolicyDistributor::distribute uses host docker + host listener path; dns_propagation/lds_ack use host docker) -> initial deny-all + DNS works (core promise holds) but applying USER --policy/preset + live DNS-domain reconciliation do NOT work on macOS lite. This is a milestone-sized subsystem refactor NOT exercised by test_lite_macos.py -> DEFER to a dedicated new session (replan), with the core deny-all egress promise proven. (G3) macOS Lima full-backend restore_session_networking still uses host socket -> full-backend track, separate.

M21-S4 DEFER local: workspace (test 8) to the macOS-lite-usability follow-up. Two real macOS issues: (1) the host rsync is Apple openrsync (protocol 29) which lacks --mkpath (rsync>=3.2.3) that the create-time push uses (mkpath=true) -> fix = mkdir-then-rsync (no --mkpath) on macOS, OR require GNU rsync; this likely also affects 'sandbox sync'/cp on macOS. (2) guest_path defaulted to the HOST path (/var/folders/..), not /home/sandbox/workspace/ — documented default (local:<host>[:<guest>], guest defaults to host) so test 8's /home/sandbox/workspace expectation is also off. Skip test 8 with a tracked reason; fix helpers for tests 1-7,9. Coherent deferred chunk with G2 (policy/DNS) + repo/boot-cmd = the macOS-lite-usability layer (replan).

M21-S4 EXIT CRITERION MET: test_lite_macos.py live E2E first-light = 8 passed, 1 skipped (local:, deferred). Passing: create-reaches-running, no-vmnet-slot, stop-and-restart (FIX2 gateway-recreate), remove (FIX3a delete_network_on_socket), denied-egress-blocked (CORE PROMISE), ssh-access-over-forwarded-socket (exec), mixed-lima-and-lite-pool-accounting (ps-parse), shared-workspace-tcc (lenient). The first-ever lite-on-macOS data plane is proven end-to-end against a real daemon+gateway VM. Template fixes confirmed live on fresh create: docker-socket drop-in (/var/run/docker.sock 0666, forward up, ensure_ready passed — no 300s timeout), 9p top-level mountType (/tmp/sandbox-shared mounted type 9p), route-helper temp-copy+install (create/egress tests pass). macOS lite data plane = DONE end-to-end from clean install.

Adding M21-S6 to complete it (after S5 M13/M14/M17 integration). (total sessions: 180 → 181)
discoveries: M21-S4 lite-on-macOS is mostly wiring of built components (VmnetPool session_count + lite tokens, GatewayManager::with_gateway_socket + docker_cmd -H, ensure_egress_bridge, two-NIC gateway args, setup/teardown_macos_gateway, gateway_docker_socket all exist). Net-new: ContainerRuntime socket/home-awareness, an internal Docker bridge inside the gateway VM, running sandbox-route-helper INSIDE the gateway VM (the central net-new piece), a macOS branch in the container-create handler (currently not cfg-gated, broken on macOS), and an install-time 9p mounts stanza on the gateway template. Lite avoids the sandbox-VM boot so its live E2E is NOT blocked by 249 - should be runnable on this host.

Prerequisite pass caught a real Pass B bug (todo-3 verify): macOS stop_session for Container released the lite token but start_session never re-claims it, so every stop-start cycle decremented the pool counter without incrementing = over-admission. Fixed by mirroring Linux (token retained across stop; only remove releases) + 2 regression tests. Also landed: clippy uninlined_format_args fix, Makefile build/stage-route-helper-linux-aarch64 targets wired into setup-dev-env, and the gateway-VM /etc/sudoers.d/sandbox-route-helper NOPASSWD provision (scoped to the one binary; existing gateway VMs need re-provisioning).

M21-S4 review NEEDS CHANGES: security PASS (route-helper --vm-gateway-mode gate sound, sudoers scoped, isolation + fail-closed confirmed) but 3 BLOCKERS in the macOS lite RESTART path (start_session falls through to generic Linux): B1 restore_session_networking_lite uses host GatewayManager not forwarded-socket; B2 start_session has no macOS Container early-return so the in-VM route-helper is never reinvoked = egress bypass after stop/start (core-promise); B3 ensure_network targets host Docker not the gateway VM. Fix = a dedicated macOS lite start path mirroring create_session_macos_lite. Plus I1 Makefile :ro, I2 getcap probe, I3 audit comment.

M21-S4 functional gap found pre-live-E2E: ensure_image (main.rs:1939, runs before the macOS lite early-return at 2163) builds/ensures the lite image in the HOST Docker via docker_home (no socket param), but create_session_macos_lite runs the lite container via the forwarded gateway-VM socket where sandboxd-lite is absent - so a macOS lite create would fail with no-such-image. Review missed it (focused on restart-path + egress). The live E2E first-light will likely surface more (first-ever lite-on-macOS boot).

The e2e daemon's gateway VM + artifact-staging paths live under the sandbox-test daemon uid - NOT the currently-running operator-501 gateway VM, and NOT _sandbox uid 60 (which the Makefile stage targets use). So running test_lite_macos.py live first requires resolving the macOS e2e harness model (todo 254: daemon user, gateway VM path, artifact staging to the daemon LIMA_HOME) + bringing up a gateway VM with the new template in that home - a substantial prerequisite overlapping M22-S8 install-e2e - before any first-light debugging of the lite path itself.

M21-S4 live-E2E env facts: (1) conftest.py is Linux-only and CRASHES AT IMPORT on macOS via pwd.getpwnam('sandbox-test') — aborts pytest collection of the whole dir, so conftest must be made macOS-import-safe before any pytest run (test_lite_macos.py bypasses conftest fixtures: bare 'sandbox' + ambient socket; needs sandbox on PATH + SANDBOX_SOCKET). (2) Built artifacts exist (aarch64 route-helper, host sandboxd-lite:0.1.10) but NOT staged at operator daemon_lima_home; Makefile stage-* targets stage to WRONG path /var/lib/sandboxd/60/60/lima (uid from _sandbox=60, not actual daemon uid) — todo 260. (3) No sandboxd daemon currently running.

M21-S4 conftest made macOS-import-safe: module-level pwd.getpwnam('sandbox-test') guarded (try/except KeyError -> _SANDBOX_TEST_UID=None); a single lazy pytest.skip at the top of _launch_daemon_as_sandbox_via_sudo (the chokepoint all cross-user fixtures + autouse _ensure_base_image/_dump_daemon_log_on_failure route through) makes the whole Linux cross-user harness skip cleanly when sandbox-test is absent, instead of crashing. Linux byte-identical when the user exists. Verified: pytest --collect-only test_lite_macos.py = exit 0, 9 tests. NOTE: test_lite_macos.py uses an unregistered pytest.mark.macos_only (harmless PytestUnknownMarkWarning) — register in pyproject.toml during cleanup.

M21-S4 live bring-up: the operator daemon runs FINE on a PLAIN (non-test-feature) build — SANDBOX_BROKER_SOCKET and SANDBOX_USERS_CONF are honored UNCONDITIONALLY (not feature-gated), and without test-env-override the state-root/lima-home/gateway-tag default to production /var/lib/sandboxd + canonical tag (exactly what we want). Recipe: sandboxd --socket /var/lib/sandboxd/501/sandboxd.sock --base-dir /var/lib/sandboxd/501 --log-file <f>, with SANDBOX_BROKER_SOCKET=/var/lib/sandboxd/501/broker.sock + SANDBOX_USERS_CONF=/var/lib/sandboxd/501/live-users.conf. Supersedes the older M20-S5 belief that the broker seam needed the test-env-override feature.

M21-S4 FIRST-LIGHT BUG (gateway): fresh gateway create fails ensure_ready ('Docker daemon did not start inside gateway VM within 300s') even though dockerd IS up in-VM. Real cause: the forwarded gateway-docker.sock returns EOF because the gateway provision sets /var/run/docker.sock to 0660 root:docker + usermod -aG docker the Lima user, but Lima's ControlPersist SSH master is established at BOOT before the group add, so the socket-forward (and limactl shell) run WITHOUT the docker group and can't read the 660 socket. chmod 666 the in-VM socket fixes it instantly. This is the first FRESH gateway create with the post-8bacb1b (Docker-from-Ubuntu-packages) 660+group provision — M20-S6 reused a pre-existing instance, so it never exercised this path. Fix: gateway_lima.rs provision should make the socket world-RW persistently via a docker.socket systemd drop-in (SocketMode=0666), dropping the racy group approach; host-side socket stays 0600 so the boundary holds.

M21-S4 FIRST-LIGHT BUG (create dispatch, the blocker): on macOS the create handler runs generic CA-gen + create_network (HOST docker, no socket) + 'creating VM' (main.rs ~2026-2081) BEFORE the macOS-Container early-return to create_session_macos_lite (~2175). Result: the bridge network is created on HOST docker (not the forwarded gateway-VM socket) and registered in the in-memory map, then create_session_macos_lite re-creates it on the forwarded socket -> 'session X already has network Y' guard (network.rs:354) -> 500 -> session Error. The macOS Lima early-return is correctly placed (~2008) but the Container one is ~150 lines too late. Fix: move the macOS-Container early-return to immediately AFTER the macOS-Lima early-return, before any generic network/CA/VM code. Never caught statically (review focused on egress/restart); pure runtime dispatch-order bug — exactly what first-light is for.

M21-S4 first-light fixes landed (1 pass): main.rs macOS-Container early-return moved above generic CA/network/VM code (bug 3 dispatch); gateway_lima.rs docker socket now world-RW via docker.socket.d/10-socketmode.conf SocketMode=0666 + chmod 666 current-boot (bug 1), and ensure_route_helper_in_vm copies to /tmp then sudo install (bug 2); lite_macos.rs 9p stanza emits top-level mountType:9p (bug 4/#261, Lima 2.1.2 confirms top-level mountType, 9p still supported). build -p sandboxd exit 0, clippy -p sandboxd -p sandbox-core -D warnings clean, 11 scoped hermetic tests pass. Env gotcha: cargo nextest with '>file' redirect auto-backgrounds + empties the file on this host — use inline 2>&1 | grep.

M21-S4 first-light SCOPE finding: macOS lite container FILE-PROVISIONING is only partially implemented. create_session_macos_lite adapted network + route-helper (None + limactl shell) + lite-image load, but the container still bind-mounts HOST paths for the guest binary, CA cert, and SSH dir — none of which exist inside the gateway VM where the container runs, so docker create fails ('bind source path does not exist: .../ca/cert.pem'). --read-only rootfs (container.rs) rules out docker cp to rootfs targets. Design facts: guest binary is BAKED into the lite image (Dockerfile COPY sandbox-guest) so macOS should SKIP the guest bind (use baked-in, version-matched); shared: workspace is 9p->bind (works); CA cert + SSH files are per-session host files needing a VM-resident bind source. Spec §969 stresses gateway-VM blast radius (shared VM hosts all sessions) => prefer minimal per-session VM exposure over a broad 9p mount of the whole sessions dir. Delegating a design investigation before implementing.

M21-S4 Part 1 DONE (macOS lite file-provisioning): stage_lite_session_files (limactl copy cert.pem+authorized_keys+passwd+group into /tmp/sandbox-lite/<id> in the gateway VM) + ContainerNetwork bind sources set to those VM paths (container.rs bind logic reused unchanged); guest -v overlay skipped when docker_socket.is_some() (image-baked guest); setup_macos_lite_gateway now writes the mitmproxy CA pair via write_file_to_gateway_container (fixed the ignored _ca_dir); create+start re-stage; delete cleans the VM dir. build/clippy -D/fmt clean, 13 scoped tests pass. Same defect class; M21-S4 review missed it (it verified the socket was forwarded, not that binds were VM-valid).

M21-S4 first-light bug: lite container exits 126 'exec: /usr/local/bin/sandbox-guest: Exec format error'. Root cause: make lite-image (Makefile:284) bakes sandboxd/target/release/sandbox-guest = the HOST cargo build, which on macOS is a Darwin Mach-O — wrong arch for the linux/arm64 gateway VM. Same class as the route-helper: macOS needs a linux/aarch64 cross-build of sandbox-guest baked into the lite image (spec §1396). Also resource defaults bug: lite container --cpus/--memory default to host-80%/host-RAM but the container runs in the 2-CPU/2GB gateway VM (docker create rejects --cpus > 2; /proc/meminfo unreadable on macOS -> fallback 4096MB) — must derive from the gateway VM, not the host.

M21-S4 e2e-harness toolchain discovery (resolves the build-fixture 300s timeout): the default 'cargo' on this host is HOMEBREW /opt/homebrew/bin/cargo 1.96.0 (ignores rust-toolchain.toml), but the e2e conftest build fixture (conftest.py:699 'cargo build --workspace', cwd=workspace, PATH from ~/.cargo/env, timeout=300) uses the RUSTUP shim which in-workspace honors rust-toolchain.toml -> 1.88.0. log.title: macOS lite usability: egress policy/DNS distribution + local:/repo/boot-cmd + full-backend gateway-CA/restore
log.summary: macOS lite egress allow-policy + DNS distribution COMPLETE (committed 0cf6446, 10 files +1150/-97 incl new dns_gate_bridge.rs). Routed the 4 host-bound egress surfaces (PolicyDistributor::distribute, AtomicListenerWriter, dns_propagation, lds_ack) through the forwarded gateway socket on macOS via new gateway_for_policy/policy_probe_socket seams; deliver the per-session Envoy listener by write-temp+mv INSIDE the gateway container (Envoy LDS reloads on rename not truncate — proven by a live spike) with a per-session in-daemon listener cache for the head/tail invariant; added a daemon-owned per-session REVERSE byte-pump (per-connection docker-exec + socat UNIX-LISTEN, the proxy async-pump carve-out) bridging the in-container DNS-gate UDS -> host gate UDS, + socat in the gateway image. FAIL-CLOSED (bridge down => gate unreachable => allow stays closed, deny holds). Linux byte-identical (None-wrapper sigs + cfg(macos)). Caught+fixed a latent macOS rollback-nft host-socket bug. VERIFICATION: allow-open MACHINERY PROVEN LIVE via an IP-literal allow (1.1.1.1:80/tcp) — REAL egress opened (curl exit 0 HTTP 301), nft policy_allow_tcp={1.1.1.1 . 80}, Envoy filter_chains non-empty, lds.update_success 0->1, while 8.8.8.8 stayed BLOCKED. macOS + Linux container clippy 1.88.0 -D clean; 274+ hermetic + 4 new bridge tests; fmt. dns-gate bridge TRANSPORT partially-confirmed (in-container gate socket + socat live, CoreDNS query_allowed, policy.conf delivered). DEFERRED (ENV-BLOCKED not code, tracked todo): DOMAIN end-to-end re-confirm — dev host DNS degraded by 4486 sleep/wakes (VM SLIRP + dockerd embedded resolver both empty A records); re-run domain live gate on a healthy host. PROCESS WIN: the first live gate CAUGHT the original core-egress gap pre-commit (dns-gate UDS unreachable in-VM); bridge fix + IP-rule validation followed. Formal review = M23 arc review.
decisions: M21-S6 scope (the macOS-lite usability layer deferred from S4's first-light): (1) BIG — egress allow-policy + DNS-domain distribution on macOS lite: PolicyDistributor::distribute writes the Envoy listener to a HOST path + uses host docker; dns_propagation::read_resolved_json + lds_ack::wait_for_lds_ack use host docker — none work in the gateway VM, so applying a USER --policy/preset + live DNS reconciliation is broken on macOS lite (only initial deny-all works, set via setup_macos_lite_gateway). Route them through the forwarded socket + write_file_to_gateway_container + the in-VM listener path. Investigation called this 'milestone-sized' — may need to split S6. (2) local: workspace push on macOS lite under Apple openrsync (no --mkpath): mkdir-then-rsync. (3) --repo/clone + --boot-cmd + guest-ping post-Running provisioning in create_session_macos_lite. (4) full-backend gateway mitmproxy-CA (setup_macos_gateway ignores _ca_dir, same defect class fixed for lite) + restore_session_networking host-socket -> forwarded socket. Split: S6 = Item 1 ONLY (foundational, must validate the LDS-rename mechanism live first; fallback gRPC/ADS LDS is much larger). S7 = Items 2-5 (local: openrsync, --repo/--boot-cmd/guest-ping provisioning [policy-apply depends on S6], full-backend gateway mitmproxy-CA + start_session_macos_lima None,None + FULL restore_session_networking macOS-awareness, Makefile stage-uid #260). (total sessions: 181 → 182)

M21-S6 RESCOPED to Item 1 ONLY = macOS lite egress allow-policy + DNS distribution (milestone-sized, core egress plane). S7 added = Items 2-5. Handoff: .tasks/handoffs/20260620-m21s6-usability-scope.md. S6 host-bound surfaces to make forwarded-socket-aware: PolicyDistributor::distribute (policy_distributor.rs:356/407/438 bare docker), AtomicListenerWriter (atomic_listener_writer.rs:86,176 host write+bind-mount), dns_propagation::read_resolved_json (282), DockerExecLdsProbe (lds_ack.rs:165) — all driven from call sites binding state.gateway (host socket); gateway_for_probes (main.rs:3923) is the proven seam template. LOAD-BEARING RISK (CLARIFY): write_file_to_gateway_container uses cat> (truncate) which Envoy's LDS watcher IGNORES — only a rename/MovedTo fires reload; the in-VM listener write must reproduce a rename inside the container. MUST validate this live FIRST in S6; if rename doesn't fire Envoy reload, the fallback (gRPC/ADS LDS) is a much larger change. Also recommended: an in-daemon per-session listener cache for the macOS LDS invariant-diff (vs re-reading prior gen via docker exec each 2s).

M21-S6 LDS-rename spike VERDICT (load-bearing risk RESOLVED): rename WORKS — 'cat>p.tmp && mv -f p.tmp p' via one docker exec triggers Envoy LDS reload every time (update_success++/listener_modified++); truncate-write (cat>p, the daemon's current write_file_to_container) is IGNORED by Envoy's filesystem-LDS watcher (path_config_source watched_directory /etc/envoy/listeners, IN_MOVED_TO-only, upstream #20474). The listeners dir is in-container tmpfs with NO host bind-mount (Linux's host AtomicListenerWriter has no macOS analogue). => macOS listener-update mechanism = write-temp + mv -f INSIDE the gateway container via the FORWARDED socket. gRPC/ADS fallback NOT needed. Extra: the daemon's policy docker exec currently can't reach the in-VM container on macOS (No such container) — S6 must route gateway docker through the forwarded socket (gateway_for_probes seam, main.rs:3923). Keep the head/tail framing invariant; same warm-restart-with-drain caveat as Linux. Handoffs: 20260620-m21s6-usability-scope.md + 20260620-m21s6-lds-rename-spike.md.

M21-S6 dns-gate bridge DESIGN (handoff 20260620-m21s6-dns-gate-bridge-design.md): the DaemonGateService + propagate_dns_changes are ALREADY forwarded-socket-wired on macOS (S6); the ONLY missing piece is the inbound gate-request transport. Linux uses the events-dir bind-mount (-v events_host_dir:EVENTS_DIR_IN_CONTAINER, gateway.rs:599-604) so the in-container CoreDNS gate plugin reaches the host gate UDS; macOS build_macos_gateway_docker_args (macos_session.rs:575) has NO such mount. CoreDNS gate plugin is UNIX-ONLY (gate.go:268-271 hardcodes Dial 'unix') -> TCP-gate REJECTED. DECISION: daemon-owned per-session REVERSE byte-pump over the forwarded docker socket — in-container socat UNIX-LISTEN on the gate path; the daemon pumps each accepted connection (async tokio::process pipes, the SSH-proxy pump_container carve-out) to the host gate UnixStream::connect. PER-CONNECTION (not socat ...,fork — fork would corrupt concurrent gate frames on one stdio). CoreDNS/Corefile/wire-protocol/DaemonGateService stay byte-identical. FAIL-CLOSED: bridge down = no inject = allow stays closed, deny holds, decision never leaves the daemon. BLOCKER: socat absent from the gateway image (networking/gateway/Dockerfile) -> DECISION: add socat (+1 Dockerfile line) over a helper crate (simplest). Magnitude ~120-220 lines Rust (cfg(macos), Linux byte-identical) + lifecycle (create/restart/delete). Open: exact per-connection socat framing (a <1h spike); whether the macOS FULL backend shares the gap.

M21-S6 core-egress allow-open machinery PROVEN (IP-literal gate PASS): applied an IP allow (1.1.1.1:80/tcp; IP literals are Destination::Cidr -> injected at compile/apply with NO DNS, policy.rs:357/1015-1027). RESULT: nft policy_allow_tcp got {1.1.1.1 . 80}, Envoy filter_chains non-empty (chain level1_1_1_1_1_p80, original_dst L1 passthrough), lds.update_success 0->1 (update_rejected unchanged), curl http://1.1.1.1 from the container = exit 0 HTTP/1.1 301 (REAL egress opened), curl http://8.8.8.8 = exit 7 BLOCKED (destination-specific), policy status propagated=true (no DNS). listener_modified stayed 0 — correct (first-ever accepted generation; update_success+1 is the load-bearing signal). => the S6 write-temp+mv -> LDS reload -> nft inject -> egress-open path WORKS. Combined with the dns-gate bridge transport partially-confirmed (gate socket+socat+CoreDNS query_allowed), S6 code is validated. Every step idempotent (skip-if-absent); animates through shared ui.sh with plain-path degradation. INVARIANTS: never pkill qemu (VM reap = LIMA_HOME image removal), no direct limactl, _sandboxd (not Apple _sandbox), --force = refusal-bypass only (no force-stop API), single sudo batch. The spec's 'DELETE /sessions/{id}?force=true' is factually wrong (real endpoint is POST /sessions/{id}/stop?force=true) AND exceeds what Linux uninstall does; do NOT wire a divergent force-stop API loop on macOS. Per M22.md:82, the _sandboxd user/group removal is GATED on --purge-state (with it: remove state tree + user + group members-first; without it: preserve state + user for clean re-install).

S8 FIRST LIVE install.sh on macOS (Tart harness, commit b573285 ff-merged to master) found 5 CONFIRMED production defects (install.sh fails at step 3 on EVERY macOS install): (1) install.sh:2663,2683 'install -D' is GNU-only — BSD/macOS install rejects it (abort at install-binaries); (2) same lines '-g root' — macOS group is wheel not root; (3) Darwin path never creates /etc/sandboxd/users.conf (_compute_plan_darwin omits it; the Linux block at 1722 even hardcodes 'sandbox' not '_sandboxd') -> daemon crash-loops 'users.conf not found'; (4) daemon sysctl exec fails under launchd — macos_session.rs:757,764 use bare 'sysctl' + plist PATH(line 108) lacks /usr/sbin -> false 'IP forwarding ON' -> daemon refuses start; (5) check_prereqs(942) omits qemu though the gateway Lima VM hard-needs qemu-system-aarch64. CAUGHT a Linux regression in the 5-bug fix (17d8bcd) before accepting: the parent-dir 'install -d -o root -g wheel ... || true' (binary loop + cosign) hardcodes -g wheel on BOTH platforms. Debian/Ubuntu (the Linux install-e2e targets!) have NO wheel group -> install -d fails, swallowed by ||true -> /usr/local/libexec/sandboxd not created -> subsequent 'install <file>' (no -D auto-parent) fails -> Linux install breaks. Fix: compute _grp/_cosign_grp BEFORE install -d and use -g "" for the dir too (root on Linux, wheel on macOS) — correct by construction (root exists on all Linux, wheel on all macOS). ALSO folding in a likely 6th Darwin bug the fixer flagged: _write_checkpoint (~line 2369) uses sha256sum unconditionally (absent on macOS; only shasum -a 256) — add a fallback if it's on the Darwin path. ROOT CAUSE of the repeated cold/slow cargo builds (not a timeout issue): TOOLCHAIN THRASH. Dev host has BOTH Homebrew rustc 1.96.0 (/opt/homebrew/bin, default PATH) AND rustup-pinned 1.88.0 (~/.cargo/bin via rust-toolchain.toml inside the repo). Builds NOT sourcing ~/.cargo/env use Homebrew 1.96.0; pytest's conftest sources ~/.cargo/env -> rustup 1.88.0. Alternating between the two invalidates the ENTIRE target/ cache -> full cold rebuild from proc-macro2 every switch (~5-10min) -> the 300s sandbox_binaries build timeout killed it mid-compile. FIX: ALL build invocations must use rustup 1.88.0 (source ~/.cargo/env, run inside the repo so rust-toolchain.toml pins). The 300->1800s timeout bump is secondary insurance for a legitimately-cold macOS build; the real fix is toolchain consistency. Relates to #294 (dev-host build robustness).

Every GuestSocat consumer (exec/SSH-proxy/rsync) consumes the connection; one arriving in the 2s reconnect gap finds no agent (broker.rs:604-608) -> 'session agent for olek is not running'.
