Completing it would record that the defect existed and was surveyed; it never existed, and the item was an open work order against a fabrication that would have resurfaced to whoever drained the backlog. The census that establishes zero was nonetheless run and is on file.

The placement-mode field is not three identical edits. Both Lima network-record literals have the operator identity as a live local and take a one-line change. The lite path constructs its record inside the shared allocator, which receives neither a session operator nor any identity, so the field is filled at the daemon-side persist point where the operator is already in scope — not by threading an operator parameter through a cross-crate allocator shared with the Linux path. There is no write-then-update window because the persist point is downstream of construction.

That fill-in must land together with a correction to the allocator's own comment, which asserts the per-operator partition is a platform concept the allocator is not part of while the allocator is precisely how that platform's lite backend allocates. The comment is the likeliest generator of the absent field rather than a description of it, so correcting only the value leaves the reason someone would re-introduce it.

Declined to authorize retiring the third check's frozen approved-set even though a false positive on correct code was demonstrated in it. Retiring a check is a permissive change and that set still reports two unexplained containment violations; removing the check that produced findings nobody has explained discards the findings with it. The order is explain first, retire second.

The fix is the collapse idiom, not the missing retry. Both the name resolution and the store read answer not-found and could-not-determine with the same absent value, on the same path, and one of them documents that conflation outright. Adding a retry to one of them treats the symptom at one site while leaving the shape that produced it. The change is to stop collapsing absent with undetermined anywhere on the restore path and to route every undetermined case through the visible decline rather than a silent skip.

Not ordering a measurement of the macvlan reading. The slot-to-address map is a pure function, so a collision hands both sessions the identical VM address, not merely a shared segment; the fix and its priority are unchanged whichever way the reading resolves. The two readings differ only in characterization.

The addon fail-open is out of scope for this milestone - it is platform-independent and pre-existing, not a consequence of the gateway ownership change. Filing as todos rather than fixing in-session, and surfacing at the milestone boundary. Severity is latent rather than live only because nothing on the request path currently raises, which is a measured claim whose denominator I have now asked for.

Whether the generated ruleset reaches the gateway container at session-create is still the load-bearing untested question, and the masquerade result makes it more important rather than less: that rule is precisely what separates the contained production path from the leaky arm. Dispatching it read-first - trace the call path before booting anything - and pairing it with a read-only observation of the already-running gateway VM to settle the DNS inference without mutating it.

Ruled against widening the unfiltered session reader from crate-private to public in order to unblock the residual-reads conversion. It is a deliberate access-control boundary and widening it would trade a durable property for a scheduling convenience; worse, its own documentation already names two consumers structurally incapable of calling it, so the widening would be justified against a description nobody has validated. The three affected call sites wait on the network-info operator-uid fill instead, which promotes that item from deferred cleanup to prerequisite.

Ten daemon-side owner-resolution sites will read the persisted owner field on the network record rather than routing through the unfiltered store accessor. The accessor route needs a Session per site, obtainable only from a list accessor carrying the identical 'not for handler code' contract as the one already declined for widening — the same permission with no modifier touched and no diff for a reviewer to see, which is worse than the explicit widening refused earlier.

The owner-invariant check set stays un-retired. Both residual flags are false positives on correct code but of two different classes: one is caller-side delegation the checks do not model, the other is two checks disagreeing about a single host-scoped carve-out site. One shared fix retires neither, and the disagreement between the two checks is itself the finding — a carve-out defined twice will diverge again, possibly in the permissive direction where nothing reports.

The three prose defects on the store boundary are filed as one pass rather than three items. Their shared cause — no validator ties a doc comment to the item it sits on — is visible only across them, and fixing them separately would leave the mechanism unnamed.

Retracting an earlier reason of mine: I cancelled a verification step on the ground that no production path pulls an image by name. That was false. The delegate had censused every way to REQUEST a pull, correctly and completely, and reported it as the behaviour never occurring; the pull arises from a default that no call site names. The cancellation stands on an unrelated ground, but my confidence in it was borrowed from a claim that had not been measured at the scope I used it.

The gateway-VM in-place observation stays declined, re-derived from scratch rather than inherited: the premise that partly supported the earlier decline was retracted, and the corrected version makes the blast radius larger, not smaller. The decision is unchanged because the surviving ground is a hard constraint on touching the host's VM fixture, which is not a cost/benefit input - not because the tradeoff came out the same way.

The gateway-VM DNS break is promoted from inferred to a traced production defect. Its fix will be DESIGNED before it is written: the surface is egress enforcement, the current defect fails closed, and an over-permissive repair would fail open - strictly worse than the bug. The rule shape, what it newly permits, and what that permits an attacker in the VM host namespace to do must be stated before any code is written.

Correcting my own claim from earlier this session: I said a decision that rested on two grounds and lost one had suffered a real loss of robustness. That was wrong. The surviving ground was independently sufficient all along, so the second was corroboration and nothing load-bearing changed. Listing a redundant ground beside a sufficient one manufactures a false fragility later - state which ground is sufficient at the time you state it.

Correcting a briefing error of my own: I told a delegate the deferred backlog was about 80 items when the dump I had produced in the same turn contained 236. The wc -l output was in my own tool result; I had run it to confirm the dump succeeded, not to count, so it never displaced the remembered figure. The cost was not the number but that it propagated as method - I scoped the delegate's sampling instruction against a denominator three times off.

This session has in practice become a verification session rather than an implementation one: nothing committed, and it has filed close to half the standing backlog itself. The findings it produced are real production defects on the egress-enforcement surface, so the work was worth doing, but the next planning step should absorb them as implementation sessions rather than letting them sit as todos. Flagging forward rather than editing the plan.

Chose the option that matches the pre-DNAT tuple via conntrack original-direction, over both the hook-priority variant and disabling the Lima host resolver outright. The priority variant is equivalent today but would silently widen the day anyone adds another redirect; disabling the host resolver has a genuinely empty permission delta but trades it for a silent DNS regression on the end user's machine, and the risk is wider than split-DNS - it assumes the fallback upstreams are reachable at all, which a locked-down corporate network may not allow. Prefer a named bounded permission over a silent degradation on someone else's network.

The health probe should assert only the deny-all base table, not the DNAT or policy tables. Teardown removes the latter two, so the base table is the one artifact expected for a running gateway's whole life, and its absence is exactly the restart failure. Its injection window is milliseconds rather than the tens of seconds the DNAT tables need, which sidesteps the constant-margin hazard entirely. The assertion must list the table by name rather than grep the ruleset: the base table's name is a proper prefix of the other two, so the grep form passes on a container that has DNAT and no deny-all.

The enforcement-blindness finding cannot be closed by the health-probe change alone. On the backend arm the monitor skips, a truthful probe converts an unseeable failure into a seen failure that still triggers no recovery - an observability gain, not a fix. Requiring the backend-by-platform matrix before any implementation, so the probe change cannot be shipped as a resolution of enforcement blindness on the platform this milestone is about.

Recorded against my own earlier reasoning: one of the three grounds I gave for rejecting the disable-the-host-resolver option is weakened by a later read. I argued its fallback upstreams might be unreachable on a locked-down corporate network, but the product already hardcodes public resolvers for the gateway's DNS server on that platform, so it already assumes that reachability. The decision stands on the remaining sufficient ground - a zero permission delta traded for a silent change in resolution semantics across every VM-internal consumer - but the practical consequence is that the rejected option is a more reasonable fallback than I implied if the chosen one proves hard to validate.

Adding an nftables assertion to the gateway health probe does not close the recovery findings. The probe converts an invisible failure into a visible one that nothing acts on; the enforcement gap is a separate fix and the findings stay open until it lands.

Both failure modes of the chosen DNS fix are fail-closed: it either fails to load and aborts gateway setup, or loads and matches nothing and DNS is denied. Validating it is therefore a reliability and debuggability concern, and ranks below the two open fail-open items rather than above them.

Approved the nftables check-mode validation with two pre-registered controls — a deliberately misspelled keyword that must go red to prove the parser was reached, and a delete of a nonexistent table that distinguishes parse-only from kernel-reaching check. A green may only be reported as the ruleset loading on that userspace and kernel, never as the fix working.

An evidence-labelling discipline grades each conclusion and not the model it came from, so claims sharing a wrong model fail together whatever their labels say. On any retraction the separate question is what else was derived from the same model, and those siblings must be re-derived rather than re-checked.

The surviving forward-path exposure is the only fail-open claim left and rests on the model that just collapsed, so it now outranks validating the DNS fix. Re-derivation must census every writer to each table in lifecycle order, ending at the state a restart can occur from, rather than re-reading the same rule text.
Ordered the forward-axis writer census ahead of the semantic match rig: the forward hole is the only fail-open item left, while both failure modes of the DNS fix are fail-closed.

Comments adjacent to a policy rule are load-bearing and must be no stronger than what was measured; sent back an image-path comment whose no-network clause exceeded what the pull-policy flag guarantees.

Did not accept the retirement of the callsite set: my authorization was conditional on both being false positives of the same class, and they are of two different classes, so the precondition never fired. A conditional authorization whose precondition fails is not a weaker authorization.

Recorded that making the sink-argument check consult the existing method-name carve-out is a design goal with a missing term rather than a wiring change, so it is carried as open rather than queued as mechanical.

Removing one of two justifications for a permissive firewall rule promotes the survivor to sole load-bearer with nobody re-verifying it, because the rule itself did not change. The surviving justification must be marked as inherited-and-unverified rather than silently retained or deleted.

Three defects this session share one shape: a rule whose correctness depends on something invisible at its own site — a permit and its deny in tables with different lifetimes, a permissive rule whose surviving justification was never re-verified, and a gate that works only because of a different rule above it. Grep, review and find-usages are all local, so nothing traverses 'this is only safe because of that'. The dependency must be written at the site.

A dependency written as a justification is worse protection than one not written at all. The health predicate's premise was recorded at its site, phrased as a reason things are safe, which reads as reassurance and forecloses the question rather than marking fragility. Write such premises as failure conditions naming what voids them, not as reasons the code is fine.

The five percent already-fixed ceiling applies only to the age-selected stratum and must not be carried to the top of a consequence ranking. High-consequence items attract work, so the top of that ranking decays faster than an age-selected sample, measured here at two of six against three of forty-two. An evidence-weighted sort also buries fixes for the same reason it buries defects.

When a number is load-bearing, verify it by performing an operation that must traverse the whole set — sort, enumerate, render, walk item by item — not by re-reading or re-asserting it. Two independent delegates today caught errors in their own work this way and by no other means: one while drafting concrete packet sends, one while performing a re-sort. Reviewing the artifact found neither.

The obvious predicate-level fix has opposite outcomes per platform: on Linux it routes control into an already-correct unfiltered recovery arm and the gateway self-heals; on macOS lite it produces detect-warn-continue every thirty seconds. A fix validated on Linux would look complete and change nothing observable on macOS. The integration tier is Linux-only and cannot run on a macOS host, so validation is structurally guaranteed to happen on the platform where the fix works.

Retracted the caller-discipline sentence I had ruled the fourth instance of the structural class. An untruncated caller census shows it is factually correct: the only site setting the flag true on a real session VM is unreachable on the macOS path, the macOS session path passes false explicitly, and the sole macOS true is the base-image build. Dropped on the principle that a contested exemplar corrupts a newly-named class, not because the class test failed - being true is the normal state of a member.

Adopted a companion clause to the traversal rule: performing an operation that traverses the set catches errors upstream of a deliverable, but a claim that is itself the deliverable has no downstream and needs a traversal commissioned deliberately. Reachability claims are the standing candidate - they read as structural facts, ranking decisions hang on them, and writing one forces no walk of the path.

Correcting forward the evidence status in the replan reason that created the new milestone. It says the gateway is measurably fail-open across a restart on the Linux route. The mechanism is source-derived by control-flow trace at a named commit, and the Linux conclusion is a derivation from code that is identical on both targets, not a second observation - the delegate stated explicitly that no runtime observation was made on Linux. The rig that did run measured DNAT and conntrack semantics, a different question. The milestone framing must say source-derived, not measured.

I adopted the rule that a load-bearing claim with nothing downstream needs a traversal commissioned deliberately, and then violated it in the next action by sourcing a milestone number from memory rather than listing the directory. The claim was load-bearing, since it named the file to be created, and terminal, since nothing downstream would have checked it before an overwrite. Diagnosing a class of error does not inoculate against committing it, and having just adopted the remedy is not protection either.

Delegation prompts will add a framing line: if the question is what breaks rather than what you are permitted to do, decide it yourself and report the reasoning. The standing escalate-do-not-work-around instruction was converting risk trade-offs the delegate was better placed to judge into permission requests only the lead could answer.

Refused to ship the new gateway-restart milestone with regression coverage that lands only in the Linux-only integration tier while the macOS side is a manual replay. That reproduces the milestone's own failure mode - a barrier held open by someone remembering to check rather than by construction - in the document meant to close it. Its closing session must require at least one automated check that actually runs on macOS, or name the gap as an explicit residual.

Standing practice: before committing a planning document, run an independent verification pass by an agent that neither wrote nor reviewed it. Here that pass found four confirmed defects after a review-plus-fix cycle by one agent had passed the same document twice, including a scope hole that left a session unable to satisfy its own exit criterion.

Sequencing the typed-signal session before the predicate session is a design choice, not a constraint the source trace establishes. The trace says all three barriers are independent, describes clearing the predicate alone as producing a monitor that correctly detects the failure, and explicitly declines to be read as a work plan. The choice stands on its own grounds; the justification must stop citing a section that says the opposite.

A residual-escape clause that a session discharges by writing the residual is self-discharging, and reproduces the failure the milestone exists to close. Where a requirement may prove unachievable, the escape must require a ruling from outside the session rather than a note the session writes itself.

My stated reason for sequencing the typed-signal session first was refuted on measurement: the alternative route is not free-text parsing but an equally typed closed op carrying the same accretion warning. The surviving argument is route-independent and stronger, and the preference between routes is now stated as the milestone's design choice rather than as a fact.

When the justification for a plan's structure has to be rebuilt twice from two independent refutations, suspect the structure rather than repairing the justification a third time. The milestone's first session exists to add a wire variant, and both arguments for why it must come first have now failed on measurement. Resolving whether that session should exist takes priority over any further wording repair.

The permit/deny lifetime asymmetry is accepted as residual for this milestone rather than removed structurally, and that position gets recorded in the plan as the milestone's own choice with the bounded window named. Removing it structurally means making the per-policy render emit a third table and reworking the teardown ruleset that deletes only two, which is a different change of a different size. What the standing ruling requires is a derivation and a recorded decision, not a prescribed patch, so an explicit accept with the open instance left pointed at satisfies it and a silent omission does not.

The milestone switches from detecting a restart to reading enforcement state directly: the predicate asks whether the deny-all floor is present rather than whether the gateway restarted since the last injection. Grounds — it is stateless, so no new persisted operand and no on-disk compatibility question; it measures the property the project exists to guarantee instead of a proxy for one cause of that property failing; it catches rule loss from any cause, not only restart; it fails closed when the container cannot be read; and it costs the same single variant on a closed enum as the alternative. Naming the self-serving part so it stays checkable: this choice also deletes the stored-operand comparison that several review findings snagged on, which is a real simplification but also a reason to look twice.

My own ruling contained an overclaim and two findings caught it. I recorded the residual lifetime window as bounded to one gateway-monitor cycle where it had been unbounded. The container health state also continues past the monitor check while it reports Starting, and the gateway image sets a thirty-second start period, so the real bound is at least one cycle plus that start period. The error is in the fail-open direction and the text is mine, not a delegate's. The bound must be restated as what the source supports rather than what I asserted.

RULING on how the per-operator agent learns the ownership mode: defer the mechanism, keep the switch structurally off, and finish the call-site conversion anyway. Grounds, in order of weight. (1) Making the suffixed mode unconditional contradicts a committed exit criterion that switch-off behaviour stay identical to the prior tree, and forecloses any field rollback for a subsystem whose whole promise is unbypassable egress. (2) Both env-var shapes put the read in the agent's own environment, which is per-plist and therefore per-operator, manufacturing a skew axis that the ship-as-one-versioned-set property had eliminated; skew is silent because check-in carries no handshake. (3) Nothing can set the variable by any supported install path today, so adopting a mechanism now buys nothing and adds a failure mode. The mechanism should be chosen in the change that first wires the switch to a real install path, because that change touches the plist, the installer and the docs together.

COROLLARY to that ruling, and a correction to the brief's framing: deferring the mode mechanism does NOT license leaving the remaining call sites unconverted. The brief says the leave-it-daemon-wide options stay available indefinitely under the defer ruling, which is true for correctness but converts the divergence into a latent trap. One batch is already converted; a half-converted tree is behaviourally identical while the switch is off, so no test can catch it, and whoever eventually throws the switch inherits a container leak per teardown and wrong-gateway probes. The safety of the unconverted sites would live entirely in a flag being off, with nothing traversing that dependency. A uniformly converted tree is equally identical under switch-off and removes the trap, so convert.

Also from that ruling: put the daemon-side half of the switch prerequisite in the code, at the environment variable definition, stating that the agent side is not wired and what must be decided before the switch can be turned on. The agent side already carries this note in its own words at the naming divergence. Making it symmetric puts the warning where someone setting the variable will actually look, rather than only in a plan document that will not exist later.

RULING on the lite-image tarball lookup: keep the loader and the shipped test behaviour, and treat lite as gateway-owner-only while the switch is off. Rejecting the plan bullet that would add a symmetric two-levels-up fallback, because measurement shows it would point at a location nothing writes: the gateway tarball has two producers and the lite tarball has one, and that producer is a dev make target, not the installer. Adding a fallback to a path no producer populates is dead code on the day it lands. Rejecting the fix-the-producers option too, but on scope rather than correctness: it moves the install and dev-host contract, and staging a hundreds-of-megabyte lite tarball from the installer is a product call about what every install should carry, not a call this milestone should absorb.

Two repairs that ruling does require, both in code rather than in a plan file. First, the loader comment justifies itself by today's producer set, saying there is no second location to look in; that is true now and becomes misleading the moment any per-owner staging path exists, and it never states the consequence that matters, which is that a non-daemon gateway owner's lite load fails under the switch on. Restate it as the consequence. Second, the shipped test's name asserts a policy while its body pins a configuration, so if the producers are ever fixed the name reads as forbidding the fix. Rename it to state what the body actually pins.

That ruling also resolves the reported staging-path conflict without a code change: the lite staging target writes to the daemon's own operator home, which is only correct when the gateway owner is the daemon, and gateway-owner-only lite is exactly what the ruling adopts. So the target is correct for the supported case rather than wrong, and it needs no edit; what it needs is for the limitation to be stated where the operator meets it.

RULING on the unresolvable-operator policy: uniform decline. Log at error with the session id, mark the session's networking degraded, and surface it in diagnostics, by calling the decline reporter that already exists rather than writing a second policy. Rejecting the fall-back-to-the-daemon option outright: it is precisely what the operator type was built to prevent, having deliberately no uid accessor and no option conversion so the silent default cannot be spelled. Rejecting the split recommendation (fall back on teardown, refuse on setup) because it does not map onto the code: three of the five helpers return unit and cannot express a refusal without a signature change, and one of those three sits on the setup side while carrying a shipped documented promise that its failures do not propagate, so adopting the split would retract that promise as a side effect.

A correction to how the security argument for that ruling was framed, which changes what it distinguishes. Declining does not act against the wrong gateway; it does not act at all. So the wrong-gateway hazard, which is the failure the project exists to prevent, is avoided by both the decline and the refuse options equally, and the security rationale separates those two from the fall-back option rather than separating them from each other. What decline and refuse actually differ on is only whether the caller learns by an HTTP error or by a degraded status. That is a reporting choice, not a safety one.

A second reason to prefer decline that is stronger than consistency: it makes an open question moot instead of requiring it to be answered. The DNS gate bridge's shipped fail-closed argument covers failing to start, not starting against the wrong gateway, and nobody has traced what the in-VM resolver plugin does with a gate connection for a session it does not host. Under decline the bridge is never started, which is exactly the case the existing argument does cover. Under fall-back it would be started against a foreign gateway and that untraced question would become load-bearing. Condition on the ruling: each of the five sites must be checked to confirm its decline is fail-closed, and any site where declining would leave a session with egress but not the right policy needs a hard refusal instead.

RULING on the probe factory's signature: it gains a required owner parameter and the daemon health handler resolves per session. The section's premise that this handler has no derivable owner is true of its signature and false at its call site, which sits inside a loop with a full session row in hand, so the option the section could not see is the one to take. Rejecting the optional-owner form because it recreates exactly the site class the sweep cannot grade, where a reader cannot distinguish deliberately daemon-wide from never converted without reading the caller. Rejecting explicitly naming the daemon's gateway because under the switch on it would report every operator-owned session's status by probing a gateway that does not host it. The decline case reports through the existing free-form status string, so no schema change.

The precedent that decided the probe ruling, and the way its supporting argument was misread. The already-shipped sibling decision establishes deciding per endpoint on whether the answer is a host property or a caller property, not always-caller: the same handler resolves image presence per caller and resolves the Lima version daemon-wide, and both halves are in the tree. Gateway status for a given session is a session property, so it resolves per session. The health handler's own doc calls itself daemon-wide, which reads as supporting the explicit-daemon option, but that carve-out is about whose sessions are listed and not about which gateway is probed. The two clauses had to be separated before the doc stopped looking like evidence for the wrong option.

RULING on the sweep instrument: commit the successor gateway-owner invariant checker under a committed tools path and let it be the acceptance gate; do not commit the original class-based predicate. It wins on demonstrated detection power rather than tidiness, having found a third owner-keyed sink that nothing checked while the class it replaced was standing in front of it. It also reports whether it is measuring anything, printing per-clause denominators, a scan-scope line with a landmark check, and carrying a self-test injection mode, where the class predicate cannot distinguish a clean tree from a collapsed selector. Leaving the criterion discharged by argument, or by whatever sweep someone happens to run, is a guard on an axis that cannot fail.

Two consequences of that ruling worth stating so they are not rediscovered. The checker anchors at a fixed revision by design, which is right for auditing a claim about a particular commit but wrong for a committed gate, so the committed copy should default to the working revision and keep explicit anchoring available as a flag. And retiring the predicate's two false-positive classes stops being necessary for acceptance, because the classes belong to the instrument that is not being committed; the class predicate stays useful as a work-list generator for the remaining batches, which is a different job from being the gate, and the recorded false positives are what make its count readable.

Accepted a second decline holder rather than reusing the recovery one. The recovery holder replaces its whole list by design, which is right for a pass that re-answers 'which sessions can we not place' in full and wrong for a per-session helper: recording through it would erase the last recovery report. The ruling forbade a divergent decline *policy*, not a second data structure; the policy (error + session id + owner + reason, degraded mark, one line per session) is matched exactly.

Accepted clear-on-resolve for the per-session decline holder, which the recovery holder does not have. Without it the map only grows and keeps lines for deleted sessions. The entry means 'this session's operator is unresolvable now', so clearing it when the operator resolves keeps it true; the recovery holder gets the same property for free because a clean pass empties it. Degraded is deliberately not cleared alongside: that a gateway can be named again is not that one was rebuilt.

Accepted threading the kernel-supplied operator uid at sites that already hold an authenticated identity, and per-session store resolution only where no identity exists. The peer-credential uid is strictly resolved at accept time, so routing it back through a store-row lookup would add a failure mode and buy nothing. The daemon-wide health handler is the site with no identity in hand, and it resolves per session inside its loop.

The clear-policy and apply-policy sites return an error rather than declining silently. A silent decline there would answer 'policy cleared, session is now fail-closed' while the old permissive allow-list stayed installed — a genuine fail-open. This is the hard-refusal outcome the decline ruling reserved for exactly this shape.

Correcting the earlier ruling that threading the authenticated caller uid is right wherever an identity is in hand. Authenticated caller identity and session owner are two different quantities, and the lookup that selects the row filters on the owner *name*, which does not bridge them: they diverge whenever the name-to-uid mapping moved between create and now. The row's own operator uid is always present and immutable, so it is strictly the better source. New rule: create-time passes the caller uid, since the caller is the owner by construction; every post-create site resolves from the row.

The stop and remove handlers get a hard refusal, not a silent decline, when the row's operator cannot be resolved. Reporting a session stopped or removed while its containers survive is the same fail-open shape as reporting a policy cleared while a permissive allow-list stays installed — the caller is told the thing is gone and acts on that. An orphaned container with egress and no lifecycle owner is the worst version of it.

Correction to the prior remaining-work plan: the daemon-wide gateway manager field will NOT be deleted. Deleting it would force correct Linux sites to spell an owner they cannot use, and the resulting compile error proves nothing because on Linux every uid yields the same route. That half owes only a per-row owner resolution in the startup reconcile pass, plus consideration of a platform cfg on the field as the compile-time guard whose absence let that pass drift.

The retraction above strengthens rather than threatens the ruling to defer the ownership-mode mechanism. That ruling assumed the agent could already name a per-operator gateway once told which mode it was in; in fact its reachable paths address the unsuffixed VM unconditionally, so the mechanism is even further from wired than the ruling supposed. No other conclusion rested on the refuted model.

The invariant checker's non-caller-uid acceptance term gets re-anchored, not retired. Retiring an acceptance term is a permissive change, and its claimed redundancy is not currently measurable: a redundant suppressor and a dead one produce identical output, and the demonstrations that could distinguish them are the ones that broke. Retiring would also promote the surviving term to sole load-bearer for the site unreviewed.

The clause left vacuous by the field deletion gets re-pointed rather than retired or silenced. The right question about a check that stopped matching is what region it guarded, not whether its assertion still holds: deleting the field removed one spelling of daemon-built-route-reaches-caller, not the region, which is still occupied by the two long-lived objects built from the daemon's startup route. Since those conversions have no compile-time tripwire, the re-pointed clause becomes the only instrument that can see a half-conversion.

Accept the checker going red on the working revision once re-pointed. A gate reporting genuine outstanding work is the honest state; scoping or allowlisting to reach green would introduce the accepted-violations list whose absence is one of the instrument's better properties. Expected end state is self-test green and default mode red.

The checker lands in the directory that already holds a committed checker wired into CI, not the path named in the original ruling. That path was chosen before the precedent was known; one directory for this class of instrument beats two.

Endorsed a deviation: the NIC-map-miss diagnostic threads the gateway instance name, not the owner uid. My ruling said thread the owner; at the monitor site the owner is derivable and wrong, because the manager producing the map is still the unconverted daemon-wide singleton, so naming the owner would print a per-operator instance while quoting the daemon's map — a new false statement replacing an ambiguous one. The general principle is that a diagnostic must describe what the code actually consulted, which is not always what it should have consulted.

One of my own acceptance criteria will be recorded as UNMET at close rather than reinterpreted to fit. I wrote that no milestone, session or planning-document identifier may appear in any source file, comment, test name or commit message, at a time when I believed the population was about two sites. It is over a hundred and sixty, across crates this milestone never touches, and seventy-seven are operator-visible output with tests pinning the literals. Narrowing the criterion now to whatever the work happens to satisfy would be the failure the criterion existed to prevent, so the honest record is that it stands as written and is not met.

Milestone-identifier removal is scoped to the Rust workspace plus comments and docstrings in the end-to-end suite. Eight functional string constants naming real VMs and containers at runtime are excluded: a rename must preserve the uniqueness that keeps concurrent test files off the same resource name, must not break any cleanup that matches by prefix, and cannot be exercised here at all. An unexercised rename of test identity into a suite nobody present can run is worse than carrying the violation.

The closed-operation-set property is guarded only by a count whose second operand lives in a handoff document that will not survive the increment. That is being moved into the checker as a clause with the constant declared beside its patterns, carrying its own caveat in code: a fixed-name denylist covers regression against a known shape, not the general property, because it cannot see a new free-form field under a name nobody has thought of yet.

Clause counts get pinned only where the population is supposed to stay fixed. The closed-operation-set clause pins because a change in its count IS the signal. The daemon-wide-reader clauses do not, because that population is meant to drain to zero as the work lands, so a pin would be edited on every increment — and a check whose numbers are routinely edited to make it pass has trained its own bypass, which is worse than the gap it closes.

The acceptance criterion forbidding milestone or planning-doc identifiers in any source file is not merely unmet but partly unmeetable: two applied migrations carry such tags and cannot be edited without a renumbering exercise, which is a far larger decision than a de-tagging sweep. The criterion needs rewriting rather than chasing.

The population this identifier criterion governs is durable surfaces only, not the whole repository. Ephemeral planning artifacts citing each other is expressly correct, so a repo-wide census inflates the denominator with files the rule does not reach and was the wrong measurement in kind, not merely in value.

Classification by whether a cited file currently resolves is replaced by classification on what kind of thing the target is: a planning artifact is ephemeral whether or not it is on disk today, so a pointer to one is a dead link with a delay and the repair is to inline the constraint it carried.

Declined to compact the memory index to the size a hook demands. Four index entries were measured to carry their only copy of the actionable clause, so the byte target is reachable only by deleting content or retiring entries, and retiring races with other sessions writing the same file. The index stays above the hook's target and below the read limit.

The invariant checker will derive its wrapper set by iterating from the known sinks to a fixpoint rather than hardcoding the four names measured today. A hardcoded list closes the known holes and leaves the shape open, which yields a check that looks complete because its gaps are patched. The derived set must print its size as a computed scope figure and the self-test must inject at a wrapper call site, so a derivation that collapses to empty fails loudly instead of passing.

A source reference to a planning document tracked in the repo is the same violation as one pointing at an ignored path. Tracking makes the link resolve today, not the target durable, since such documents are rewritten and deleted between increments. Classify on the kind of thing the target is, never on whether it exists now.

The remedy is to delete the pointer from the source file and inline the constraint it carried. The target document is never renamed and its filename never matters. An earlier framing that de-tagging required renaming a tracked document came from reading the criterion's identifier wording as the goal rather than the harm, and that framing is withdrawn.

The census of durable surfaces pointing into .tasks/ is six files, not the four previously recorded. The earlier figure came from a grep scoped by pathspec to Rust and Python sources but reported as repo-wide; the two extra sites are a CI workflow and a shipped README. Corrects the prior count.

A count of affected sites was relayed upward as evidence that a ruling was more consequential, without anyone reading what each site carried. The count was right and the cost inference was backwards. Accepting a figure from a trusted source ended the checking on both sides, and neither side had an incentive to deflate it.

An injection self-test for a fixpoint-derived set proves the set is non-empty and contains the member it injects at, not that the derivation reached the depth it claims. A derivation that stopped one hop early would pass a hop-one injection while silently dropping a third of the call sites. Depth needs its own injection at each hop.

The gateway-owner invariant checker is closed: derived wrapper set, three-rung control ladder, structural closure argument bounding the type exclusions, and the struct-field forwarding path stated as an open hole rather than chased. The two real create_session findings it reports remain unfixed and unruled.

The identifier-cleanup property is 'a durable surface names an ephemeral artifact'. Prose expresses that with no path in it, so a path-literal sweep cannot close the class - nine such prose pointers survived a sweep that had certified their files clean. Authorized fixing them plus one dead rendered link in a tracked design doc; deferred functional runtime string literals (verifying a change needs Docker, and no reader follows a session name to a missing file) and live links whose target exists (nothing dangles; only the target's filename carries an identifier).

Recording forward rather than editing the plan: the verification criterion requiring that no milestone/session/planning identifier appear in any source file, comment, test name or commit message is UNMET and partly UNMEETABLE. Frozen applied migrations make part of it permanently unsatisfiable, and the criterion is worded around a marker while the operational harm is dangling references - so it is both too narrow to see the real sites and broad enough to attach phantom costs to sites it does see.

Capturing forward: the recorded switch-collapsing gateway-owner accessor does NOT cover the lite create-session path's ContainerRuntime registration. That mechanism presupposes a uid already present in the call expression; this site passes none, so there is no argument to reroute - the accessor is the wrong shape there, not merely unapplied. Worse, the flagged expression never reads the route field, so routing it through an accessor would turn the check green while leaving the 13 sites that actually consume the route untouched. Whatever gets scheduled, 'the check is green' is not the observation that settles it.

The two flagged gateway-owner sites differ in kind. The non-lite one is unreachable on macOS (an earlier return fires on the same condition) and the owner-uid concept does not exist on Linux, so it has no uid to get wrong on either platform. Keeping it flagged anyway as a tripwire: the conclusion depends on that early return, and a carve-out would have to encode a reachability fact the checker cannot verify and that would rot silently. Accepted cost - the checker exits nonzero on a clean tree permanently and cannot become a CI gate as-is; revisit that trade only if promotion is proposed.

Bounded the dead-pointer cleanup: finish the ruled sites, then take the prose-vocabulary sweep as a MEASUREMENT and stop. Remainder becomes a todo, not a commit. Rationale - the class has been redefined three times and each redefinition was correct, which is exactly how a detour made of justified steps becomes unbounded. The harm (a reader follows a pointer and finds nothing) is mild and does not worsen with time, while the cost of chasing it grows with every honest correction to the predicate. Stopping rule is 'we know the size of what remains', not 'the class is closed'.

Resolved the dead-pointer property: trackedness and ephemerality are two different questions on two timescales. Trackedness decides whether a reader fails today; ephemerality decides whether the pointer is permitted at all, and per the governing convention it is the one that governs. So a pointer to a TRACKED spec must still be deleted-and-inlined, not given a path - the opposite prescription would introduce a convention violation. Both properties happen to yield the same edit, which is why the wrong reason went undetected.

The 82-site figure is retired as a denominator for the conversion work. Re-running the identical script on todays tree gives 15, but 49 of the 67-site drop is one class whose zero is a respelling artifact, and both runs came from an instrument blind to 45.9 percent of its own scope (a whole-file cutoff at the first cfg(test), hiding 5758 production lines in three files). Progress against this work is not measurable as a fraction of 82; classes must be tracked separately or not at all.

Replan deferred rather than performed. The newly measured scope (impermissible references, tidiness labels, the lite route shape) cannot be turned into a session count without two decisions that are not mine to make: what criterion the tidiness class should be held to, and which of three shapes the lite route fix takes. Replanning to a fabricated total and revising it immediately is worse than leaving the plan honest and the work in todos.

Adopting the construction-time route-resolver shape for the container runtime, on the ground that its crux is settled by an existing compiled instance of the same daemon-supplied-closure mechanism between the same two crates rather than by argument, and that the alternative puts a Docker concept on a trait two of whose three impls have no Docker. Closed-op-set check passes: no broker op gains a field, only which uid an existing typed route value names.

On the checker class whose two violations would survive a correct fix: not silencing them with carve-outs, and not re-basing the regex onto the route property, because the daemon uid is three hops from every use site and no pattern over a call expression can reach it. Instead narrowing the class name to the property it actually detects, a handler reaching a startup-owned singleton, which is true and useful on its own. The gap that caused this whole error was a name broader than its patterns; widening the patterns is structurally impossible here, so the honest close is narrowing the name. Consequence: the route invariant loses its static guard and must move into a behavioural test, which makes switch-on coverage a blocking prerequisite rather than a deferred item.

Ruling on the prose sweep after a delegate measured my criterion wrong in three places. Accepting its correction that identifiers are outside the rule entirely, on the ground that editing an image tag or a function parameter changes behaviour, which is a different exemption from a label that is simply a true local reference. Widening the ephemeral-tracker-reference bucket from its proxy census to the full measured population, because leaving three quarters undone would read as done to the next reader. Splitting the phase-label class into its own later pass, since spelling does not predict class and each site needs a read.

Ruled that a third file may be edited despite a delegation prompt and a handoff verification criterion both naming two, on the ground that the criterion was a prediction of the diff written before anyone counted and has since been measured wrong twice. A verification criterion that is really an unmeasured prediction loses to a measurement.

Narrowed the missing-operator-uid hard error on the container runtime to VM-hosted runtimes only, rather than erroring uniformly. A uniform error would have failed 29 create/start sites across 7 Linux-only integration suites that pass no identity, none of which can be executed on this host. On a host-routed runtime the route factory discards the uid, so demanding one adds a failure mode with no route consequence. Accepted that this moves safety on the macOS path from a check in the code onto an enumeration of call sites that stamp the identity.

The remedy for a wrong document pointer in source depends on where the target lives, not on whether the pointer resolves. A target under the ephemeral work-scaffolding tree must have its content inlined and the pointer deleted, because repairing it yields a correct link to a file scheduled to stop existing. A target under the shipped docs tree may be repointed, preferring a named section anchor.

Diagnostic remediation text will be moved from a string field into a dedicated type so that a bare platform-specific command literal fails to typecheck, and that type must never gain a From<&str> impl, which would re-open the hole as a convenience. Cheap because the outcome type carries no serde and is referenced in a single source file, so there is no wire, schema or on-disk consequence.

A test scanning rendered remediation text for platform-command tokens is refused: it passes today while a known member of the class stays broken, because that member names no platform command at all. A guard green over the defect it was written to catch is worse than none, since its presence closes the question.

The update-failure recovery text will iterate the backup set rather than restating its membership. The defect is two hand-maintained enumerations of one set with only one of them platform-branched; iterating buys by construction the property that every file the recovery text names was actually backed up, closing the backup-omission finding from the other side.

AUTHORITATIVE, supersedes a ruling issued only by message. Comment-citation cleanup: the locator-less 'the design says X' attributions are NOT an authorial idiom and must not be scoped as one. They are residue from a single 2026-05-23 bulk edit that stripped spec section references from 183 files, deleting named anchors while PRESERVING line numbers — the exact inversion of the cite-by-anchor rule. A later repair commit patched the amputations by RECONSTRUCTING document names, so some document names now in comments were invented by a machine and read as authoritative. Rulings: (1) corrupted comment fragments are fixed unconditionally, no policy question; (2) the deleted anchors are recovered from the original diff as SOURCE MATERIAL for writing an inlined constraint, never restored as pointers, since the targets are ephemeral; (3) machine-reconstructed document names are their own class and must be identified separately from authored ones; (4) size the job from a measured sample before committing to the full set.

Sequencing: the todo about stating the broker-gate dependency at both docker arms is NOT independent work and must not be dispatched yet. It is gated on the in-flight check of whether the new commit ever puts the daemon on the local docker arm while holding an operator uid. If it does, the gate stops being an untraversed condition and becomes a boundary that runs, which changes the fix from documentary to urgent and changes what review it needs. Dispatching it now would settle that question by whoever reaches it first.

The container runtime and the HTTP proxy must resolve their docker route from one function rather than from two that agree. A comment in the proxy currently reads the two paths agreeing as evidence both are correct, when one takes a raw operator uid correctly and the other requires a collapsed one; agreement between two independently-written paths is the property that rots first. The mechanism is to be proposed with justifying call sites rather than guessed.

The lite-image rebuild gate lands daemon-side rather than client-side, because an endpoint exists and does the wrong thing; the client-side precedent it resembles is a disanalogy, refusing there only because no endpoint exists. For the all-backends default the ruling is neither of the two options offered: the axis is whether a user learns the lite image was not rebuilt, so an all-backends run may skip the container arm only if the skip is visible in normal output, and otherwise must fail rather than skip silently.

Ruled that a session row carrying no operator attribution splits by WHEN the null appears, not by inspecting the row: a post-migration startup count with an explaining message covers the operator-caused cases, and the per-request internal error covers the genuine daemon defect.

Ruled that spec-anchor citations removed by the bulk edit are neither restored nor merely deleted: the remedy is to inline the fact the reference stood for, which two prior commits already established as precedent. Tracked-in-git is presence, not durability.

A durable surface referencing an ephemeral planning artifact is repaired by inlining the constraint into the durable surface, never by restoring the link. Deleting the sentence is correct only where a reader loses nothing.

Comments describing the served-row behaviour are gated until two measurements land: what the wrong-uid route resolved to concretely, and whether the path is reachable outside a test. Writing to the strong reading before measuring would produce the promise-formatted-as-description defect this session has been excavating.

Repairs to durable surfaces that referenced ephemeral planning artifacts inline the content in place rather than restoring or deleting a pointer; correct under either resolution of whether those artifacts are tracked, so it needs no ruling to proceed.

When a change adds a violation that a checker's stated steady-state rationale does not cover, the repair is a strictly non-permissive annotation recording that the new site is unjustified — never an allowlist, never renaming the read to defeat a spelling check, never rewriting the rationale to bless it.

Ratified the doc-write bar for the macOS failure baseline: write a claim only if it can be re-checked from the code alone. Rationale is asymmetric correction — a doc is consulted instead of re-measuring, and filing product-as-harness licenses a permanent marker while harness-as-product self-corrects in one commit.

Approved substituting the correctly-resolved operator uid at all ten defaulting call sites plus the rotted justification comment, in one commit with the two risk classes in separate hunks. Deciding factor: one site persists the wrong answer to the store rather than only returning it.

Withdrew my own class-B partition figure rather than reconciling it against the delegate's. I could not produce its derivation or scope, which makes it a record of a measurement rather than a measurement; a documented derivation supersedes an unrecoverable one outright.

Ruled that stripped spec citations are restored as prose with the citation dropped, not with the anchor reinstated. The targets resolving today does not license the reference: the prohibition rests on those artifacts being deleted later, and a live link is indistinguishable from a soon-to-be-dead one by any present-tense observation.

Rejected a blanket redo of the earlier repair commit in favour of a comparison pass. A restore-from-pre-image redo would reinstate the very citations the sweep was right to remove; only sites whose replacement asserts something the pre-image did not need action.

Confirmed the citation ruling is unaffected by repository state, because it never rested on it: the prohibition follows from stated policy about future availability, not from whether the tree is tracked, ignored, or force-added. Tested the opposite reading of the gitignore evidence and found it fits equally well, so it moves nothing either way.

Ruled that a false claim in an unamendable commit message obliges correction on the editable surface that a reader reaches from it: quote the frozen sentence verbatim, state what the artifact actually establishes, and give the condition under which the stronger claim would hold. Rewriting shared history to repair prose is disproportionate; leaving it uncorrected is not an option either.

Two commits landed with swapped authorship (a comment-repair message carrying an 11-file cross-crate rename; a rename message carrying another agent's uid work). Ruling: leave the history, do not rebase — rewriting a branch four agents are committing to risks losing real work to fix a record whose content is correct. Correct forward instead.

Bare git commit is banned team-wide and commits now serialize through the lead: request a token, commit, verify, report, release. The emptiness guard issued earlier is insufficient by construction — it closes the window between your own stage and commit, not the window between your stage and another agent's commit, which is the same length and not under your control.

Applied migrations V004/V006 had their comments edited by the bulk comment commit, which diverges refinery's checksum and would abort daemon startup on any database that applied them earlier. Ruled: do not restore the comments — restoring repairs a possibly-empty population and breaks every database created since. Remains a release-contract question for the user.

The nullable-uid doc corrections in session.rs and guest.rs land as one commit rather than two, since both describe the same subject; the separate record-correction commit is a different kind of artifact and stays separate. Replace the six-locator example list with a statement of the three dispositions: refuse for anything that mutates or locates a runtime, report for health, skip for read-only enrichment.

Repair order inverted for the damaged-comment sweep: silent net-deletion sites take priority over typographically self-announcing ones, since the latter recruit any future reader into noticing them and the former do not.

Lite-image rebuild fix approved after the premise it was first ruled on turned out to be wrong; the daemon gets a platform branch returning a notice, the CLI prints the daemon body instead of a hardcoded string, and the notice text is a pure function so it is testable off-platform. Only the host-side topology half is measurable here; the in-VM half stays explicitly unmeasured.

A dangling commit carrying substantial abandoned work from a prior session is reachable only via ORIG_HEAD, which the next reset or rebase overwrites. Authorized preserving it with a tag: additive, local, reversible, and it prevents an irreversible loss. Whether that work returns is the user's call at the milestone boundary.

Memory-index compaction stays with the orchestrator and no delegate edits the memory directory. Two grounds: a hook that fires on the orchestrator's tool calls is aimed at the orchestrator and is not an assignment to whoever reads it, and a read-merge-write pass over a file under concurrent append silently drops entries written between the read and the write - a data loss with no diff and no failing test. Also ruled: a delegate standing down returns work to the orchestrator and cannot transfer ownership to a peer.

A scope stated in a message and dropped from the artifact is the recurring failure and it happened again: an agent correctly reported that a blob cannot discriminate between two mechanisms, then wrote the stronger mechanism claim into a durable memory note carrying only a population-size caveat. Ruled: the note records what the blob establishes and marks the mechanism undetermined with what would settle it. If the object turns out to be a deliberate probe, the hazard has zero observed instances rather than one, so the near-miss rate readers were told to reason about would have no numerator.

The shared-mechanism claim across the recovered findings is stated as a bounded population, not a closed one: three named and examined, one further label referenced but unrecovered. Guessing the missing member would produce a class that is an artifact of the guess.

Verdict accepted as two mechanisms rather than one: a conjunctive acceptance condition with no owning predicate, which each consumer reimplements as whichever subset was locally cheap; and separately a branch taken on the wrong axis. Collapsing them into one sentence would have left the second unfixed.

Re-verifying falsely-closed sites outranks repairing known-live ones. A pending item survives neglect; a wrongly-closed one leaves every future queue permanently, including its own author's. Cheap-and-invalidating beats expensive-and-additive.

A negative verdict from a search may no longer stand alone: closing a site now requires positive evidence of repair, not absence of evidence of damage. Both instruments run and disagreements are the finding; replacing one matcher with another only relocates the blind spot.

Repair order set: partition the bare markers by provenance against the damage commit's parent first, then the net-deletion sites, then re-localize the undecidable class as it shrinks. The policy-violation population and the operator-visible program data are held for the user. Rationale: misfiling in-scope damage as out-of-scope debt removes it from every queue exactly as a wrong clean verdict does.

The proposed migration-time owner for the users.conf post-condition is held for the user despite being the right fix shape: it turns on a design question about what the CLI takes as the daemon uid, the bug it closes was demonstrated latent rather than live, and adding an abort path to a migration is a new upgrade-time failure mode that lands on top of an already-open release-contract question.

The single-writer rule for the memory directory stands, but on coherence grounds rather than the lost-update mechanism I originally gave. Exact-string edits cannot serialize a stale whole-file buffer, so my stated justification was refuted; the rule survives because concurrent authorship produces competing framings of one lesson, which is the failure actually observed.

Prohibited the private-GIT_INDEX_FILE + commit-tree + update-ref commit route for all delegates on this shared tree; path-scoped commit plus a reset of the same path is the only sanctioned form. The isolation the low-level route buys is already provided by a path-scoped commit, while its costs are not: update-ref overwrites the reflog's standard commit-subject line, which is the only per-object record of how a commit was created and the instrument an attribution investigation depends on, and omitting the update-ref loses the work with no error anywhere.

Amended the shared-tree commit protocol after measurement showed the previous wording was itself unsafe: the cleanup pathspec is mandatory (bare reset unstages peers), a porcelain index-column check is required before naming any path (a peer's staged path commits under the caller's authorship with no warning), and a narrow carve-out permits one and-chained add-then-commit solely to introduce a new file, since the sanctioned route cannot create one.

The per-gateway-owner orphan sweep stays macOS-gated. The property its tests pin — one pass per distinct gateway owner — presupposes an operator-to-owner mapping Linux does not have, since lite resources there sit on the host Docker daemon swept once. Absent property, not a coverage loss; the premise is now recorded at the definition with the condition that would reverse it.

Three gateway-naming todos are deferred as blocked by design rather than by effort. The agent-side gateway-create constant cannot be renamed alone - the daemon still creates and starts the gateway through its own direct path under the unsuffixed name, so renaming one half without the sender makes the two halves address different instances. The gateway manager's caller-supplied Lima home is unreachable until the registry has a reader. And exercising the per-operator switch end to end is now unblocked at the code level, but the remaining half is a live run against a gateway VM, not an edit.

Made the per-owner gateway-manager registry the single source of GatewayLimaManager instances, rather than converting readers one at a time off the startup singleton. Because the slot-to-NIC cache lives in the instance, two managers over identical inputs are not interchangeable, so any partial conversion silently breaks the readers it moves. Startup now readies the manager it takes from the registry and the AppState singleton is removed; background and recovery paths select by an owner uid they already hold. Workspace tests match the pre-change baseline.

Documented the logged-out delta on the durable guides (hardening's security-trade-offs section plus a new operations section on the login prerequisite), and deliberately did NOT add it to the older macOS spec's known-deltas list: that spec is an ephemeral artifact and editing it after the fact is chasing intent backward. The durable surfaces are what the criterion is about.
discoveries: The daemon-side singleton surface changed phrasing rather than shrinking: socket-path resolution now goes through the Docker route field. A sweep built on the old socket accessor or the name constant reports 4 sites and would conclude the work nearly done; the real surface is 82.

The store-open Docker orphan scan runs before the agent broker socket is even bound, so no check-in or logout state can exist at that point. Its defect is that a bare docker invocation reaches the host daemon rather than the one inside the gateway VM.

There are two persisted operator-uid hints on a session, not one: a session column stamped from the socket peer credentials at create time, and the network record's routing hint. The recon and the network field's own doc-comment both assert the network record is the only one, which is false.

The gateway-owner accessor reads the current process uid when the switch is off, which is only the daemon's uid if the daemon is the caller. The CLI links the same crate and runs as the operator, so it would get operator identity with the switch off. Nothing enforces the precondition, and the sibling Lima-home helper carries the identical unstated one.

A must-use domain enum does not force the residual case to be handled: the attribute does not fire on an if-let scrutinee, so a one-liner discards the unresolved arm with no diagnostic. Type-level unlosability is an overclaim; the real guarantee has to be a conservation property asserted where the partition happens.

The network record's operator uid is authoritative rather than merely fresher: the macOS Lima start path stamps it with the same uid it just claimed the vmnet slot under, so the hint and the live resource cannot disagree. This is the reason the reversed precedence is right, stronger than the staleness argument that motivated it.

The must-use attribute is also silent on a match carrying a wildcard arm, not just on if-let. Any future proposal to make a residual case unlosable by choice of return type should assume match is not a safe harbour either.

The startup reaper was fail-open: when the session list could not be read it logged that it was skipping the pass but handed both reapers an empty live set, which asserts that no session exists and would have made every live session's container, volume, network and VM look orphaned. Fixed to genuinely skip.

An admit-triggered reaper pass would be unsafe as a straight copy of the reconcile-on-check-in precedent: both reapers read the live-session set first and enumerate host resources second, which is harmless only because they run before the socket is bound. With the API live, a session created between the snapshot and the listing would have its resources classified as orphaned and deleted. The reconcile path is safe under the same ordering only because it acts on already-running sessions.

The claim that the recovery guard and the bounded-recovery helper are generic over the latch is false as written: both are concretely typed. It happens to hold only because a per-owner map keeps the same value type; a set-of-recovering-owners spelling would have forced both signatures to change.

Adversarial review of the reaper check-in gate cleared its central safety argument by measurement: the reaper still sits between the live-session read and the API socket bind in both revisions, so the TOCTOU that justified refusing an admit-triggered pass does not apply to the pass that landed.

The reaper's swept set was verified across all four platform-x-backend cells: both Linux cells byte-identical, Lima-on-macOS strictly narrower, Docker-on-macOS identical with the switch off and deliberately wider with it on. The commit message's unqualified 'nothing new becomes reapable' is false only in that last cell, which is the feature itself; the in-code docs carry the correct scope.

The Lima and Docker per-operator reapers disagree on platform gating: the Docker one is macOS-gated at both definition and re-export, the Lima one is unconditional. The check-in reachability premise that makes per-operator sweeping safe holds only on macOS, so the ungated Lima entry point would silently narrow to the daemon alone if ever wired on Linux.

Phrase greps miss doc-comment prose in this repo because rustfmt wraps sentences across line breaks, so no single-line pattern spans them. A sweep for an overclaim's own wording came back complete and was not: two further copies surfaced only on a multi-line search. Any claim sweep over Rust doc comments must be line-break tolerant.

The Linux Lima helper gates on its target uid, not only its caller: the requested uid must be non-zero, resolve through the passwd database, and hold sandbox-group membership before setresuid. A doc sentence asserting the opposite was drafted and corrected in-flight. Both target checks read host configuration rather than runtime liveness, which is what actually distinguishes them from the macOS check-in set.

Warning an implementer that fix-forward commits are where the next overclaim gets written caused it to catch and correct its own, mid-batch, and to drop a second-order overclaim from the replacement draft. First in-flight self-catch of this pattern in the phase.

Independent verification of the correction batch: the privileged-helper gating sentence is accurate — all three target gates exist in the stated order and strictly before the single setresuid call site. Two of the four claims still carried an incompleteness in the correcting sentence itself, found only by a pass that did not read the author's reasoning.

A claim about where a version floor is enforced named two sites and missed a third, which is the only blocking one: the shell installer refuses to proceed below the floor. The author swept Rust because it was editing Rust, so the strongest enforcement site was invisible. Enforcement crosses language boundaries and the strongest site is often outside the language under edit.

The macOS check-in set is not purely a liveness fact: peer classification rejects root, floors the uid, and requires sandbox-group enrollment before admitting. So it is host-configuration AND liveness, the same category it was being contrasted against. The contrast is not false but reads as exclusive, and the universal it supports overclaims in the same direction.

Warning an implementer about fix-forward overclaims produced a self-catch but not immunity: the same batch still shipped two further wrong claims that only an independent pass found. The warning is worth keeping and is not a substitute for verification.

My briefing asserted the recorded reason for the latch asymmetry was a race. Measured false: the commit says no such thing, and the actual recorded reason is a key-versus-route mismatch. The distinction decides the question, because a race argument would have been invalidated by sharding the session list while a key-route argument survives it. Paraphrasing the reason changed the claim, not just its scope.

Gateway recovery previously engaged the latch before listing sessions, so a failed list engaged and released it; the list now happens in the daemon and a failure returns before any latch is engaged. The window was one synchronous database call against a ten-second poll, so nothing can observe it.

The model-pin dispatch failure reaches nested subagents. A delegate that spawns its own helper hits the same credit error because the override requirement lives only in the orchestrator's context. Delegation prompts must carry the requirement forward, otherwise a delegate silently loses whichever check it tried to delegate.

A comment claiming that an operator directory for a uid no longer in the passwd database fails in a fast name-service lookup before touching the filesystem was measured false in both halves: directory creation is the first statement, and the only name-service lookup happens afterwards inside a macOS-only block, while the Linux branch resolves nothing at all and says so.

The verification pass cited those same lines as evidence that the tree already recognised the unreachable-operator class. The cited evidence was itself a false claim. The conclusion survived on different grounds, but grounding a verdict in an in-tree comment verifies nothing — it moves the unverified claim one hop.

Regrouping a short enumeration into 'the one that blocks' plus 'the rest that do not' turns the rest clause into a fresh unmeasured universal. Caught in draft: two remaining version-floor sites were about to be described as reporting rather than blocking, but the template's declared minimum makes Lima itself refuse the instance at start.

The limactl version floor has three enforcement sites that stop different things: the installer refuses to install, the gateway template makes Lima refuse the instance at start, and the doctor check renders a row and stops nothing. Startup compares no versions at all; the only version read feeds the diagnostics payload.

Deriving recovery shards from the session list leaves the per-operator mode with zero shards when every session is declined or absent, and the gateway restart is reachable only from inside the per-shard loop. A crashed gateway is then never rebuilt while its trigger keeps re-firing. This is the same property the shared mode was deliberately given and the per-operator arm silently lacks.

The in-code defence for that gap argues from a per-owner monitor that does not exist in this tree. The monitor that does exist is the one that would spin. A comment can rest on infrastructure that was planned rather than built, and reviewing the comment against the design rather than the tree passes it.

The interval justifying the recovery ordering delta is misstated in the code: the reader polls every thirty seconds in the gateway monitor, while the ten-second figure belongs to the separate trigger loop. The conclusion holds more strongly than written, but it names the wrong loop.

An honest source for the carried owner set exists: the agent broker's connected-uid set is live, populated by check-in and already consumed by reconcile, and the executor fails every operator-uid Lima op without a checked-in agent while the daemon's own uid runs directly. The gateway manager registry is dead code with no enumeration and cannot serve.

The review's account of the misstated interval was wrong about both the site and the defect. No such comment was added by the commits under review. The only in-code claim of that kind is pre-existing and its error is different: it says a failed restart retries on the next trigger tick, but the failure counter is zeroed immediately before the call, so the earliest retry is three ticks.

A failed gateway recovery is not retried at all on three of its four post-start error exits, because all three are reached only after the container daemon answers. The monitor's next probe then succeeds, the failure counter is zeroed, and the sessions the run marked degraded stay that way indefinitely. Found by measuring a comment that asserted a retry delay, not by testing behaviour.

The operations guide now documents a remedy for a field that is structurally always empty in this build: production uses shared ownership, whose arm returns an empty decline list unconditionally without consulting either resolver. The spec row authorising the field says as much in its own text.

A commit message describing a comment it corrected used the singular where two such comments exist, and the untouched one still carries the wrong claim. Definite articles assert uniqueness in exactly the way bare quantifiers do, and nothing in a diff review surfaces the copy that was not edited.

A test named for waiting a full threshold of probes before retry passes with the reset ordering inverted, so it pins arithmetic over two constants rather than the ordering its name claims. The defect it was written to prevent can be reintroduced without turning it red.

The gateway VM's eth0 nftables table is host-namespace hardening, not session-egress policy: it declares only output and input chains, no forward chain, and exempts every non-eth0 path. Sandbox egress is re-originated by the gateway container and traverses forwarding and container NAT, which this table deliberately does not touch. A failed application is a blast-radius regression on the VM's own processes, not an egress-enforcement gap.

My escalation gate was built on a doc-comment that overstates: it says a failed eth0 ruleset leaves the uplink forwarding whatever it is handed, invisibly from inside the sandbox. Read against the generator eight hundred lines below, that table never governed container egress at all. I set a security trigger from prose rather than from the ruleset it describes.

My claim that a recovery latch prevents overlapping runs was wrong in mechanism while right in conclusion: the recovery entry point has a single caller inside a sequential loop, so overlap is impossible by loop construction, and the latch exists to stop the monitor fighting a run already in progress. Twice in one batch I asserted a true conclusion from a false mechanism, and a delegate acting on the mechanism rather than the conclusion would have built the wrong fix both times.
