Nearly half the backlog was filed by one session, which is a signal about todo-filing discipline rather than about the codebase: a cluster that looks like a standing theme may be an artifact of a single session's local view, and volume should not be read as importance.

Read confirms nothing inside the gateway container installs nftables rules: the entrypoint, both logger crates and the CoreDNS plugin contain zero invocations (checked at low matching strength - 34 case-insensitive hits, all binary names, log strings and prose). The loggers are consumers of rules written by the daemon. So the restart finding stands on two independent legs: the kernel discards the ruleset (measured) and nothing in the image restores it (read).

The container's HEALTHCHECK script runs five probes - Envoy ready, a mitmdump process check, CoreDNS health and two logger health endpoints - and none inspects nftables, so all five pass against an empty ruleset. Docker's cached verdict is what the daemon's gateway monitor branches on, and re-creation is reachable only from NotRunning or Unhealthy. The re-injection path is correct; the condition that would call it is unobservable to the only thing that calls it.

The lite session container and the gateway container are created with OPPOSITE restart policies - no-restart for the session container, restart-unless-stopped for the gateway. A bare grep for the flag returns both sites, and a test asserting the no-restart form quoted without its enclosing function would support either answer with equal confidence. The discriminators are the surrounding arguments, not the flag name.

Lima's dns config key is subordinate to the host resolver being disabled, not an independent switch - its own shipped documentation says the dns rules apply only when hostResolver.enabled is false. So it cannot suppress the DNS redirect while the host resolver is on. The emitted gateway template sets eleven top-level keys and none touches DNS or the resolver; the only DNS-touching emissions in the repo target session guest VMs, pointing them at the gateway container.

A generated config file found on disk is evidence about the generator version that produced it, not about the generator in the tree. The gateway VM's on-disk Lima config is stale - it lacks a networks key that today's generator emits. Reading the artifact instead of the generator is a trap I walked a delegate into by asking it to read what the daemon emits; it avoided it by reading both and labelling which was which.

Correction to an earlier characterization of the gateway VM DNS defect: it is not that all DNS from the VM host namespace breaks. The redirect is qualified by destination, so a query aimed at any other resolver on port 53 is never rewritten and works today. What breaks is DNS via the Lima host resolver, which is what the guest's resolver uses by default - so every ordinary lookup. The defect's rank is unchanged; its blast radius is narrower and more specific.

Image provisioning is inspect-then-build, never inspect-then-pull, and both image repositories are bare local names that Docker resolves into the official-images namespace where they cannot exist. So every implicit pull under Docker's default policy is guaranteed to fail - slowly, and with a message about registry authentication rather than the missing image. Passing the never-pull flag converts that into the exact error string the code's own comment already promises.

Creation-time readiness and steady-state health are two different probe surfaces in the gateway lifecycle: the creation path runs per-component docker exec probes and never reads Docker's HEALTHCHECK verdict, which is consumed only by the monitor. So adding a rule assertion to the container healthcheck cannot deadlock against the daemon's first injection - the hazard I raised does not exist, for a structural reason rather than a timing one.

A latent coupling between two constants nothing ties together: the component-readiness timeout is 45 seconds while Docker's clock to unhealthy is a 30-second start period plus three ten-second retries. Roughly fifteen seconds of margin between a Rust constant and a Dockerfile directive, neither mentioning the other. Inert today because nothing on the creation path reads the health verdict; it becomes live the moment anyone asserts on the DNAT tables in the healthcheck.

Policy expressiveness differs by platform on the DNS-resolve axis. On macOS the gateway's DNS server is pointed at three fixed public resolvers, so an internal host is not resolvable by construction; on Linux it forwards through Docker's embedded resolver to the daemon host's resolvers, where an internal name does resolve if the host knows it. The comment justifying the macOS choice guarantees that it never weakens deny - true, and the security axis - while saying nothing about the resolve axis it closed off.

The Lima DNS redirect has symmetric UDP and TCP appends against the same destination, so the baseline's TCP accept was defeated by exactly the mechanism that defeats the UDP one. The defect's blast radius does not grow - it had only ever been described on one protocol. The chosen fix covers both for a statable reason rather than by luck: the redirect rewrites address and port but never the transport protocol, so one pre-redirect tuple match spans both.

An append-only working document is a generated artifact whose early sections were generated against an older tree. A correction made in a late section had propagated backwards into an earlier one written before it, and one function carried three different line spans across the document, each correct on the day it was written. Both are invisible to the only reading anyone performs - forward, once. Correcting a claim means sweeping backwards for the phrasing, not just forwards for the conclusion.

Gateway ruleset loss after a container restart partially self-heals: the first allowed DNS query reinstalls the dnat and policy tables in full, leaving only the deny-all base table missing. A later casual re-check therefore sees two of three tables present and would refute a true finding — the absent base table is the only diagnostic observation.

On macOS with the container backend, gateway recovery is a missing call rather than a missing capability: the correct repair is the macOS lite gateway setup path alone, not teardown followed by setup, because setup does not re-create the lite bridge that teardown removes.

The chosen DNS fix lands in the gateway VM's own nftables policy, not the gateway container's ruleset. So it does nothing for the container-restart rule loss — two defects on two surfaces that have been travelling together only because they surfaced together.

Check-mode nftables validation cannot test the semantic claim the fix rests on — that the pre-DNAT destination is visible at the filter hook downstream of the nat hook. A rule that loads cleanly and matches nothing is the exact failure to avoid and is indistinguishable from success under that instrument.

The new nftables comment asserting that every image arrives by local load is true only because the same diff adds an explicit never-pull flag at four call sites. Comment and flag are mutually load-bearing and must ship in one commit; splitting them naively lands a false assertion in an egress-policy file until the second commit arrives.

Everything newly added to the Lima gateway module is gated to macOS, so a Linux CI run exercises none of the new predicate and none of its eighteen tests. Only the four ungated argv tests in the docker-argv crate get Linux coverage.

An explicit never-pull flag on container create and run is the direct remedy for the previously retracted claim that no production path can trigger an implicit registry pull. The work reads as unrelated to its brief but is not unrelated to this investigation.

The claim that a sandboxed workload could reach Envoy's admin interface is retracted: the policy compiler emits an admin socket bound to loopback. The read went to the config generator rather than to two prose hits describing it, since the config is supplied at runtime rather than baked into the image.

The gateway's base table does not keep its create-time deny-all contents: a later function flushes the input chain and replaces it with an opened set, and another does the same to forward. Reasoning about steady-state contents from the creating function was wrong, and most of what was called newly exposed after a restart was already open.

After correction the input-path loss is small and specific: an unauthenticated liveness endpoint becomes reachable from the VM subnet, and the real cost is losing the trailing reject as a default-deny stance for any port a future component binds non-loopback. The link-local and IPv6 drops live in a self-healing table and are not losses.

A pre-registered outcome table can misclassify the success signature: two counters reading different fields of the same packet are not mutually exclusive, so the predicted result was written down as instrument failure. Exclusivity must live within a pair, over one quantity with rival values.

Pre-register counts and ratios rather than booleans when a degenerate path could produce the same firing — an inert conntrack subsystem makes ct-original match anyway, so a boolean rig would confirm the hypothesis for the wrong reason.

The candidate DNS-fix ruleset loads on the target nftables/kernel pair and the kernel round-trips the conntrack-original expression unchanged, verified in a hookless chain with a positive control. That establishes loadability and expression validity, not that the rule matches the intended traffic.

Content-free idle notifications are not liveness evidence in either direction; they fired while the agents were mid-work and again while children were outstanding. Transcript mtime is the cheap direct measurement, but it establishes activity only, not that the agent is answering the message just sent.

Three of four items I held as outstanding were already complete and one was a phantom whose premise I had personally retired. A compaction preserves an item's topic label and drops its resolution status, so completed and open items re-enter the queue indistinguishable. Re-measure status across a context boundary, not just quantities.

A wrong belief encoded twice in different structures is immune to reference-following: the misfiled pin and a separately-authored residual expectation of 17 share a belief, not a reference, so fixing one leaves the check red and the redness reads as a new problem. Grep the value and its consequences, not the identifier.

Denominator reporting per regex alternative exposed a dead check half: one alternative matched nothing at either revision because the real spelling nests through an accessor. Unaccounted-for zeros now print ZERO, UNEXPLAINED rather than reading as clean.

The lite image path is not uniformly docker-load-from-tarball: ensure_image and rebuild_lite_image build with docker build on the host-Docker path. A comment asserting 'every image arrives by docker load' was false as a universal and had already been repeated as established before being caught.

Backlog triage denominators: 236 items classified from full filed text, 42 opened against source, 194 on the filer's word. Verdict flipped on 3/42 (7%), refined on 5/42. The 42 were selected as most likely to have decayed, so ~5% already-fixed is a ceiling for the 194, not an estimate. Two axes unmeasured: doc-drift items that rot by citation rather than by claim, and cross-checking against open GitHub issues.

Measured on kernel 6.8.0-117-generic, at filter hook OUTPUT priority 0, downstream of a dstnat-priority DNAT in the same namespace: 'ct original ip daddr' and 'ct original proto-dst' yield the pre-DNAT destination. Corroborated independently by conntrack -L reading the original tuple out of the kernel's own structure, sharing no mechanism with the nft counters. Scope is that hook and that kernel, not the gateway VM generally.

A ct-state-new DNS gate rule matches only the first packet of a flow; every later original-direction packet reads established and is excluded. It is correct only because the chain's baseline accept for established,related sits above it, and nothing at the rule's own site records that dependency. Removing or reordering that baseline silently degrades the gate to first-packet-only, breaking any resolver that reuses a source port.

A backlog ranking was contaminated by using evidence strength as a tiebreaker: the top is verified because verification lifted it there, not because the top was sampled. Of a 60-item user-facing band, 6 carry a live citation and 54 rest on the filer's word. The list is self-confirming exactly where a reader spot-checks it, and cannot surface an unopened item that would outrank the current top. Evidence status must be a separate column, never a term in the sort.

Backlog items fall into classes the severity axis has no column for: work that is unowned because it sits between areas rather than because it is low value; follow-ups whose trigger is their own success, invisible for the whole period anyone is watching; items whose conclusion survives verification while their mechanism does not, which a verdict-level check cannot see because the implementer acts on the mechanism; host-state items a commit-unit backlog can never close; and evidence rot, which is a pickup-cost dimension orthogonal to severity.

The gateway health predicate reads process liveness only across five probes, none reading nftables, so a Docker-restarted gateway container with an empty ruleset reports Healthy and the monitor's recovery arm never fires. Its own doc-comment states the licence for not reading nftables: the deny-all floor is in place from t0. That is true of a container the daemon created and false of one Docker restarted, so the predicate is correct under an invariant the restart policy silently voids.

Three independent barriers keep the restart hole open, and any one left standing keeps it open: nothing observes that a gateway netns is younger than the last injection into it, and the docker inspect format is a closed enum with no restart signal so the daemon cannot express the question; the one predicate that could carry it answers a different question; and the arm it would land in discards exactly the affected backend. Clearing only the predicate yields a monitor that detects the failure, logs a warning and continues past it every thirty seconds.

Correction to an earlier entry this session: the user-facing backlog band is 44, not 60. The 60 was asserted and never enumerated; a mechanical count gives 45 distinct IDs, minus one already fixed. So the split is 6 verified and 38 on the filer's word, not 6 and 54, and the verified fraction is 14 percent rather than 10. A related claim that 43 of the band sat in four areas was also wrong — those areas hold 24. I had already used the 60 in my own reasoning before it was corrected.

Re-sorting the backlog by claimed consequence with evidence as a separate column moved two of six opened items out as already fixed and promoted two above the previous top. The new first item is an egress bypass compiled in on macOS by a cfg attribute that removes a rejection, defended in-tree by a caller-discipline argument at a trust boundary built specifically not to trust that caller. The second is a policy-application step that lands after the VM is up and Docker is answering in both the startup and recovery paths, making the no-policy window unconditional rather than restart-triggered.

The restart hole exists on Linux too, held open by a single barrier rather than three. The gateway module carries zero target_os gates, so the health predicate and its false invariant are literally the same code on both targets; the platform branch above it changes where the probe runs, never what it asks. Barrier three is absent by construction because lite and full converge on one gateway-creation function on Linux, so the recovery arm is correctly shaped for every backend it can receive.

A checkable discriminator replaces the retracted instance: the phrase by construction is an overclaim whenever the alternative is expressible. Where a wire type carries the value and the rejecting guard is compiled out on the platform in question, the property holds by the current caller population choosing it. The census that established it is its own disproof, since a property needing fifty-seven hits across two crates and a distant early return is not one the construction enforces.

Confirmed instance of shared-cause agreement between delegates, warned about by one of them within the hour it occurred. Two independent arrivals at the same structural shape were not two measurements: neither delegate had read the site, the class framing in my own brief supplied the shape, and an instance was fitted to it and reported as a find. The reported-rather-than-measured label is what kept the retraction to one paragraph.

The milestone set is not recorded in the tracking state. The string M25 appears zero times in the whole of progress.json, yet a milestone file and its map block have been committed on disk since 2026-08-17. Tracking records session totals and the current position, never the milestone roster; milestone identity lives only in the plan documents. To find the next free milestone number, list the milestones directory - inferring it from the tracking state or from the current milestone returns a stale answer with nothing marking it stale.

Seven existing milestone files prescribe the bare cargo nextest --profile integration invocation that CLAUDE.md explicitly tells you not to use (it yields ~17 spurious failures without the test-env-override features). The documented entry point is make test-integration. This is a house habit in plan docs, not a one-off, so any exit criterion citing the bare form is self-defeating on a real Linux host.

The gitStatus block in the session prompt is a snapshot taken at conversation start, not at the current turn. Measured three commits stale in a long-compacted session, which led a subagent to report a false framing (a commit landed during this session) when the pinned sha was in fact HEAD. Measure HEAD directly whenever it is load-bearing.

The gateway monitor reads Docker's cached HEALTHCHECK verdict first and returns on Healthy, before the fuller gateway_status probe is ever called. Both run the same in-container liveness script, so they are one measurement read twice, not two independent barriers.

The restart-discards-the-ruleset link is measured, not inferred: a real gateway container was restarted three ways and the ruleset was gone in every arm. Only the control-flow conclusions about which code paths react to that are source-derived. Stating the whole area as unmeasured understates the evidence base.

On the operator agent, container inspect is answered by the inline docker handler, not the stream-class handler. A new inspect-format variant must also reach the mirrored enum in the agent's protocol module and both of its From impls, or the two sides of the broker channel drift.

The inspect-format enum's own doc-comment is headed 'Adding a variant is a security change' and states requirements for doing so. Any session planned as additive wiring that adds a variant is planned in contradiction to a warning at the site it edits, and must carry that site's requirement as scope.

Five instances in one document of the same defect: a summary of a cited section keeps half a conjunction and drops the clause that constrains it, while still reading as a faithful attribution. Every instance survived a review-plus-fix cycle by the agent that wrote it. Only re-reading each cited section against the sentence attributing to it surfaced them.

The container-scoped macOS e2e target is the one e2e target that does not take the gateway image as a prerequisite, and conftest's session-scoped preflight calls skip when the image is absent. A session-wide skip exits zero with every collected test skipped, so any gate phrased as 'nothing that passed before now fails' passes vacuously. Grade such runs on collected and passed counts, not on absence of failures.

The agent-side validation arm for container inspect binds its remaining fields with a rest pattern, so adding an inspect-format variant does not force a change there. Exhaustive matches elsewhere in that path do force one. It is the single site in the set where the two sides of the broker channel can drift silently, and it is the one a compile-failure argument must exclude.

The broker wire already carries a typed enforcement-state read, live today for the policy distributor's rollback snapshot. Its table enum names the DNAT and policy tables only; the deny-all floor is a third table with no wire representation. So neither candidate restart signal is expressible today, and either route needs a wire-shape addition agreed on both sides before anything can consume it.

In documents that cite a full path once and then continue with bare colon-line references, inserting new text that names a different file silently re-anchors every bare reference that follows it. The references still resolve, so a resolution sweep reports clean while pointing at the wrong file. Only a sweep run after the mutation catches it.

The inspect-format enum already carries a variant that reads the container PID, live and validated on the broker channel, and it changes across a restart. So a restart signal is expressible today without any wire addition. The enum's own doc-comment instructs a caller to check whether an existing variant already serves the need before adding one; a plan bullet undertook that obligation in prose and the check was never run.

The stdin-command validator passes the apply-ruleset body through uninspected beyond a size cap, reasoning that content fed to nft on stdin has no command line to protect. Because nft accepts list commands on that same input, the op is a read channel as well as a write one. Not an escalation, since a caller that can write rulesets already outranks a reader, but it means enforcement state is reachable over the existing op set.

A ruleset-presence probe must assert on the deny-all base table by exact name. The two policy-plane tables are re-rendered in full on the first allowed DNS query, so a probe asserting on them self-heals to green in exactly the broken state it exists to catch — flaky in the fail-open direction. Compounding it, the deny-all table's name is a proper prefix of both others, so any substring or grep-shaped lookup passes on a gateway that has DNAT but no deny-all floor.

With the deny-all base table absent there is no chain at the forward hook at all, and both TCP and UDP remain contained by other means. What escapes is IPv4 non-TCP/UDP, actively masqueraded. So a TCP or UDP egress probe is blocked in both the broken and the repaired state and cannot discriminate between them; run first to establish a baseline it would suggest the gap does not reproduce. Any test of this repair needs the deny-all table's presence or a non-TCP/UDP escape probe.

The container-inspect enum has six variants and every one reads current state rather than incarnation identity. Four are value-identical across a completed restart by construction. The container PID is the only difference-detector, and it fails in the fail-open direction twice over: it returns zero for a stopped container, which is also the value a failed inspect produces, so a sample taken during a stopped window compares equal later and reports no restart; and PID recycling makes equality prove nothing in general. Sameness is the direction such a predicate must be trusted in.

Two existing ops could carry the signal without adding an enum variant: the apply-ruleset stdin op, whose validator deliberately does not inspect its body, and the network-inspect op, which renders no format string and so returns full JSON that both call sites discard. Both are rejected on the same ground — each obtains the read by evading the review the closed enum exists to force, and each widens the read surface rather than narrowing it. Two independent investigations reached that principle separately.

The DNS-propagation path re-injects the two policy tables on every gate hit, which is the mechanism behind their self-healing, and it early-returns when the ruleset is empty. So the fail-open window is intermittent and policy-shape-dependent rather than persistent, and it never restores the deny-all floor. Anyone measuring blast radius or designing a reproduction has to control for DNS activity and for policy shape, or the gap will appear not to reproduce.

The degraded gateway has two distinct states and conflating them makes a test look sound when it is not. Immediately after a restart no tables exist at all and TCP egress genuinely escapes. Once the first allowed DNS query re-renders the DNAT table, TCP and UDP are contained again while the deny-all floor is still absent — and that second state is the one an observer normally finds. So an egress probe discriminates broken from repaired in the first state and not in the second, and which state a test lands in is a timing variable, not a choice.

An egress probe issued by hostname triggers a DNS lookup, and that lookup is itself the transition from the fully-degraded state to the partially-self-healed one. So the instrument converts the state it is meant to measure, and the conversion happens before the result is read. Any reproduction or regression test for this has to probe by address, or otherwise establish the state by a path that does not run the healing mechanism.

NftTable::ALL is iterated by read_nftables_state to build the policy distributor rollback snapshot. Adding a third variant to ALL would silently widen that snapshot to a table the policy plane does not manage and teardown does not delete; the existing ALL.len()==2 test is the guard, and the response on failure is to leave ALL alone rather than bump the constant. Adjacent: read_nftables_state treats a missing table as fine, which is correct for a snapshot and exactly wrong for an enforcement predicate, so it must not be reused as one.

The agent-side validation arm for the nft-table-listing op matches with a rest pattern over its table field, so a new table-enum variant passes validation with no compiler complaint - the same silent-absorption shape already documented for the container-inspect op. What does force the change is the name() exhaustive match plus both protocol From impls; neither enum is non_exhaustive.

The typed nft-table-listing op renders five argv elements with the table name taken from a closed match and no shell, so the exact-name lookup holds by construction and the substring-match trap cannot be written at that seam. This is an argument for the typed route over a healthcheck-script nft invocation, where the grep -q form is one tidy-up away and both forms exit 0 on a healthy container.

Measured instance of correction commits reintroducing the defect. Of four structural findings in the rewritten milestone document, two are defects in text the rewrite added specifically to close earlier findings: the newly added daemon-restart replay criterion grades a repair on a code path the source measured as shape-wrong for the macOS lite backend, and the newly added test-extension gate states a fail condition describing a pre-state that does not exist, because the test it extends covers one enum variant rather than the two the criterion assumes. The fixing pass is where the next overclaim gets written, and here it happened twice in one pass.

Three of the four structural findings are exit-criteria defects, and all three answer one question: what state does this criterion fail in, and does that state exist? One orders a document corrected in the direction the previous session establishes, so it grades a session on making the doc less accurate. One grades a repair on a path that is shape-wrong for the platform, while naming no platform. One names a fail condition that cannot occur. Exit criteria are a small, high-density defect population and that single question is the sharp instrument for them.

The standing decision from the source trace that a macOS lite gateway repair must call the setup routine alone and must not precede it with teardown, together with the implementer trap the trace names, is carried nowhere in the milestone document. The section is referenced exactly once, inside a verbatim quotation of a different section that merely points at it. The only review clause in the relevant session protects the Lima backend case, which is precisely the gate the trace predicts a teardown-then-setup implementation would pass. Same omission shape as the defect that forced the rewrite.

Third instance of the same defect class in one document, and this time both verification passes found it from different denominators. The source trace carries a standing decision that a macOS lite gateway repair must call the setup routine alone and must not precede it with teardown. The milestone document does not carry it, and the word teardown does not occur in the document at all. Every exit criterion in the affected session observes the deny-all table being present, and a teardown-then-setup implementation reinstalls that table - so the plan cannot distinguish the forbidden implementation from the required one, and the forbidden one passes. Fail-open verified by criteria that cannot fail, for the third time in this artifact.

The omissions pass built 46 constraints from the source and scored them: 30 carried, 3 half-carried, 12 not carried. The carried set includes everything the three earlier audits found, and the omissions are a disjoint set from them. Each pass finds a fresh disjoint set of missing constraints, which is the signature of a compressed restatement drifting from its source rather than of a document with bugs. Counted against the alternative reading: 30 of 46 carried and each missing item now individually located with section provenance is a work list, not a design failure. Fixing rather than restructuring, but with the constraint verdict column as the checklist instead of the findings prose.

A claim about where information lives can be falsified by the act of writing it elsewhere. The milestone framing said the residual acceptance lives only in the milestone document and a progress log; the same editing pass that carried that sentence forward also wrote the residual into the session plan, making the sentence false at the moment it was committed to text. Caught by the agent that did it. This is the content-level sibling of the positional case where an insertion above a citation invalidates that citation - the write moves the thing it describes, so verifying before the write is structurally insufficient. Any claim about the complete set of places something appears must be re-checked after the edit lands, not before.

The forbidden repair implementation is one copy-paste away, measured rather than supposed. The teardown-then-setup pair the source decision prohibits already exists twice inside the same macOS conditional block as the arm the session will edit, the nearer copy about eighty lines below it. That is what makes a source-level discriminator necessary rather than fussy: an implementer reaching for the nearest working example finds the prohibited shape first. It also rules out a bare occurrence count as the check, since the teardown identifier appears legitimately on several pre-existing paths - the check has to grade the arm, not the file.

The milestone document invented a prohibition and the false prohibition hid the better fix. It states that violating the standing repair decision cannot be graded by any runtime observable the milestone has, and settles for a source-level review check. Measured false: the forbidden routine logs unconditionally at info level on both entry and exit, branch-independently, the daemon defaults to info, and the session's existing replay criterion already requires reading that same log. The document reached its universal by reasoning from the damage branch's warning-level log and generalising to the whole routine. A constraint you cannot quote is invented, and this one cost a cheap runtime discriminator that catches the violation at execution instead of at review.

A plan can commission the very edit that trips its own mechanical check. One scope bullet tells the session to write a comment naming the forbidden routine at a specific match arm; a sibling exit criterion greps the diff for lines naming that routine. A compliant implementation therefore fails the check. Measured scope for the same check: seven production call sites and sixteen textual occurrences of the identifier in one file, so two of sixteen carry signal - which confirms the document was right that a bare occurrence count is not the check, and wrong that the form it chose is safe.

Third independent confirmation that the enforcement predicate cannot be bypassed, derived cold with the previous conclusion withheld, and it corrected the shape of the earlier answer rather than merely repeating it. The status function reaches the predicate on every non-failure path, so a passing container healthcheck cannot skip it. The monitor loop can skip it - the predicate is reached from exactly one of four health arms - but the two skipping arms are both named in session scope with correct locators, and the session's own replay criteria are unsatisfiable while either survives, so the closure is enforced rather than asserted. Two residuals: the unhealthy arm also bypasses but routes into recovery and is fail-closed, and a platform-specific recovery latch continues before the cached read and is disclosed as deferred.

A delegate handed a second-hand site count re-measured it and found the brief undercounted: four sites carrying a false enum-cardinality doc-comment were actually five, plus a sixth on the far side of the broker seam no prior audit had named. Exhaustive From impls force the code across that seam and force nothing about the prose, so a criterion naming only the argv crate is fully satisfiable while shipping false comments on both sides.

A punch-list item briefed as a platform-blind criterion measured out as backend-blind instead: the platform was already named and the open axis was lite-versus-full. The delegate reported the mismatch rather than forcing the framing. Both corrections this pass came from delegates re-measuring a mechanism the brief asserted, which is what the hedge-every-asserted-mechanism instruction exists to produce.

The session's own work-queue labels were phantoms, third instance of this class. Notes recorded batches 6-8 as blocked pending an implementer and a verifier; reconstruction measured that the recovery fix batch landed, both verifiers reported, and batch 6a landed. Nothing was ever waiting on a silent agent. What actually blocks the remaining batches is four undecided design questions the orchestrator owes, which no label named.

A pending scope bullet now contradicts shipped code: the batch-8 item that would change where the lite image tarball is looked up is pinned in the opposite direction by a test that landed this session, and the staging make target's path is wrong under switch-on regardless of which way it is decided. Needs a ruling before batch 8 can start rather than being implementable as written.

The sweep exit criterion's named instrument does not exist in the tree: the census script the criterion cites was never committed. Its successor is the gateway-owner invariant checker written later in the session. A criterion naming a missing instrument grades nothing, and the count it would report is the criterion's whole content.

The subagent-returned hook fires on async agent LAUNCH, not only on return, and its text asserts the subagent has returned. Combined with its standing instruction to run the progress CLI, it produces a false premise plus a prohibited action in one block. Previously logged occurrences only counted the delegate-facing pressure; the orchestrator-facing false claim is a separate defect.

Clippy is not enforced anywhere in this repo. Every clippy string under .github/ is a rustup component install, never an invocation, and the Makefile has no clippy target - only the fmt check. So the clean-clippy project convention is upheld only by whoever remembers to run it locally, which is the mechanical reason many Rust-touching commits can land unlinted. Fmt is gated; clippy is not.

A green hermetic test run over a fully-cached build certifies the source but not the build-and-exec path. When cargo reports finishing the test profile in a fraction of a second, nothing relinked, so this host's unsigned-CLI cold-exec hazard was never exercised. Treat cached-green as weaker evidence than green-after-relink and say which one was obtained. The same trap has a sharper form: a lint invocation that returns instantly is a cache replay measuring nothing, and forcing a real recheck means changing the invocation, for instance the lint level, not repeating it.

The broker check-in frame carries no version handshake by design, so a mode skew between daemon and per-operator agent is structurally unobservable at the protocol level. A mode rejection is observable via the agent name validator and its consequences via diagnostics, but the skew itself is not. This is what makes having the agent report its own ownership mode a protocol change rather than a field addition.

A decline policy for unresolvable operators is already shipped on the recovery path via report_declined_sessions. Any different policy chosen for the create and teardown paths would give the daemon two policies for one condition, so the shipped shape is the default and a deviation needs a stated reason.

Install-time staging is gateway-only: the installer stages the gateway image tarball and there is no lite staging anywhere. So a plan bullet adding a loader fallback for the lite tarball would add a fallback to a path nothing writes; the asymmetry is in the producers, not the loader.

The daemon health check already holds full session identity at every one of its six call sites, since it iterates sessions with the row in hand. A claim that the gateway owner is not derivable from the probe helper's inputs is true of the signature only, not of the call site.

The committed milestone exit criterion does not name the missing census script. It says the converted sites are verified by sweep rather than by count. The path that does not exist is cited only by a criterion inside a gitignored handoff. So the earlier concern touches two different artifacts, one committed and one not, and only the uncommitted one names a nonexistent file.

The macOS networking-status mapper returns None unless a session is both Running and Lima-backed, so a declined lite restore writes a degraded entry that never reaches the session DTO. The write is still right, but the lite decline is materially quieter than the Lima one: only the error log and diagnostics carry it.

Declining a teardown leaks a gateway container, and diagnostics reports that only while the operator stays unresolvable. That state was already reachable before this change, since a failed gateway stop is a best-effort warning, so the leak has no durable record on either path. Leak visibility is a separate concern from operator resolvability and needs its own signal.

Two pre-registered injections that revert this conversion at its two most load-bearing sites were predicted to pass with zero failures, and did. The suite structurally cannot observe the difference while the ownership switch is off: nothing builds the app state in a test, and with the switch off the per-operator route and the singleton are the same value by construction. Tests cannot be the gate for this conversion; the committed invariant checker has to be.

The workspace does not build on Linux at HEAD, pre-existing and unrelated to this conversion: the docker-argv crate is scoped to macOS in the manifest while the daemon uses it cross-platform. The failure is a name-resolution error, which aborts before type-checking — so any earlier Linux run that hit it proved nothing about the code past that point, including cfg arms this host cannot compile.

A green cross-platform build cannot distinguish 'compiled and used' from 'quietly gated out'. The discriminator is the absence of dead-code warnings naming the new functions, which is what actually shows they are live on the other platform.

The single-session health handler already answers ownership attribution two ways in one function body — one site prefers the row's uid and falls back to the caller's, the neighbouring site uses the caller's outright. The inconsistency is in the tree today, not introduced by the conversion.

The proxy module reads the singleton route but never mentions the app-state type anywhere in the file, so any census scoped to files naming that type cannot see it. That is a wrong denominator rather than a wrong filter, and it is invisible from the result: the sweep returns a clean, plausible, smaller number.

Correcting the earlier entry about the proxy module: it does not read the app-state route at all. The receiver there is a different per-request struct built from the per-operator factory, so it was an attribution site, not a missed reader — the singleton had exactly four. The wrong-denominator lesson survives but sits one hop over: a sweep keyed on a field name fixes the denominator and still cannot tell you which type you landed on, and a familiar receiver name supplies a type in the reader's head that the sweep never checked.

The macOS Lima start handler was writing the caller's uid into the stored network record on restart. That field is the resolver's first hint, so it was not one mis-routed request — it overwrote the record every later resolution reads, converting a transient divergence into the stored answer. The sweep that found the conversion sites was scoped to places that consume a uid; this one produces one. A read-only sweep cannot find its own corruption sources.

Deleting the singleton route field produced exactly one compile error, at the construction site. That is the positive evidence that its readers were genuinely converted rather than merely appearing converted — and it is evidence no test in this suite could have produced.

The daemon-wide gateway manager field is host-level, not owner-keyed: it holds a Docker route, and on Linux the route factory ignores its uid entirely while on macOS the host socket hosts zero gateway containers. 29 of its 34 readers are unreachable on macOS via runtime early returns carrying no cfg attribute. Its hardcoded host route is not an unconverted remnant — the named constructor has one production call site against eleven for the route-taking one, which is the shape of a type already converted.

The container runtime is the genuinely owner-keyed one: same route field as the gateway manager but pinned to a gateway VM rather than the host socket. All five of its runtime-trait methods bind an operator uid and discard it while the sibling Lima impl uses the same parameter to select per-operator. Its conversion is internal (route becomes a factory), so no call site changes and — unlike the field deletion just landed — no compile-time tripwire exists to prove it complete.

The startup reconcile pass over session networking is a platform defect, not an ownership one: it carries no cfg anywhere, is called unconditionally, and git history shows it predates macOS support and never gained a macOS branch. Unfiltered iteration over all sessions is not evidence of daemon-wide design — the gateway monitor iterates identically and resolves an owner per row.

The operator agent does not derive the gateway VM it addresses from its own uid. Its live in-VM and Docker paths call a helper returning a hardcoded unsuffixed constant; the uid-derived name is used only by two gateway-creation handlers that have zero daemon-side senders and are therefore unreachable. A prose claim asserting otherwise was written and then refuted by its own author's consequence check.

A sweep for planning-document citations in source anchored on the section sign followed by a digit, making every named-section form invisible to it. True population is 130 occurrences across three classes — external standards, shipped user docs quoted in operator-facing errors, and planning documents — of which only the third violates the convention. The earlier report of a single remaining hit was an artifact of the pattern, not a measurement of the tree.

Two operator-facing daemon-startup failure strings cite a documentation path that does not exist, on the code path where the daemon refuses to start. The repair is not a filename swap: the real file documents the helper only in table rows with no such heading, so correcting the path leaves the section anchor naming nothing.

A correct refactor silently invalidated a verification control: rekeying a recovery latch read from the daemon uid to the resolved operator uid removed the source string three self-test demonstrations were anchored to. The instrument failed loudly rather than passing vacuously, which is the only reason it was noticed, but source-text anchoring is its main maintenance cost.

The planning-document citation class in source is 108 sites, not the two first reported, and 77 of them are live code rather than comments: operator-visible step identifiers printed by the update flow, with four tests asserting on the literals. Fixing them is a refactor of operator-facing output plus its tests, and raises a design question about what an operator should see instead — a spec step number means nothing to someone who cannot read the spec.

A correction that lowers severity: the planning-artifact directory is tracked in git, the cited spec exists, and the section identifiers resolve. The citations are a convention violation and a maintenance liability, not dangling references. The convention still holds, because the rule's premise is that these artifacts may be rewritten or deleted between increments, which tracked-today does not defeat.

Four separate sweeps this session each measured a subset of their intended class because the pattern was narrower than the concept: a section-sign pattern anchored on digits, then the section-sign class itself as a subset of planning citations, since a filename cited without a section marker is invisible to it. Bare milestone identifiers without a session suffix survived a sweep that reported the milestone-tag class clear.

The deferred backlog is over sixty items reaching back many milestones, which is itself a replan signal, but almost all of it predates this arc and is hygiene rather than obstruction. The exception is the item recording that per-operator gateway behaviour has never been exercised with the switch on: every claim about switch-on behaviour derives from probing name derivation directly, so the green unit suite cannot speak to it at all. That is the milestone's central promise and the one thing no amount of further hermetic work can settle.

A token class exists here that no pattern can separate: bare milestone identifiers and Apple Silicon chip generations are spelled identically, and the same literal is a genuine milestone reference in the end-to-end tests and a genuine hardware generation in the install tests, where it explains that nested virtualization needs a later chip. The discriminator is what the surrounding sentence is about, so only reading recovers it. A regex-first sweep of this class corrupts those files, and a careful pattern is not protection, because the pattern is not what rejects them.

A clause can go vacuous a second time, by a different mechanism, and the alarm that caught the first time is blind to it. The invariant checker's line-anchored scan misses chained reads that the formatter has split across lines: re-pointing one clause without also moving it to raw scanning would have found one site of four, reported a non-zero denominator, and looked healthy. Total collapse raises an alarm; partial collapse reports as a working clause.

A control demonstrated that a redundant acceptance term is redundant rather than dead by mutating a real site INTO the shape only that term can carry, instead of deleting the term to see what breaks. The term matches a spelling, not a property, so a correct refactor that rekeys the argument leaves the property intact while the spelling vanishes — which is why the observation and the retirement decision come apart.

One demonstration that had been failing was not a broken control: under the per-operator mode the trigger is supposed not to fire, and its reachability had rested on a daemon-keyed reader that a correct refactor deleted. Recovering it needed a two-part mutation that both injects the per-operator site and restores the deleted spelling, which converts it from a stale control into a regression test for the defect that refactor fixed.

An aggregate comparison cannot see a compensating change. I specified the closed-operation-set guard as a single count against a single constant; a delegate pointed out that deleting one allowed field name and adding one forbidden one leaves the total unmoved while putting a path on the wire. The fix is per-name baselines rather than a sum, and the general form is that any check comparing one number to one number is blind to swaps within its own population.

In this repo's tool shells grep resolves to a ugrep shell function, and zsh does not word-split unquoted parameter expansions though it does split command substitution — so building a file list into a variable and passing it unquoted to a recursive search sends one giant filename, warns on stderr, and reports zero matches.

The milestone-identifier population has now defeated two separate sweeps claiming completeness over it; a case-sensitive pattern reports clean while lowercase citations survive, and one survivor sits inside an f-string assertion message that prints a planning-document path at test-failure time.

Comments inside already-applied SQL migrations are frozen: refinery 0.9.1 defaults abort_divergent to true and the store never overrides it, so a comment-only edit changes the checksum, diverges from the recorded history row, and aborts daemon startup on every deployment that has applied that migration.

The gateway-owner invariant checker's serving-function clause anti-detects rather than merely missing: with the parent counter non-zero it prints an affirmative claim that conversion is done, while a daemon-keyed read one hop below three serving handlers raises nothing. Its serving set is a one-level signature test with no call-graph walk.

Whether a gateway fact is a host property or a caller property is settled at the use site, not by uniformity: the Lima version reads identically from every manager, but what makes it host-scoped is that its consumer's remediation is to upgrade the host binary, so a per-operator answer would be a malformed question.

Three agents independently hit shell-plumbing instrument failures in one session — an unquoted parameter expansion passing a whole file list as one filename under zsh, a bashism returning empty for a piped exit status, and a pipeline exit code read from the wrong command. All produced plausible numbers and none was caught by inspection.

Subagent turns carry no sidechain entries in the shared session transcript, so a delegate cannot recover its own pre-compaction commands from it; any figure carried across a compaction is unquotable by construction unless it was written to a file when taken.

The identifier class has at least four distinct spellings — bare, hyphen-or-underscore two-part, unseparated, and a different letter-pair prefix with a dotted number. A pattern anchored on a word boundary with a required hyphen misses the unseparated form entirely, which is how a container-name literal survived one sweep while being found by another.

A committed invariant checker for the gateway-owner uid now exists and fails on the current tree: two session-creating handlers still read the daemon uid where they should read the caller's. The instrument self-tests by injecting a violation per clause and reports per-clause denominators plus the size of the region it cannot see.

A conditional exemption string in a check reports its reason as fact. One that reads 'converted, IF the parent count is non-zero' certifies completion while an unconverted site sits outside the clause's reach; the repair is two separate changes, deleting the sentence and printing the blind region's size unconditionally.

cargo build does not resolve intra-doc links, so the standard fmt/build/clippy/nextest chain cannot catch a broken bracketed type reference in a doc comment. cargo doc --no-deps -p <crate> runs in about three seconds and is the missing check for any doc-comment-only edit.

Sweeping for milestone identifiers is a proxy for the property that actually causes harm, which is a source file pointing at an ephemeral planning artifact. The proxy only matches where the pointed-at filename happens to contain an identifier, so it found two of the four tracked files carrying gitignored .tasks/ references and reported a complete census.

This repo keeps its milestone and session-plan documents tracked under docs/internal/ rather than the planning skill's default ephemeral location, so a source reference to a milestone document resolves today and is not a dead link. Whether it is nonetheless a durable-surface violation is a separate ruling from whether it dangles.

A uid-forwarding wrapper defeats a sink-anchored invariant check. The checker's patterns anchor on the function that resolves an operator to a route, but a one-hop wrapper that passes its own uid parameter through launders a wrong uid at the wrapper's call site, where no pattern looks. Two such wrappers are known, one with seven call sites, and neither name appears in the checker.

The two route handlers outside the checker's caller-identity landmark are legitimately outside it: one takes no parameters, the other is daemon-wide in which rows it lists rather than which gateway it probes and already derives an operator per row. Fifteen of seventeen is a ceiling, not a shortfall.

The uid-forwarding wrapper class around the operator-to-route accessors has four members across fifteen call sites, all in the daemon entry point, and converges at the second hop because one wrapper wraps another. Enumeration anchored on the parameter type rather than its name, so the finding that no member uses a non-uid-shaped name is a falsifiable negative. Forwarding through a struct field remains unmeasured.

One badly-worded acceptance criterion produced two opposite errors in the same session. Worded around identifiers, it was too narrow to see two source files pointing at ignored planning paths whose filenames carried no identifier, and simultaneously broad enough to invent a document-renaming requirement that the underlying harm never implied.

.tasks/history.json is tracked in git despite /.tasks/* appearing in .gitignore, and carries 587+ self-references. Any repo-wide census of .tasks/ pointers that does not exclude it reports a wildly inflated denominator.

All three citations of one milestone doc turned out to be redundant with a complete explanation already sitting beside them, so the fix was deletion rather than inlining. Generalizes: a pointer that survives next to a full rationale is decoration, and the site that looks like it needs the most care is often the cheapest in the set.

Widening the gateway-owner invariant checker to cover uid-forwarding wrappers found zero new violations: the coverage hole was real but unexercised on this tree. The wrapper class is four members over fifteen call sites, converging at the second hop, and a type-anchored sweep confirmed no member was excluded by a non-literal parameter type.

A control that stubs an instrument dead varies whether it exists, never how deep it goes. For a fixpoint-derived set, only a max-hops cap distinguishes a one-hop scan from a converged one; the two controls feel like the same discharge and having the first is what stops the second being built. A three-rung ladder where each rung removes exactly one case makes the counts between rungs the evidence.

The migration-file freeze covers EVERY already-applied migration, not a named subset. I restated it as two specific files and a third was then found carrying a handoff reference and is unfixable for the identical refinery-checksum reason. The general rule was already recorded correctly; narrowing it to instances is what made the third look editable. State this prohibition as a property, never as a file list.

On this macOS host the \b word-boundary escape is INERT in 'git grep -E' (GNU extension, absent from POSIX ERE, silently matches nothing rather than erroring) while being live in other grep tools on the same host. It fails toward everything-is-clean, so it is at its worst in a control asserting a known-present site is still visible. Use -P or anchor on literal context.

The idiom 'cmd --check && echo CLEAN || echo NOT-CLEAN' converts tool-absence into a substantive negative verdict: the || branch fires on any nonzero exit, so 'the tool is not installed' and 'the code is dirty' produce the same output. A delegate nearly reported a rustfmt-clean file as unformatted this way. Second instance this session of a status check reporting on a different command than it appeared to certify.

The 82-site conversion surface may no longer be reproducible: the sweep script that produced it is not in the tree (embedded inline in a handoff only), and at least one of its six classes is now half-dead because the field it matched has been removed. Until re-derived, treat 82 as a historical number - claiming N-of-82 complete would be a reconciliation rather than a measurement.

Repeatedly correcting a proxy can produce an unbounded scope expansion in which every individual step passes review. Nothing in the local decision surfaces the cumulative cost, because each correction is genuinely a fix to the previous one's blind spot. Budget the SEQUENCE, not the step - and prefer a measured, named, deferred remainder over pursuit of a complete one, since a class defined by a relationship may not be closeable by mechanical means at all.

The .tasks/ tree is NOT uniformly gitignored: the ignore rule reads as covering all of it, but 35 files there are force-added and tracked (34 specs plus history.json), while handoffs (205 on disk) and test-runs (73) are 0 tracked. Never infer trackedness from an ignore rule - force-add is invisible to it; run git ls-files on the subtree.

Measured size of the identifier/dead-pointer class after sweeping vocabulary rather than paths: roughly 30 further dead pointers (18 planning-phase citations, 3 stale todo IDs, 8 hidden by rustfmt wrapping the number onto the next line, 2 miscellaneous), plus about 131 bare planning-phase labels that are the literal target of the in-repo no-milestone-tags rule. Three sites are frozen inside applied migrations and permanently unfixable. Recorded as todos - the bound holds and none of these are being fixed now.

A deferred todo label outlives the measurement that justified it. A todo reading "roughly 30 dead pointers, delete each" is executed by someone holding a regex, not the per-site resolution that produced the count - and here the matching population was five times the dead one and contained live references. Deferred work items must carry the method that distinguishes members from matches, not just the count.

The gateway-singleton sweep class named "docker route pinned to daemon uid" reports zero today, and its patterns are aliveness-checked live. But the patterns match two spellings, one of which (a field on AppState) was removed from the codebase entirely. The property is still present at the lite create-session site, which no class-C pattern can match. So that zero is a false zero with respect to the property, and it accounts for 49 of the 67-site drop. A pattern surviving an aliveness check still cannot see a property that was respelled.

The per-operator gateway switch-on path is covered by neither tests nor static checks, and these are the same hole seen twice. The lite create-session site that pins the docker route is invisible to the sweep class named for exactly that property, and the switch-on behaviour has never been exercised end to end. So the one code path that changes when the flag flips has no test and no checker, and a green suite plus a green sweep say nothing about it.

Outside-the-surface was used as a deferral reason and should not have been. The lite create-session route site was set aside partly because it fell outside the 82-site sweep surface, but that surface was never the scope - it was what one pattern set could see of the scope. A site is outside a regex population for reasons that have nothing to do with whether it matters, so membership in an instrument output is not a prioritisation signal.

Verified a delegate’s output against its artifact rather than its report, which never arrived. Index compaction went 20311 to 17045 bytes with 112 entries before and after, zero link targets dropped, 10 sections both, and all five bolded index-only tails confirmed present in their topic files. The suspicion that hitting the byte target exactly meant trimming-to-target was wrong. Bound: the backup covers only the index, so content deleted from a topic file during migration would be invisible to this check.

Correcting an earlier entry: the sweep class named "docker route pinned to the daemon uid" falling from 49 to 0 is real remediation, not pattern decay. A named commit on master deleted the last bare-field sites and the successor spelling takes an operator uid by construction, so the zero is true of the construct the pattern matched. What was wrong was the class name: it named a property that lives in two constructs while matching only one, so the container-runtime site was never counted at 49 either. A zero you can attribute to a real fix is the hardest kind to re-open.

A test doc-comment justifies itself by citing a struct field that was deleted months ago, while the test it describes is correct. The surrounding occurrences of the same string are all a longer, still-existing name, so a substring search reports the site as healthy. Same name-versus-successor trap as the route class.

A delegate has now produced three proxy censuses in a row with the same profile: full precision, recall between a quarter and a seventh. Each time it collected the class it was incidentally looking at rather than the class it was naming, and each time it had just been corrected on the previous instance. Intimate knowledge of the mechanism does not prevent it; only measuring the denominator separately does.

After the migration that drops legacy operatorless sessions, every surviving session row carries a non-null operator uid, so an absent operator identity on the container start/create path is a corrupted-invariant case rather than a normal one. The hard error there is justified by the consequence of proceeding (silently resolving to the daemon uid), not by the case being unreachable.

A prose-pointer instrument that read only doc comments was biased, not merely imprecise: plan references cluster in doc comments while local step labels live in line comments and assertion strings, so the undercount was systematic and would have persisted at any sample size. Corrected population is 193 across three classes, not 131 across two.

A comment in the event-ingestion pipeline test now states that daemon-wide SIGTERM emits no gateway shutdown event, which is true only because that path is missing. It names the shutdown-signal function rather than a line, so whoever fixes the defect will find it by grep. The comment must be updated in the same change that fixes the defect.

A census anchored on the route saw one of four argument positions carrying an identity at a single call site, measured against a converted twin found by reading rather than by the pattern. Route-anchored methods undercount identity-carrying arguments roughly fourfold there.

The broker executor holds a uid taken from getuid, stored on a struct and read back at five sites -- the exact shape of the route defect -- and is correct, because the uid is a discriminator in an equality test rather than an identity to act as. What separates the two is what the value is used for, which no pattern over shape can see. Confirms narrowing the checker's class name rather than re-basing its pattern, and constrains how the behavioural test must be written.

No production path needs registry credentials, and the argument is structural rather than a census: the routed seam is a closed op set with an exhaustive argv match, and every variant that creates a container routes through a builder pinning the pull policy to never. The one path that does contact a registry is the Linux lite image build, which is off the routed seam entirely and pins its own client-config directory, so no user's config is consulted regardless of HOME.

Grepping for the word pull to find registry contact returns about sixty hits that are almost entirely an unrelated workspace subcommand. The word does not spell the property; what settled the question was the closed op set and the pull-policy constant.

The lite-image build inherits the justification written on the host docker route -- runs in the daemon's own context against the daemon's own Docker -- without being that route, so the premise was never written down beside it. On macOS the premise is exactly what fails, and the daemon says so in its own words elsewhere in the same file. Same shape as the broker gate: a justification that lives elsewhere and nothing traverses.

A delegate corrected its own count of macOS-branched image touchpoints from three of five to four of five after a grep listed a call site its reading said should not exist. The misread came from starting a read window below a compile-time branch arm. The correction strengthened its conclusion rather than weakening it, which is the direction that gets least scrutiny.

A pointer can be live and still wrong: a source comment cited a specific line range of an events document as authority for preset merge semantics — intact phrase, plausible line numbers, wrong document entirely. No liveness or staleness check can see this class; only asking whether the target is the kind of document the claim would live in.

Two documented instrument traps on this host — a word-boundary escape that matches nothing in git grep -E, and unquoted shell variables not word-splitting a pathspec under zsh — were both walked into by an agent that had already written both down. The remedy that worked was a liveness control returning nonzero in the same invocation, not the note.

Measured across 28 code-to-doc citations: every defect sits in a line-number range and every named section anchor resolved exactly. An anchor breaks loudly when its heading is edited; a line number rots silently on any insertion above it. Cite by anchor, never by line number.

A wrong line range was found copied verbatim into two files along with the sentence it accompanied. Pointer defects propagate by prose reuse rather than by independent authorship, so identical citations are one defect and should be found as a pair.

The platform branch on diagnostic remediation text was applied by check identity — is this check about a Linux facility — when the property needing the branch is guidance content: does this message name a command that exists on the host reading it. The two axes agree on three checks and diverge on eleven, so the defect regenerates with every check added.

Two copies of one piece of platform knowledge exist, one correct and one not: the installer marks certain privileged setup steps skipped on macOS, and the update-failure recovery text prints them unconditionally. The correct-copy/wrong-copy split is the shape that regenerates, not the wrong copy itself.

A pattern-based census of platform-facility usage was bounded by its own coverage control: a known class member found by reading contains no facility token at all, so the sweep cannot see it. The 681 ungated hits are a lower-bound generator, not a population; precision against the graded class is about two percent.

A single source of truth across the installer shell and the Rust update path is not achievable: the step list exists only as 128 string labels at call sites with no struct, enum or table to derive from. The shell copy stays a second copy, tolerable because it is the correct one and the Rust copy is the one that drifted.

A shared cargo target/ that has hit the pathological-bloat state does not fail loudly — it makes test binaries hang at startup, and intermittently. One agent saw a nextest run exit 144 with an empty run phase after a clean build and could not explain it; a second agent independently diagnosed the tree as no longer able to start test binaries. Same condition, two agents, neither able to see the other's evidence. Treat an unexplained empty or truncated test run in a shared tree as a host symptom to correlate across agents, not as a one-off to shrug at.

A document name appearing in a source comment in this tree is not evidence that the document exists or ever existed. A 2026-05-23 strip removed named spec anchors; a follow-up repair commit reconstructed plausible document names to fix the resulting broken sentences. A machine-invented document name reads as authoritative in a way a bare line number never does — a line number is visibly mechanical, a named document looks like a person citing something real. Treat every document name in a comment as unverified until checked against the commit that introduced it.

The build-tree hard-link failure is reached at a far lower size than the project doc records: the documented instance was ~150 GB / ~1.4 M files, this one was 25 GB / 489k files, both with the deps directory at the filesystem's 65535 hard-link cap. Size is not the discriminator and the recorded figures read as a threshold. The invariant is the link cap; the two symptoms are binaries hanging at startup at 0 CPU and a test run exiting 144 with an empty run phase after a clean build; the fingerprint is cargo's reported size disagreeing with the filesystem's reclaimed size, one summing over links and the other counting each once.

The bulk comment edit that stripped internal document references also substituted one word for another about 139 times, and roughly ten of those hit the word where it named a value in the code rather than the document, leaving comments that describe the code incorrectly today. The mechanism is that a substitution keyed on a word cannot distinguish that word's senses, and the affected word doubles as a widely used local variable and part of a type name. Repair is one word per site and exactly recoverable from the parent commit, but only when the pre-edit line and surrounding code are read at each site rather than pattern-matched.

The question of whether comments that attribute a constraint to a document without stating it need separate repair is closed by measurement, not by judgement: the full population of 114 locator-less role-noun comment sites was walked with context, and the subset that loses a constraint is empty. The four that attribute without restating lose only a rationale or a pointer to further reading, with the constraint stated in the same comment. Also measured: a rustdoc pointer and the thing it points at are usually adjacent, so reading a comment line-scoped systematically overstates this class.

Free space is a true and useless instrument for the build-tree hard-link failure: it read 653 GiB before the clean and 678 GiB after, and would have shown healthy at every moment of the failure. The direct probe is the maximum hard-link count in the debug deps directory, where the filesystem's u16 cap is the fault and a small number is healthy; it measures the cause in one command and costs nothing when the answer is no.

The macOS config-migration rewrite of the per-uid allocation config is a latent trap, not live data loss: the installer's Darwin branch stamps the current schema version at creation and was introduced already doing so, so no host installed from source has ever held a pre-migration file. That population is empty rather than small. The only route to it is an operator hand-writing the file before install, and the transform is additive and preserves unknown keys by construction. What is real is that the macOS arm has no backup for that rewrite on either the installer or updater side, while the installer branched the Linux equivalent correctly.

The installation guide states that an absent or zero schema version in the per-uid allocation config is brought up to date by the framework on the next daemon start. The daemon never migrates config, and the loader's minimum accepted version makes such a file a refuse-to-start. An operator following that sentence gets a dead daemon, and the sentence is also the generator of the only population the migration trap can act on, so repairing the code without it leaves the input source live. Cross-platform, not macOS-specific.

Whether the macOS daemon should require the per-uid allocation config at startup is an open question in the record, not settled behaviour: an earlier milestone found startup refusing on that file's parsing before reaching its own prerequisite checks, and argued the shared validation is wrongly un-gated on a platform that allocates from a different pool. Any correction to recovery documentation that cites the current un-gated call sites as authority is building on the disputed side of that question.

The bulk comment edit's damage to precise document citations was manufactured rather than authored: in at least two files it deleted the resolvable path and kept the unresolvable part reference, which is the mechanism that produced the population of bare section markers. That inverts the reading of those sites and makes recovery mechanical, since the deleted half survives in history. A repair pass over them must read every candidate first, because at least one comment in the same population exists specifically to record that a path is dead and would be destroyed by a mechanical repair.

The HTTP proxy hands a raw operator uid to the owner-keyed docker-route factory, which on macOS builds a route naming the operator rather than the daemon, so the executor takes the operator-agent branch. The agent derives its docker endpoint from its own per-user Lima home and refuses it as a parameter, while with the per-operator-gateway switch off the gateway lives under the daemon's, so the socket does not exist. This is the one member of the owner-uid class whose direction is inverted: wrong on the current tree and correct once the switch is on, because the collapse becomes the identity. The invariant checker never opens that file, its own header names the blind region, and the sole test over the proxy state builds a factory that ignores its uid parameter and is therefore structurally unable to observe a collapse.

A question inherited through a context compaction arrives pre-formulated and reads as settled, which is how a false equivalence inside it survives reissue. The question asked whether a commit puts the daemon on the local executor arm while holding an operator uid, asserting parenthetically that this was the condition making a dead branch live. Those are complements: the branch goes live on an uncollapsed uid, and the described state is what is observed when the collapse did run. Answered as asked the answer is yes, so a true answer would have closed the investigation on a false basis.

A commit that described itself as a comment refactor changed 360 non-comment lines out of 3625, including user-facing text in five shipping files and an assertion pinning one of those messages. A later commit repaired its collateral damage, listed five fixed categories and reported that all five verification greps returned no hits; three damaged sites are live in the tree because those greps were comment-scoped, copied from the damage commit's own description of itself. A repair's search space must be derived from the damage's diff, never from its scope sentence, and when one of N verification claims proves under-scoped the other N-1 came from the same method and are unaudited.

The same bulk edit rewrote a phrase meaning proposed-by-a-document into one meaning derived-from-measurement, inside a document that states two sentences later that the measurement was never performed. This is a distinct failure mode from flattening two senses of a word: the substitution upgraded the strength of a claim rather than its vocabulary, manufacturing a provenance assertion. It is detectable only where the surrounding prose happens to contradict it, so anywhere the neighbours were silent it now reads as fact.

The lite-image rebuild endpoint has no platform gate although its sibling image-ensure path does, and the underlying build spawns docker with no route or host override, so it targets host Docker unconditionally. The CLI default selects every backend, so the plain rebuild command reaches it on macOS. Where a host docker exists the build succeeds and returns success while the image sessions actually use inside the gateway VM is untouched. Separately, the macOS lite image has no refresh path outside a source tree at all.

On macOS the SSH-shaped surface and the guest-agent surface open a socat stream into the same container but resolve their route through different functions, so an operator gets working exec alongside broken ssh, cp, sync, git-remote and IDE attach. A wholly broken backend is found immediately; a backend whose first operation works and whose second silently does not gets attributed to the second thing. Unequal operator and daemon uid is every shipping and test configuration on macOS, with equal uid appearing only in one documented dev override, so the failing half is not an edge case.

The e2e test named for the headline lite-on-macOS SSH promise opens no SSH connection; its body exercises the guest-agent path instead, which is the one that resolves correctly. This is not a coverage gap but a coverage gap that asserts it is covered, so an audit asking whether the path is tested finds the name and stops. Third instance today of one shape: a check structurally incapable of observing the property it is named after, reporting green. The other two were a route factory that ignores its uid parameter and a repair commit whose verification greps could not reach the region where its damage was worst.

The bulk comment-rewrite commit was never a one-token rename: ~1270 removals of one term against ~145 replacements with the obvious substitute, the remainder becoming a hand-written vocabulary of role-nouns. Its own commit message is false on scope, on line-kind, and on kind-of-edit.

Three delegates independently found the same class in that commit: replacements that assert something the originals did not — a document exists, a measurement happened, the subject is right. All read as more rigorous than the bare citations they replaced, and none is findable by pattern.
