M11: close the DNS-rotation propagation race architecturally. CoreDNS resolves new IP and answers VM in <1ms, but sandboxd dns_propagation_loop polls resolved.json every 2s — VM's TCP arrives at gateway nft set before the IP is admitted, deny-logger RSTs. Phase 3's CARGO_FASTLY_CIDR_POOL (9d1dca7) and #39 GITHUB_INTERACTIVE_CIDR_POOL (874a9bb) work around this for known CDN supernets but don't generalize. Two viable architectural fixes: (C) inline nft add element from sandboxpolicy CoreDNS plugin's WriteMsg interceptor BEFORE returning DNS answer to VM (race-free, cross-language coordination — Go plugin writes nft state managed by Rust daemon, risk of divergence with rebuild-from-cache model); (D) synchronous gating where CoreDNS plugin holds DNS response until sandboxd acks nft update (file/fifo barrier, adds DNS latency but architecturally clean). Both require redesigning the propagation contract; out of scope for polish session. Investigation handoff in M10-S8 progress log.

S9 candidate: no per-source UDP rate limit in sandbox-deny-logger. TCP path enforces a per-connection cap; UDP only has a per-process cap. A noisy sender from a single VM can starve the deny-event channel for other sessions.

S9 candidate: conntrack netlink recv buffer fixed at 4096 bytes. Adequate for IPv4/UDP entries but a CT entry with rich extension NLAs (mark, timeout, helper) could exceed it. S9 candidate (review m3): in sandbox-deny-logger UDP receive loop, conntrack lookup runs unconditionally before rate_cap.try_admit(). Under a deny storm at >cap rate, every dropped datagram still pays the netlink send+recv cost. Cheap fix: invert order so lookup only runs on admitted datagrams (rate_limited summary doesn't need per-datagram tuples). Pairs naturally with #108 UDP rate-cap hardening.

S9 candidate (review m4): conntrack netlink Socket is in blocking mode (netlink_sys::Socket::new doesn't set SOCK_NONBLOCK) and lookup runs inside tokio UDP task without spawn_blocking. Either (a) add a comment explaining why blocking is acceptable here, or (b) wrap socket in tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd (the impl AsRawFd is already there). conntrack.rs:236-258, udp.rs:107-141.

S9 candidate (review m5): iter_nlas in conntrack.rs:489-516 allocates Vec<(u16, &[u8])> per call, called 3-4x per kernel reply (top-level, IP sub-tuple, proto sub-tuple). M18-S10 deferred: lite-image entrypoint chown for the non-1000 operator case. For operator uid != 1000, the container runs as that uid but /home/sandbox is owned by 1000 mode 0700 → EACCES on home-dir writes. Fix paths considered: (a) drop Dockerfile 'USER 1000:1000' + bundle gosu/su-exec, container starts as root and entrypoint chowns + drops to operator — bigger image surface; (b) bind-mount a host-side /home/sandbox dir pre-chowned to operator_uid by the daemon — refactor of image's /home/sandbox semantics; (c) chmod 0777 /home/sandbox in the image — security regression. None of (a)/(b)/(c) is M18 critical-path. File for M18-S11 review or M19. Surfaces only when operator uid != 1000.

Broker CHECKIN deny path returns no error frame to the peer — the operator's client sees only a dropped connection with no reason. No test asserts the PRODUCTION enrollment group resolves on the host — the gap that let the broker deny every operator on a production config while the whole suite stayed green. Every broker test drives the membership gate through the test-env-override seam pointed at a synthetic group that exists, so the gate is tested correctly but the identity it gates on never is. This cannot live in 'make test' (it is a host-provisioning assertion, not a hermetic one, and would fail on every CI runner). Right home is 'sandbox doctor' or an e2e precondition. Same shape applies to the vmnet slot account, so cover both identities in one check.

Coverage hole in the nextest feature-flag split: every make target that runs nextest passes --features sandbox-route-helper/test-env-override,sandbox-lima-helper/test-env-override (make test and both branches of make test-integration), so the two NEGATIVE-CONTROL tests run under no make target at all - route_helper_users_conf_path_ignores_env_in_default_build and route_helper_path_resolution_ignores_env_in_default_build. Those two assert the test-only env-override seam is INERT in a production build, i.e. that a test hook cannot be used to redirect a privileged helper's path on a shipped binary. They are exercised only by the bare 'cargo nextest run --workspace', which is what the macOS CI job runs (ci.yml:284); Linux CI runs make test. The two jobs cover the union but neither alone does, and a developer running make test locally never verifies the seam is disabled in production. Net effect of the flags is +6/-2, which is why the counts differ by 4 (2173 vs 2169). Fix likely a make target that runs the default-build negative controls explicitly. Touching the Makefile's feature flags has blast radius, so this was deliberately left out of the #85 fix.

Nothing in the system observes that a vmnet slot socket is UNOPENABLE by the operator; the one check that catches it, doctor C25, catches it by independently asking a directory question. Two blind spots. (a) scripts/darwin-vmnet-drift.sh has no group or membership logic at all - it compares plist argv against loaded-job argv, and reported exit 0 on all 8 slots while the operator could not open a single one. Not a bug (wrong tool), but 'drift is green' must never be read as 'the pool is usable', and the docs should say so. (b) Doctor C17 and the daemon's own startup probe (gateway_lima.rs:2430-2434, sandboxd/src/main.rs:13450-13477) both count sockets with Path::exists() and never attempt connect(2) - and they evaluate from the DAEMON's credential, which runs as _sandboxd and can therefore open these sockets by construction. C17 reported '8/8 slot sockets present' throughout the entire period the operator was locked out. A reachability check should connect(2), and should do so from the credential that actually needs access.

Session-name collision: reject create when a live row already holds the name, make name resolution report ambiguity the way the id-prefix branch already does, and delete the row on every failed create rather than only on the vm-created rollback. Unblocks 58% of the macOS e2e failures and stops remove-by-name silently deleting the wrong session. Triage called it trivial and obvious and deliberately left product code untouched.

Operator-agent survivability across a full e2e run, two independent causes: the harness gives the agent an unread stdout pipe that fills and wedges it, and daemon-restart tests kill the privilege wrapper rather than the daemon, orphaning daemons and leaving the broker socket rebound-then-dead. Without both, no full macOS run is meaningful.

SEVERITY ESCALATION of the deny-event loss recorded earlier in this milestone: measured to affect the FULL backend as well as lite, because the gateway container is attached to the VM-facing network after the entrypoint resolves its address. Deny visibility is broken on macOS across both backends with test-visible impact; enforcement is unaffected and still fails closed.

Promote the harness-survivability verification tests from the scratchpad into the committed e2e suite: they assert the agent survives past the old pipe-capacity wedge point and that a daemon restart replaces rather than accumulates daemons. Deliberately kept uncommitted during the graded reruns so collection stayed at 160 and the comparison was not muddied. Both properties are currently unguarded by any committed test.

PRODUCTION: daemon panics at startup with a nested-runtime error when the session store holds Lima rows and daemon uid differs from operator uid, which is the normal macOS deployment. Startup reconciliation is invoked bare from async main and reaches an executor that blocks on the current runtime handle. Fix by moving that call onto a blocking task or making the path async, then sweep for other synchronous executor callers on async paths. Blocks all e2e measurement past run position 63.

The comment block above the executor's runtime-handle call is stale and partly self-contradictory: it says a temporary single-threaded runtime can be created, then does not create one, using the current handle instead. The behaviour is correct given the documented precondition, but the prose invites someone to re-break the nested-runtime crash that just cost a production restart path. Rewrite it to state the precondition rather than describe an approach that was not taken.

PRODUCTION: the macOS full backend never installs the Lima guest's default route to the gateway, so the guest has no egress at all - verified by an empty default route inside the guest against a healthy daemon-side view. It fails closed, so enforcement is intact and the backend is simply unusable for allowed traffic. Twenty-four e2e failures trace to it. Determine first whether any macOS path is meant to install this route; the Linux path is never reached on macOS.

macOS lite sessions get no per-session gateway re-create from the runtime monitor, following the backend guard added to stop the full-backend macvlan path from claiming them. The previous behaviour was doubly wrong (wrong setup function, guessed interface) so removing it was correct, but a correct lite re-create path was never written.

The gateway monitor's re-create-failure arm leaves the per-session networking status untouched, so a session whose gateway re-create fails still reads Healthy on the wire until something else changes it. Narrower than the refusal case because it retries each tick, but the same observability gap.

Run cargo clean on this macOS host before the next long session: target/ is 41 GB with 531k files in debug/deps, approaching the documented threshold where freshly-built binaries hang at process start. Transient subprocess-spawn timeouts under parallel test load have already been observed.

A throwaway probe account at uid 599 cannot be deleted: the directory service is wedged on deletion specifically while writes to the same record still succeed, and the underlying store is protected from file-level removal even as root. It was hardened as far as writes allow - no authentication authority so it cannot log in, false shell, hidden, in no groups, real-name marked as stray - and is invisible to the daemon's operator derivation. Clear it with a directory delete after the next reboot.

The name-printing subcommand of the operator-group script bypasses the operator-name validator that every mutating path uses. It only prints, so it is not itself exploitable, but its output is exactly the kind of thing a caller pipes into a privileged command - which would launder an unvalidated name through a trusted-looking helper. Route it through the same validation.

The group-membership resolution helper now exists in three places: the privileged broker authorization path, the doctor's deliberate mirror, and the new bookkeeping read. Mirroring is the established pattern here and the broker copy was deliberately left alone, since it is an authorization decision and a bookkeeping session has no business touching it. Consolidation is a candidate for a session that can properly own the privileged path.

Twenty feature-gated broker items, including the multiplexed-stream tests, are compiled by neither the hermetic nor the integration test tier - each passes different feature flags and neither passes theirs. They exist, are named as tests, and never run. Either wire the feature into a tier or remove them; dead tests create confidence nobody is entitled to.

The brokered request write is still awaited on the control loop, so an agent that stops reading its socket entirely can stall dispatch for that operator. Distinct from a slow response and unchanged by the pipelining work, which bounds response waits only. Bound the write too, or document the exposure where the no-wedge property is claimed.

Bound the logging for discarded stray-identifier response frames on the broker control connection. Currently one warning line per frame, and a buggy or looping agent produces them at whatever rate it emits - this milestone already measured a listener spinning at roughly twelve lines a second for four minutes from exactly that shape. Prefer a counter surfaced with the other broker state, or a rate-limited warning, over a line per frame. Suggested during the transport session and not implemented; the agent died on a server-side error before starting it, tree left clean.

The diagnostics path runs a docker listing with no socket flag at all, so on macOS it queries a host daemon that does not exist. Latent and pre-existing, found while re-counting the Docker surface; outside the lifecycle family's criterion so deliberately not folded into that refactor.

The e2e harness probes the staged daemon with a hard ten-second timeout and no retry, in a session-scoped fixture, so a single slow first exec voids the entire suite with eighty-five cached setup errors and zero tests run. The first cross-uid exec of a freshly relinked binary can exceed that budget in code-signing validation; it is one-time per binary identity, so a retry would clear it. Its failure message also names a missing privilege fragment as the cause, which is wrong and sends the reader to a working subsystem.

Add a container-scope entry to the macOS e2e defect catalogue for the policy-persistence restart test: it fails reproducibly at the same position under container scope, at both the pre-session and post-session commits, on the post-restart allowed leg with a resolve failure - and passes when run alone. The catalogue currently records only the full-scope run, where that test sits behind different load and passes while its other backend variant fails at a different leg. The catalogue should state that a full-scope inventory does not project onto narrower scopes.

The brokered executor discards its timeout argument and awaits the reply channel indefinitely, bounded only by agent liveness. Operation budgets are therefore enforced on the local-socket route only, and the newly-migrated policy and firewall operations inherit that. Pre-existing to the brokered seam rather than introduced by it; belongs to whoever owns the control lane.

The brokered executor discards its timeout argument on both trait implementations, so operation budgets are enforced on the local route only. Explicitly not taken by the streams session, whose seam takes no timeout at all - it is on the one-shot path. The next session touching the one-shot op surface should own it.

Stream-class operations acknowledge readiness BEFORE the own-uid gate runs, so a wrong-uid request yields an empty stream rather than a control-connection rejection. Pre-existing behaviour and the security property holds because the agent refuses to act either way, but gating before acknowledging would be tidier and would make the refusal legible.

Within one session, a DNS query arriving while the gate listener is being re-armed finds no socket and gets no injection - fail-closed but lossy. Forced by the deliberately un-forked listener shape and pre-existing; recorded rather than fixed because parallelising the accept loop would break the gate rather than speed it up.

The route-helper presence check reads the daemon's machine home rather than the owner's, which is correct only while the degenerate path is in use. It must move to whichever side owns the file once ownership flips; the operation already names the file rather than pathing to it, so the change is on the reading side. Candidate for the ownership phase.

Record in the macOS e2e catalogue that the npm-preset test has now been observed failing with the resolver shape as well as its usual event-assertion shape, joining the two preset tests already known to oscillate that way. All three trace to the same load-sensitive guest-side resolver flake and all fail in the safe direction. The catalogue currently records only the earlier two.

Add a per-session refusal rule outside the container network namespace so a pre-route connection attempt fails fast rather than black-holing. The property is already closed without it - this improves the signal, not the guarantee - but an in-container process currently waits eight seconds where it could get an immediate error. Needs to work on both platforms with its own teardown and lands on the route helper's authorization surface, so it is a session rather than a clause.

Lead for whoever fixes the full backend's missing guest route: measured that attaching the private-mode macvlan moves the gateway container's default route onto it, after which that container cannot reach the internet at all - an address-resolution failure the isolation mode produces. Recorded as a measurement, NOT as an explanation of the catalogued failures, which are a guest-side missing default route in a different place. Someone working that defect will want this fact; it is not itself a diagnosis.

Reinstall the test operator agent binary before the ownership phase begins. The installed copy predates ten commits that touched its crate, including two new wire variants. It is harmless while operations dispatch locally on the daemon-owned machine, but once ownership flips they route through the agent by design and an unknown variant surfaces as a deserialization failure rather than a version complaint. Prerequisite, not hygiene.

Add a dedicated rollback test for the new gateway egress address field on the network record, analogous to the one covering the operator uid field. The property is correct by construction - no unknown-field rejection plus a serde default - and is implicitly covered because the existing rollback test deserializes into a struct lacking both fields, but a direct test would pin it rather than leaving it incidental. Raised as belt-and-braces by the enforcement review, not a correctness gap.

Repair the gateway machine's stub resolver, which has selected a non-functional address-family upstream so the machine has working IP egress and no name resolution. It was deliberately left dead as the controlled condition for an attribution bisect and is no longer needed as evidence. It is the direct cause of at least one catalogued test failure and a plausible contributor to the resolver-shaped oscillators.

The harness helper that reads daemon log lines since a marker is returning an empty window, so two golden-image tests fail on log-marker assertions even though the daemon demonstrably emitted the expected line at the right moment. Harness defect, not a daemon defect, and it currently hides whether those two behaviours are correct.

The per-operator machine home now holds base-image metadata with no corresponding instance directory - the inverse of the state that caused the previous rebuild. Left untouched because removing it would be a fix rather than a measurement. The next full-scope run should not be surprised by it.

The macOS e2e catalogue treats the guest-resolver flake as one class when it is demonstrably two - a fast resolve failure and a resolve timeout - which separate cleanly by backend half and may have different causes and different fates. The catalogue should re-partition them explicitly and say it is correcting a conflation, not quietly re-draw the boundary. Blocked on the resolver mechanism measurement.

Record in the catalogue that counting failure shapes by grepping stderr for the curl error string is an invalid instrument: it silently under-reports tests that invoke curl in silent mode, and the under-report has already made a false conserved-count conclusion look supported by the data. Generalises past the resolver question to any shape-counting over this suite.

The e2e catalogue should name the three distinct resolvers separately - host, machine stub, and per-session gateway container DNS - because they are currently conflated and the conflation already produced one wrong causal claim in the backlog. Guest-side lookups traverse only the third; the stub serves the machine's own container daemon.

A permissive in-VM socket mode is justified in a comment by the same single-tenancy premise the route-helper perimeter rests on, and it will be false once the machine becomes operator-owned. Distinct from the perimeter claim this session corrects, not named by the threat-model section, and out of the current phase's scope - but it rests on the same dead premise and should be revisited by the ownership phase.

The read-only recon agent type has no write capability and its instructions forbid creating files via shell redirection, so it cannot produce the handoff file the delegation protocol asks every producing agent for. It returned the content inline instead and the orchestrator persisted it. Either give recon delegations a write-capable agent type or stop asking that type for a file.

Delivering the property that an interactive shell into the gateway machine is not a route-rewrite primitive requires removing the login user's blanket passwordless elevation, not merely adding a distinct principal for brokered operations. That in turn requires relocating every privileged provisioning step onto that principal - directory creation, install, mode change, capability set, firewall baseline load. Scoped as several phases of work; recorded so the ownership phase does not inherit the spec's understated version of the option.

Fix gateway-VM DNS blackhole in generate_gateway_eth0_nft_policy() (sandbox-core/src/gateway_lima.rs). Lima's stock hostResolver DNATs the VM's nameserver 192.168.5.3:53 to 192.168.5.2:<high-port> in nat/output (prio -100), which runs before our filter/output chain output-eth0 (prio 0, policy drop) that accepts DNS only on dport 53 -> dropped. Affects the VM's own dockerd (image pulls), NOT the per-session guest path. No out-of-band fix is possible: the generator emits 'flush table' and re-applies on every gateway setup (3x per e2e run), so a hand-inserted rule is wiped inside the run it was meant to enable. Fix must be in the generator: either accept the DNAT'd destination or reorder/exempt. Full measurement in .tasks/handoffs/20260819-gateway-resolver-repair.md

Re-examine any S14 oscillator triage that inferred DNS failure shape from curl exit codes. rc=6 vs rc=28 was measured non-discriminating (rc=6 at 20.06s against a certain black hole), so conclusions resting on that distinction need re-deriving from packet-level or counter evidence.

Resolve the spec precedence conflict: §5.2 requirement 2 ('narrow it', one branch) vs §4 Phase 3 criterion 4 (three branches, incl. not pursuing). Neither text establishes precedence; the recon handoff's inference that Phase 3 supersedes rests on an earlier-draft premise that does not discriminate, since §5.2 self-identifies as the later revision. Substantively moot for security posture (narrowing is a measured no-op given cloud-init's blanket NOPASSWD grant) but it determines whether §5.2 requirement 3 - the perimeter doc rewrite - is formally unblocked. Three independent reads exist to compare: s14 cold read (20260819-phase3-sudoers-perimeter-cold-read.md), the recon handoff, and a third in flight.

Check whether the gateway sudoers fragment is ALREADY narrower than what the daemon actually uses - recon found four elevated commands the daemon relies on that the fragment does not cover, meaning provisioning works only because of cloud-init's blanket grant. If so, requirement 2's 'narrow it' may be substantially satisfied already, which would change how the conflict resolves. Verify against the fragment's real emitted content in generate_gateway_template().

Orphaned spec correction: §5.2's second doc-comment correction (residual TCC framing) is addressed to phase 5, but Phase 5's file table and acceptance criteria contain no matching row - its gateway_lima.rs entries are adjacent line ranges for template interpolation, not the comment sites the correction names. The correction is assigned to a phase that does not carry it, so it will be silently dropped unless re-homed.

Repair defects in .tasks/handoffs/20260819-s15-route-helper-recon.md, which other agents are being briefed from: (a) it labels §5.2 table row 3 'correction 3' and perimeter item 3 'requirement 3' - two different items, near-identical labels, same section, open to conflation; (b) it omits §5.2's correction table except row 3, so the live external-publication prohibition is absent; (c) its early section states the doc-rewrite ordering constraint flatly as settled fact and only qualifies it ~500 lines later, so the flat claim travels badly when quoted alone.

Verify the unverified load-bearing claim behind the sudoers decision: that a brokered op arrives in the gateway VM as the SAME login user an interactive 'limactl shell' gets. Both spec reads flagged this as untraced. If false, the 'narrowing is a no-op' conclusion and the Option C rationale both need re-deriving - trace the SSH user actually used on the brokered path.

Broker op protocol has no version negotiation - an older agent silently drops unparseable lines, so op-set skew stalls to the per-op timeout instead of returning Rejected. Decide whether adding op variants needs a negotiated minimum or an explicit unknown-op rejection.

Subagent-to-subagent delegation to kio-qa-test-runner failed once with the callee declining the task as an unverifiable injection (could not resolve the caller's name in its roster). Determine whether nested delegation needs an identity the callee can verify, or whether reviewers should simply run tests directly. One observation only.

SECURITY, unverified claim needing decision: sandbox-route-helper install_default_route runs Command::new(ip), so the first ip on the inherited PATH is exec'd by a process holding CAP_NET_ADMIN. Verify whether caps actually reach the child, then use an absolute path if so.

SECURITY, unverified claim needing decision: sandbox-route-helper audit_log_path resolves the caller's own XDG_RUNTIME_DIR then HOME then /tmp, so a caller of the cap'd binary selects where its own forensic record is written. Decide on a fixed path; this is the hazard the feature-gated audit-log override was built to avoid.

Consider replacing the exec of ip(8) in sandbox-route-helper with direct rtnetlink calls. This removes the exec of an external binary from a capability-bearing process entirely, rather than hardening how that binary is located. Larger change: new dependency in a security-critical helper, so it needs its own review.

PROBE_CAPS_MARKER in sandbox-invm-argv route_helper is dead after the probe fix: its doc says it is the substring the caller looks for, which is no longer true, and it has no reference outside its own crate's test. Remove it or correct the doc.
Fix the Linux test-compile break in sandbox-core: a cfg(test) module imports a macOS-gated test-support item unconditionally, so the whole crate's tests are unbuildable on Linux.

The install-repair e2e test still asserts route-helper installedness from a single capability name, the weak check just removed from the daemon-side probe. Bring it in line with the all-capabilities requirement.
CI installs clippy but never invokes it, and the workspace lint command omits --all-targets, so warnings in test-only and platform-gated code reach master unseen.

Three capability guards in the main install script compare getcap output with an exact string equality against a kernel-order literal. Correct today, but they break into permanent reinstall the moment a capability is added to either helper - the same ordering fragility just fixed elsewhere.

No regression test locks in either capability-guard fix - the repo has no harness for Makefile recipe logic, and the existing install-script harness covers only the doctor path. A getcap-stub scenario could cover both guards and the production installer's.

A comment in the canonical-binary dev script justifies an overridable marker as existing so a unit test can point it at a stand-in. A controlled repo-wide search found no such test and no other reference to the marker. Dangling justification for an otherwise unexplained bit of indirection.

The doctor route-helper capability check uses the same substring shape just fixed elsewhere, so an over-capped helper reports healthy. It is advisory and gates nothing, and its leniency is deliberate and documented - but it is now the last surviving instance of the pattern, and someone should rule on whether a diagnostic ought to report privilege excess.

Settle whether gateway SSH-key ownership really implies daemon-or-root by stat-ing the key and every ancestor directory on a provisioned host, rather than inferring it from the code that creates them.

Settle the rootless-container deployment claim: the capability mechanism is measured but the assertion about which uid owns the network namespace in that layout is not, and no rootless deployment exists on this host to measure it.

The container-uid mapping rewrites uid zero to a non-zero uid, so prose describing the fallback as the daemon's own uid and gid holds only for a non-root daemon; sweep for other places making the unqualified claim.

Decide whether the agent-memory directory under the tooling config dir belongs in version control or should be gitignored; it is currently untracked with mixed provenance across sessions and would otherwise get swept into an unrelated commit.

An advisory diagnostic carries an unverifiable historical aside about which capability set once sufficed before an alignment change. Same class as the unpinnable predecessor state already removed from the helper: a claim about a past that no commit contains. Decide whether to source it or drop it.

The rewritten installation documentation was verified structurally but the docs site was not built, since that needs a package install and network. Confirm it renders in whichever pipeline builds the site.

The shell harness holding the new capability-guard regression tests has no make target and appears in no CI workflow, so those tests run only when someone invokes the script by hand. Wire it in, or the guards are unprotected against the next refactor.
Confirm the distributed installer artifact is genuinely regenerated from source at release time rather than shipped from a stale checked-in copy; it currently carries the pre-fix capability guard.

Identify the libcap release where the getcap rendering changed. The fix is correct at both ends of the measured range but the changeover point is unmeasured, so the comment states a range rather than a version.

Run a Linux check over the route helper's platform-gated module. The namespace address collection and the binary resolution path are not compiled on the macOS host, so they went into a commit without ever being type-checked.

A comment in the broker describes the agent as checking for a wrapper reference inside the template body on the exact path the ownership flip activates. The agent performs no such check. The comment is false today and sits on a security-relevant path.
The spec's line references into the request handler are stale by roughly five hundred lines. Its references into the validator are accurate, so the file drifted after the spec was written.

The guest agent deliberately cannot depend on the core library and the validator is excluded from the library target, so no test can check the template generator against the validator that must accept its output. Existing round-trip fixtures are hand-pasted copies that drift; that drift is what hid the fifth blocking validator.

The gateway VM instance name is now constructed in two disagreeing forms: the agent's gateway-create derives a uid-suffixed name, while the accessor used by the in-VM and Docker op paths still returns the unsuffixed constant. Harmless only while nothing invokes the gateway-create op; the rename must land in the same change as the daemon-side sender or the created VM will not be the VM those paths address.

The wrapper-validation row of the class-split requirement covers the start path, which this session did not touch: only gateway create was implemented. Confirm whether the start path needs the same treatment before the daemon-side sender lands.

No LimaOp gateway-create variant was added, so the daemon has no way to invoke the new agent operation yet. Adding it forces arms into the Linux setuid-helper path and several other match sites for a macOS-only feature; decide whether the Linux paths get a rejecting arm or a shared shape.

Bound the daemon's wait on a brokered agent reply, and parse incoming frames in two stages so a parse failure can still answer with the originating request identifier instead of being dropped silently. Today an unparseable frame pins a request indefinitely on a blocking thread while the agent keeps heartbeating.

Decide whether the request envelope and the nested operation enums should also close their field sets, as the broker operation enum now does. Left deliberately narrow so the hardening stayed within the scope that was reviewed.

Twelve tests are gated behind crate-local test-env-override features that no make target enables, so they compile in neither the hermetic nor the integration run and are invisible to every count. Decide whether to wire them into a target or delete them; leaving them is the worst option because they read as covered.

The spec's authorization-perimeter section misdescribes the grant it asks to narrow, calling it blanket when the template emits a command-scoped grant naming one binary; its line citation into the template generator is also stale by roughly two hundred lines. The spec's own phase criterion describes the same grant correctly, so the two sections disagree with each other as well as with the code.

Two copies of the claim that the gateway machine is a single-tenant daemon-owned appliance survive in the emitted machine template and its agent-side fixture mirror, where they ship into every gateway. They are true today and false the moment ownership flips, and the permissive socket mode's entire rationale rests on them.
The narrowing that converts the daemon's route parameters into the typed operation's field types has no test, and it is the only unexercised link in the daemon-side chain.

No test exercises the wiring of the containment check inside the privileged helper: the decision function is well covered, but the address collection, its ordering relative to the namespace entry, and the deny path are all in the platform-gated module, and no integration test drives the gateway mode at all.

PRODUCT BUG (macOS, 10 e2e failures): the macOS lite branch runs the create-time local: workspace push as the daemon user via the direct-spawn path instead of the operator-pivoted helper the generic lite branch uses. Its comment gives the reason (no lima-helper on macOS; the forwarded gateway Docker socket is daemon-user-only), but the consequence is that any operator-owned source directory not world-readable is unreadable to the pusher - the e2e tests use a 0700 mkdtemp and rsync exits 23. Predates M24 (introduced 2026-06-20). Fixing this needs a macOS story for pushing as the operator; it is the largest single class in the red container tier.

OBSERVABILITY GAP in the egress subsystem (9-10 e2e failures): allowed-UDP and deny events are not reaching the per-session ring buffer on macOS - the assertions report zero captured events - while enforcement is separately green in the same run (deny, empty-policy-denies-DNS, policy-clear-reverts-to-deny-all, L3 host-mismatch all pass). This is the audit trail for the property the project exists to guarantee, so it must not be filed as benign because it is old. Note the characterisation 'enforcement intact' was measured indirectly, via the enforcement tests passing, not by instrumenting the ring.

HARNESS BUG (7 e2e failures): cross-backend tests shell out to bare host 'docker' for gateway and sandbox containers that on macOS live inside the daemon-owned gateway Lima VM, reachable only via the forwarded daemon-user-only socket - conftest sets DOCKER_HOST for the daemon but not for these tests, so they get 'No such container'. The macOS-aware accessors already exist in the harness but are used only by the macos_only+lima recovery tests; they need extending to the cross-backend ones. Explicitly NOT fixed by the operator-owned gateway VM flip: that changes who owns the VM, not whether there is one.

PRODUCT BUG (macOS, 3 e2e failures): git-remote-sandbox re-execs itself via current_exe(), which on Linux resolves through /proc/self/exe to the real sandbox binary but on macOS returns the symlink path it was exec'd as. The child's argv[0] basename therefore re-triggers the remote-helper branch and parses the --socket value as the URL, failing with 'empty session name in URL'. Reproduced directly against the installed symlink. Pre-existing since 2026-04-14.

HARNESS BUG (3 e2e failures): shared: workspace tests build their source with tempfile.mkdtemp(), which on macOS lands under /var/folders/... while the configured shared root is /tmp/sandbox-shared. The daemon's 400 refusal is CORRECT behaviour and the recent message improvement did not change the outcome - the tests need to allocate their source inside the configured shared root.

HARNESS BUG + PRODUCT GAP (1 e2e failure, one real defect): the lite resource-defaults test learns host RAM by reading /proc/meminfo, absent on macOS where the facility is sysctl hw.memsize. Do NOT platform-mark it - the assertion (lite defaults are 80% of host RAM) is platform-neutral, and marking it would bury the product defect the same run exposed: the daemon logged 548 warnings that /proc/meminfo was unreadable and it was falling back to 4096 MB, which is not this host's RAM. Two fixes needed: the harness helper, and the daemon's macOS host-RAM probe.

HARNESS BUG (1 e2e failure): the L3-fail-closed-before-DNS-propagation test resolves a hostname out-of-band by shelling out to 'getent ahostsv4', which does not exist on macOS. The test's own comment says the only requirement is obtaining an IP without triggering CoreDNS, which socket.getaddrinfo or dscacheutil satisfies. Do not platform-mark it - the property under test is fully meaningful on macOS.

STALE TEST (1 e2e failure, cheapest fix in the red tier): commit bbd9d6f changed the lite shared: TCC log site twice over - it rewrote the message text and dropped its level from warn to debug - without updating test_shared_workspace_tcc_warning, which still greps for the old wording. That needle now exists nowhere in the source, only in the test. Unambiguous one-test fix.

Targeted e2e rerun, cheap (~3-5 min, one file): the npm and cargo preset tests oscillate between the lost-event assertion shape and a guest-side DNS-resolver shape across runs, with three runs recording three different combinations. Rerun test_presets.py -k 'npm or cargo' to determine whether the resolver shape is a load-dependent flake or a second distinct defect hiding inside the lost-event class. Worth doing before anyone attempts to fix that class, not before accepting the attribution.

Unexplained, deliberately not attributed: one Envoy listener rejection in the macOS container-scope daemon log, single occurrence, on the L3 propagation path, with no test failure tied to it. One observation is not a signature; recorded so that a recurrence can be recognised as a pattern rather than re-investigated from scratch.

Audit whether the agent's VM-start path should refuse an instance name that does not already exist. Starting an unknown name creates and boots a VM from the default template, so the operation is silently a creation path; decide whether that is intended and constrain it if not.

Contain the request-handler unit tests: their context points at the live per-operator LIMA_HOME instead of a temp dir, and prior runs left stray YAML files there. Point them at a temporary home, ensure nothing reaches the real limactl invocation, and clean up the files already left behind.

Decide where the gateway instance naming rule lives once it becomes uid-dependent. The rule is in the core crate and the agent deliberately does not depend on that crate, so a per-operator name may need to be known in two places; resolve by duplication, a shared crate, or by having the agent never need the name.

The request-handler dispatch tests invoke the real limactl against the live per-operator LIMA_HOME on every workspace run, and remain uncontained after the wrapper-guard work contained only its own new tests. A cleared-path helper already exists to fix them.

A comment on the create path claims Lima passes the wrapper to the hypervisor via a command-line flag. Unverified. It was deliberately left alone rather than swapped for a second unmeasured claim; measure it and correct or confirm.

Three files sit in the live per-operator LIMA_HOME whose provenance could not be established: a base template that a test run overwrote but did not create, a suffixed gateway config, and an empty-wrapper test fixture. Determine which are debris and remove those; each is named alongside its matching test in the wrapper-guard handoff.

The wrapper-path validation enforces only that the path is absolute and executable, while the module documentation claims it is constrained to a specific privileged directory. Since the path arrives from the untrusted requester, an unconstrained one lets any executable stand in for the wrapper that enforces network restriction, which would hollow out the guard it exists to provide. Decide whether to enforce the documented constraint or correct the documentation, and treat it as security work with its own review.

A wire boolean requesting unrestricted provisioning networking is guarded by a bridge check that is compiled out on this platform. Determine whether the request is therefore unguarded here, and if so constrain it. Security-relevant on the platform this milestone targets.

The claim-under-test discipline applied to review paid off twice in one session: instruct reviewers to treat the implementer handoff as an assertion to check rather than context to absorb. The review found the handoff over-claimed completeness, misattributed which platform's wrapper reads the environment variables, and omitted a route entirely.

Decide whether gating the reaper-exclusion test to macOS is correct or a coverage loss. The reaper is platform-neutral while the gateway Lima module is macOS-only. The question to answer is whether the asserted property exists on the other platform, not whether the mechanism the test uses does; the forward risk is that a later gateway VM on that platform would inherit an untested exclusion.

One production site could not take the instance name as data without changing two public signatures and was left using the fixed constant. Convert it when those signatures are next touched, or confirm it is unreachable once the per-operator switch is on.

Re-confirm whether the two nft-logger bus tests still fail on this platform. A durable note says they deterministically fail; one run shows both passing. Establish the mechanism before trusting either claim - an avoidance note with no recorded cause cannot be falsified by continuing to avoid the thing.

Three production sites still read the fixed gateway instance name, not one. The severe one is in the daemon entry point: with the per-operator switch on, the Docker and in-VM seams would name a non-existent socket and instance. All three must be converted or proven unreachable before the switch is thrown.

Switch-on behaviour for the per-operator gateway has never been exercised end to end. Every claim about it derives from probing name derivation directly. Before the switch is thrown, run the system with it on - this is the gap that the currently-green unit suite cannot speak to.

The integration and e2e tiers were not run against the per-operator gateway wiring change; the integration tier is structurally unrunnable on this macOS host, so the gateway-Lima integration coverage needs a Linux host or CI before the wiring lands.

The gateway manager's Lima home is caller-supplied and never derived from the owner uid, so a manager built for a non-daemon owner would read lite-image artifacts from a directory nothing stages into, failing every lite session at docker create with no such image. Unreachable while the registry has no reader. Fix as part of wiring the registry, not before.

Exercising the per-operator gateway switch end to end is blocked until the daemon entry-point sites that still read the fixed instance name are converted: throwing the switch alone breaks the Docker and in-VM seams. Convert those first, then run with the switch on - the green unit suite cannot speak to switch-on behaviour.

A doc comment asserts that Lima resolves symlinks before binding its socket and that exceeding the path bound surfaces as an error not naming path length as the cause. It predates this work and was carried forward unverified - the implementer that read the block flagged it as the one clause it did not independently check. It is the kind of claim that reads as measured because it sits beside measured ones.

The network record's operator-uid doc-comment claims it is the only persisted routing hint; a session column stamped from peer credentials also exists. Correct the doc-comment and the recon section that repeats it.

The V006 orphan-scan test's integration prefix no longer has a justification now that both enumerators are stubs, but it fails under same-process test parallelism for a pre-existing reason that should be understood before promoting it into the hermetic tier.

The integration test-group filter anchors on start-of-string, so tests living inside a mod tests block never match their declared group and are not serialized as intended. Blast radius across other groups is unenumerated.
Consider making the daemon-uid precondition explicit in the type for both the gateway-owner accessor and the operator Lima-home helper, rather than leaving it as a doc-stated assumption.
Delivery-doc rows for the V006 orphan scan are stale for both the Lima and Docker halves now that both enumerators are stubs.
The shared core crate has roughly 25 pre-existing broken rustdoc intra-doc links across a dozen modules; a doc-link gate cannot be turned on until they are fixed.

The reapers cannot be run while the API is live until their read order is inverted to list host resources first and consult the live-session set second, or a snapshot is interposed. Until then only the startup pass is safe, so an operator absent at startup is not swept until the next restart.

Orphaned VMs belonging to an operator who never checks in are never collected. Behaviour is unchanged by the check-in gate, but the disposal mechanism originally intended for them was refused as unsafe, so the gap now has no owner.

About 30 milestone-style identifiers remain across 8 source files, plus startup-step labels that mirror emitted log strings. The labels cannot be removed blindly without desynchronizing code from logs, so this needs a sweep of its own.
Pre-existing fail-open at the Degraded-tagging site, surfaced as a note during the reaper review and outside the scope of that fix batch.

The Lima helper's module-level exit-code table disagrees with its code: group-membership enumeration failure returns the generic exit code while the table files it under the bad-target-uid code and describes the generic one as argv-parse or exec failure. Fail-closed so it denies correctly, but the daemon distinguishes rejection categories by exit code without parsing stderr, so a group-enumeration failure is currently indistinguishable from an argv error.

The counting fake used by the reaper sweep tests counts only container enumeration, while a real sweep also enumerates volumes and networks once per pass. The pass-count conclusion holds, but the fake measures a proper subset of what a pass does.

The macOS operations guide has a diagnostics field table scoped to vmnet slot assignment and no gateway-recovery section at all. The new declined-sessions field is undocumented for operators; it is empty in every shipping configuration today, so this is a standalone doc commit rather than part of the feature.

A spec row asserts the limactl floor is enforced in three places and names a daemon startup prerequisite check among them. That check does not exist — the only version read at runtime feeds the diagnostics payload. The row also attributes the floor constant to a shared shell library rather than the installer where it actually lives. This row is the live generator of a wrong claim that has now been corrected in two descriptive copies.

Consider whether the daemon should enforce the limactl version floor at startup. The installer blocks below the floor and the doctor check reports, but neither covers a toolchain downgraded after install, which is the gap a startup check would close.

No doctor check reads the recovery-decline field, so an operator has no first-class way to see that their sessions were skipped. Decide whether the decline surfaces as its own check row or folds into an existing gateway row.

Gateway recovery's decline report is not written when the session list cannot be read: the run returns before reporting, leaving the previous run's diagnostics report standing as if current. The doc-comment's inherited claim that it is recorded on every run has been narrowed to say so rather than left false.
The recovery decline report is process-global and coupled to a global trigger. Per-owner recovery needs it keyed by owner, otherwise one owner's declines overwrite another's.

The diagnostics field table in the macOS operations guide documents the vmnet pool only, despite reading as a general field table. The recovery-decline field was placed in a sibling section rather than widening a false scope claim; decide whether the table should be retitled or genuinely widened.

Determine whether a gateway container that starts but fails its egress-policy application can carry traffic before the failure is handled. Three post-start recovery error exits occur after the container daemon answers, so the container is live at that point; if policy is absent rather than merely unverified in that window this stops being a liveness bug.

Determine whether a gateway container that Docker restarts after a gateway VM reboot forwards sandbox traffic with no sandboxd nftables present. The rules are injected from outside the container and are certain to be absent after a reboot, forwarding is a create-time sysctl that returns with the container, and neither the monitor nor the image healthcheck inspects the ruleset. Needs a live gateway VM to answer. This is the project's core guarantee, so it is selected rather than deferred.

The recovery behaviour fix and two prose corrections share a commit because the corrected sentences name the return value that commit introduces, so the prose cannot be reverted independently of the behaviour. Acceptable here, but worth noting that a claim naming a new type is structurally coupled to it and cannot be staged separately.

Decide whether a pending retry should continue to suppress the probe-threshold trigger. The backoff is calibrated for repeated failure of the same recovery, but it currently also delays response to a newly-crashed gateway, which is different information.

Decide whether a retry should force-stop a healthy VM after a post-ready failure. The blast radius covers sessions that were never part of the failed pass, and it manufactures restarted gateway containers, which is the unmeasured core-promise scenario.
Nothing removes a networking status entry when a session is deleted, so the map retains dead sessions for the daemon's lifetime. Harmless to reporting, an unbounded slow leak.

Establish whether the gateway VM eth0 baseline reaches nft as a single transaction or as separate commands. The policy text opens with a flush of its own table, so if it is not atomic then every application of it opens a window in which that VM carries no eth0 policy at all.

The gateway VM baseline is applied last in both the recovery restart and the general startup path, leaving a window of up to ninety seconds on one and much longer on the other in which the VM carries no eth0 policy at all. Reordering it is a behaviour change on the security path and belongs in its own session.

Establish whether nft -f commits its whole stdin as one netlink transaction, since that is a property of the binary rather than of this tree. Populate a table, then feed it a payload that flushes the table and ends in a rule the kernel rejects. An empty table afterwards means every failing baseline application leaves the VM bare. Needs any Linux with nft; the gateway image already carries it.

A doc comment states the gateway baseline is applied via nft -f on a tempfile. It is stdin. The tempfile shape it describes, a fixed path under the VM's world-writable tmp, is recorded eleven lines below as one of two earlier shapes removed as security defects, so the comment documents a vulnerability as the current design.

Session deletion never removes the session's networking_status entry; the three clearers all sit inside the per-session loop of the recovery pass. Unbounded slow leak, invisible on the wire — no API surface reflects it, so it will not show up in any e2e assertion.

Gateway container docker run argv has two independent definitions - the shared argv crate for the VM route and a hand-built argv in gateway.rs for the host route. They agree on the restart policy today but nothing enforces it: the shared crate's hardening test pins privileged, read-only, cap count, absence of bind mounts and docker.sock, and image-last, but asserts nothing about the restart flag on either route. Only the session-container policy has a test.

The gateway VM eth0 table's two chains have opposite defaults: the output chain is policy drop with enumerated accepts (fail-closed), the input chain is policy accept with enumerated drops (fail-open). Both input drop rules are qualified on ct state established,related and new,invalid, so a conntrack state matching neither falls through and is accepted. Not demonstrated as reachable - it needs a notrack rule that this table does not install - but the asymmetry itself is the hazard: someone adding a rule to the input chain will assume fail-closed by symmetry with its sibling.

The session policy ruleset renderer joins allow-list elements into nft text with no escaping of any kind. Safety today rests entirely on the compiler binding only the parsed-CIDR destination variant and skipping every other kind, so a parsed CIDR cannot render a metacharacter. That is a real guarantee and an unguarded one. Make the invariant enforceable rather than incidental: a type that cannot hold nft metacharacters, or a test that goes red if another destination variant becomes reachable on that path.

The two ruleset-application paths are not equivalent and only one is capped. The docker stdin path enforces an 8 MiB artifact ceiling; the in-VM baseline op sits in the validator no-check arm and has no size ceiling at all. Harmless while its body is a compile-time literal, but the asymmetry is undocumented.

A spec row still describes a multi-KB nft ruleset written by heredoc and applied with sudo nft -f through a gateway shell helper. That helper no longer exists; the path was replaced by the typed in-VM op.

A milestone doc's trailing paragraph says a parenthetical appears in the spec MUST and in the networking design doc. It no longer appears in the design doc; a later commit changed it there. Stale rather than false, and in text the correction commits did not touch.
Decide and implement the gateway's response to a Docker restart-policy restart, which leaves the container running with an empty ruleset while its healthcheck still reports healthy

The gateway crash-recovery e2e test induces failure with docker kill, which is SIGKILL from outside and bypasses the entrypoint's own exit logic, so it never exercises the real child-death path; it asserts only that a container with a new ID appears and asserts nothing about the nftables ruleset
Reconcile the gateway image tag: the reachability audit reports the workspace version as one patch level below the tag another measurement found present on the host
The gateway container healthcheck asserts five process-liveness conditions and never checks that the egress ruleset is present, so a running gateway with no enforcement reports healthy
The gateway monitor places no deadline on how long a container may report Starting; it continues past that state indefinitely, so a container that never becomes healthy is never recovered
Four comments asserting the nftables deny-all floor is unconditionally in place from t0 are false after any container restart; one of them justifies the monitor's demotion of Starting to Healthy

Policy distribution's else-branch reasons that leaving sandbox_dnat intact is fail-closed because its chain shape was laid down at gateway-create time; after a restart that table does not exist and the reasoning inverts
The combined nftables injection helper in the gateway module has zero callers anywhere in the tree

Six source comments carry design-spec section references (gateway.rs x2, policy_distributor.rs x3, sandbox-docker-argv/src/gateway.rs x1), which the no-planning-identifiers rule forbids. Two more in gateway_lima.rs sit inside functions the cleanup batch already touches and should be fixed there. RFC section references are legitimate and are not in scope.

The gateway-singleton sweep script is not in the repository — it exists only in a session scratchpad, while the verification criterion names a committed tools/ path. Either commit it at a real path or the criterion is uncheckable as written.

Six sites carry a hedge stating the forward-path reasoning has not been measured, which is now stale: two in the gateway Lima source and its emitted comment, two in milestone documents, and two spec-file corrections. Promoting them from inferred to measured-second-hand is a permissive change that strengthens claims resting on evidence whose raw logs no longer exist, so it needs a deliberate pass with the second-hand status preserved, never a sweep.

A comment in the policy end-to-end test claims an inner process reports its exit code through the shell status variable, but after a pipeline that variable carries the last stage's status rather than the inner command's. Harmless to the test since a length assertion carries the weight, but the comment is wrong and was independently confirmed wrong by two agents.

Close the packet-level gap under the forward-path conclusion by observing counters on the eth0 table's drop rules during an external UDP or TCP probe. The current support is a ruleset that was read plus netfilter semantics applied to it, not a counter that was observed.

The workspace fails to compile on Linux because two argv crates are declared only under a macOS target dependency table while cross-platform daemon code references one of them. Pre-existing and unrelated to the current conversion work, but it means no Linux build gate can pass until the dependency declaration is moved, and it silently hides whether any cross-platform edit type-checks there.
Adjudicate the third copy of the unsupported forward-path clause in the M20-S2 session summary; the audit that disposed of the other two never covered it.

The unresolvable-session-owner fallback ruling is unexercised by the landed conversion; confirm the remaining call-site batches either implement it at the callerless startup and reaper paths or record that no such site exists.

Reconcile the 89-versus-90 operator-uid occurrence count between the implementer's report and the verifier's repo-wide census; the substance was confirmed by direct census but the arithmetic does not reconcile and neither party should guess which file was missed.

Rename the route-factory field to name its owner-uid contract; it is the only one of three similarly-named route resolvers that must not be handed an operator uid, and its name is the least distinguishing.
Cover the one-line delegation from the route accessor to the extracted collapse function; the extraction moved the tested boundary down a level and left the field access untested.

Define 'request-serving handler' mechanically before any call-site invariant depends on the term; the operator-parameter operationalization identifies only four functions because top-level handlers spell the extractor differently.

Add the session-registry contract to the call-site invariant: no argument to the session manager registry may be a collapsed owner uid. A violation breaks per-operator session VMs only when the switch is on, and passes every check written so far.

Verify the remaining items under the 'PROVEN LIVE on this host' header in the earlier session summary; only the egress clause has been examined and the header's remaining authority is assumed rather than itemized.

Consider whether a caller identity arriving inside a struct rather than as a named parameter should count as request-serving; the adopted definition would read such a site as non-serving, and no such site exists at the anchored commit.

Unmeasured and not to be relied on in either direction: whether a guest process that does not need the reply can push payload through the externally-established socket. No payload flowed in either observed run. Do not write code against this until it is measured.
Census whether the timestamp-iterated-into-an-array defect in a log entry's completed field affects other entries.

A documentation file carries a false descendant of the no-forward-chain fact at three lines near 420, 425 and 438; the fact itself is elsewhere. Fold into the hedged-site sweep rather than fixing in isolation.

The checker's truncation at the first test-region marker is a latent silent-pass: guard it in the instrument by asserting the cut point sits beyond most of the file, rather than checking it by hand each run.
No crate in the workspace denies rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links, so intra-doc links are unchecked by the build and test path; decide whether to deny it at the workspace root

Route-factory field rename: execute once the call-site instrument is re-baselined and the daemon-side sweep is quiet, with the Linux cross-check as a hard gate and a post-rename denominator re-measurement

Unresolvable-operator policy: enumerate the routes to the Unresolved variant and check whether orphaned gateway rules are collected anywhere; if the variant is under-discriminated, split it as its own change ahead of the call-site conversions

Name-to-uid resolution is single-shot while the uid-to-name direction retries three times with backoff for a documented transient-failure mode, and it collapses error and absence; add the matching retry and distinguish the two outcomes

Record the gateway owner uid on the network record at placement time as an optional defaulted field; must land strictly before the per-operator switch is ever flipped or the absent case becomes uninterpretable
A comment above the deferred orphan-gateway reap carries a milestone identifier, against the project rule that milestone tags belong in git history rather than source

Eighteen assertion-message construction sites join events with a generator expression whose iterand is only safely a list by producer typing, not by any enforced annotation; a helper refactor that let a string reach one would fabricate per-character output inside a failing test's message. Decide whether a typing guard or a defensive check is warranted at the producer.

The policy addon's request hook calls its check with no exception handling and assigns the response only afterwards, so any raise from that check leaves disposition to mitmproxy's addon manager. If that is fail-open the egress promise has an untested hole; no test covers it because the suite mocks the mitmproxy module. Depends on the source reading now in flight.

The macOS pool restore collapses a store read's not-found and error cases into one absence, and the Lima branch then skips the entry silently — not declined, not counted, not reported as leaked. Whether that is a slot double-allocation risk or only a lost accounting entry depends on whether the pool registry is the sole authority on slot occupancy; measurement authorized and in flight.

Two frozen expectations in the call-site instrument disagree with the tree by one and neither is explained: an out-of-scope pin whose anchor now matches zero where one was expected, and a whole-tree census returning sixteen against an expected seventeen. Each is either a site that changed without anyone noticing or an expectation that was never right; both readings matter and a stale frozen number is exactly the dead-alternative signal.

Leak detection cross-checks the slot registry against the store in one direction only. Add the reverse: a live session whose slot the registry does not hold. That is the direction the silent-drop defect produces, it is currently unobservable, and the existing metric moves toward looking healthier when it happens.
Assign the deny response before emitting the deny event in the policy addon, so enforcement does not depend on a different file's exception handling staying exhaustive
Correct the two event-writer comments that name a 500 as the consequence of a raise; the real consequence is the request reaching the origin server
Wrap the policy addon's request hook so it denies on unexpected exceptions, making it fail closed independently of the addon manager's swallow-and-continue disposition
Validate that the policy rules field is a list when loading addon config, falling back to deny-all rather than implicit trust
Scope a test that drives real mitmdump; the addon's current suite mocks mitmproxy, so hook-exception disposition cannot be regression-tested in process

Fix the deny logger's bind address so denied TCP is recorded; it binds the address discovered at container start, before the session bridge is attached, while the redirect targets the session-bridge address
Make port-53 records in the allow stream distinguish a DNS request being made from one being permitted; denied DNS currently appears as an allow
Resolve the gateway VM host-namespace DNS breakage caused by the baseline external-interface ruleset; the accept for port 53 never matches because the guest nat chain rewrites the port first
Check whether a cold SSH without connection multiplexing survives the baseline external-interface input chain in the gateway VM
Correct the unfiltered session reader's documentation, which names two consumers that are structurally incapable of calling it given its visibility
Confirm at runtime that the generated ruleset actually loads on a live host - agent enrolled, broker up, nft exiting zero - since delivery is currently traced by reading only

Convert the ten residual daemon-route call sites to per-operator resolution. Strictly ordered after the network-record owner-uid fill: three of the ten have no caller identity in scope and can only resolve through the already-public network-info reader once that field is populated, the alternative being to widen a deliberate access-control boundary. Refuse at the two helpers returning Result, log-and-skip at the three returning unit, matching the two precedents already in the tree; drop the proposed daemon-uid fallback, which has no precedent and causes a permanent 250ms respawn loop at the gate-bridge site. Also correct the comment at that site pre-arguing its own exemption.

The network-record owner-uid fill now blocks two things, not one: the per-operator switch being flipped, and the three caller-less residual call sites. Schedule it accordingly rather than as an independent cleanup.

Examine backtracking behaviour of the authority-parsing regex in the proxy addon against an agent-controlled Host header. This is a hang rather than a raise, so it is a different failure mode from the fail-open census and was explicitly not measured by it; a stall on the enforcement path has its own disposition.

Open the content-encoding inference call in the response-text setter: it is invoked outside the surrounding try block, so unlike the rest of that boundary a raise there is not absorbed. It is the one unexamined subtree sitting on the deny path with no handler above it, and its answer could change the fail-open from latent to live.

Reclassify the daemon-wide route construction pin from the out-of-scope category to the class it belongs to: it expects the site to persist when that site's disappearance is exactly the conversion being performed, so it fires when the work succeeds. The residual-count expectation derives from the same belief and moves with it.

The list-sessions unfiltered accessor carries the same 'not for handler code' contract as the single-session one but is pub with no enforcement. Either narrow it to match, or document why the boundary is one-sided — right now the weaker sibling is the obvious route around the stronger one.

The comment justifying the session-operator resolver's step ordering becomes false once the persisted owner field is populated. It is a rationale comment, not a description — leaving it makes the resolver's stated reason contradict its own behaviour.
The network-record rustdoc claiming the owner field is macOS-only and None on Linux rows becomes false after the backfill. Correct it with the migration, not after.

Owner-invariant checker: teach it the caller-side delegation class, where the collapse happens in the caller and the sink receives an already-collapsed value. Currently reports a false positive on correct code.

Owner-invariant checker: the host-scoped carve-out is defined independently in two checks that already disagree about one site. Unify to a single definition — two notions of the same exemption will diverge again, and the next divergence may be permissive.
Gateway recovery latch is written and read under two different uid keys, so the latch is never observed and concurrent recovery races silently. No existing check flags either site.

Proxy hook: the content-encoding inference call sits outside the try block of the function that calls it, so a raise there is uncaught on the response path. Not covered by the in-file exception census.
Proxy hook: authority-regex backtracking is a hang, not a raise, so the exception census cannot see it. Needs a separate look at the latency axis.

Gateway health probes cannot observe enforcement: all five check processes and HTTP, none inspects the ruleset. A green probe on an unenforcing gateway forecloses investigation and suppresses every recovery trigger. Add a ruleset assertion to the health check.

Policy re-delivery restores per-session artifacts only. Deny-all, DNAT and masquerade come back only on a full gateway re-create, so a gateway that loses its base ruleset is never repaired by the reapply path.
On macOS the gateway monitor skips container-backend sessions, so a lite gateway detected not-running is only rebuilt at daemon startup rather than by the monitor.

Question, not yet a defect: the macOS Lima create path never calls apply-policy at all, unlike the lite path which distributes during create when a policy is supplied. Check whether the CLI issues a separate policy call, and whether the asymmetry is intended.

Two unread delivery results: the rollback path is best-effort and logs-and-continues, and the empty-policy flush discards its result with let underscore. The latter is the only delivery call whose outcome nobody reads.

Highest severity of the store-boundary prose class: the unfiltered session-lister's summary paragraph asserts per-caller isolation it does not implement, and rustdoc renders that summary in the module index. A reader who stops after the first paragraph is told the unfiltered lister is safe. Move the paragraph to the filtered sibling, which currently has no doc comment at all.

Production, end-user-facing: the gateway VM nft baseline drops DNS in the VM host namespace because Lima's DNS chain rewrites the destination port in nat OUTPUT before filter OUTPUT evaluates the port-53 accepts. Rules must match the rewritten packet, not the port the application used.

Both image loaders return success when the staged tarball is absent. Combined with no explicit pull flag anywhere, an unstaged host silently falls through to a registry pull instead of failing with the actionable no-such-image error the code comment promises. Make a missing staged image an error, or set an explicit pull policy.

Sweep the policy-delivery handoff for the loose phrasing that the gateway VM DNS defect breaks all DNS from the host namespace. The correction was made in a message; the file still carries the overclaim, and the file outlives the messages.

Read whether a TCP counterpart to the Lima DNS redirect exists. The UDP append was read to its end; the chosen fix claims to cover both transports, so if TCP is redirected and the fix lacks the matching term it is wrong in the fail-closed direction on TCP.

Determine where the gateway container's DNS server forwards upstream. If it resolves via the VM's own resolver, whether an end user can write a policy naming an internal host depends on the VM's DNS view - a live question about what policy can express. If it forwards to a fixed public resolver, internal names were never resolvable and that is a documented limit rather than a defect.

Gateway DNS policy can revert to the entrypoint default while the container still reports healthy, so a session silently runs with the default allow-list and nothing detects it. Same wrong-axis defect as the nftables blindness but on the DNS axis; confirm the direction it fails in, since the default being deny-all makes it an availability bug rather than an escape.

Undetermined: what the proxy's readiness endpoint returns for a server with no listeners. Probably two questions rather than one - whether the listener source delivered an empty set, versus never delivered at all - and a single answer would be wrong for one of them. Left unmeasured deliberately rather than inferred from recalled documentation.

Propose paired comments at the component-readiness timeout constant and the Dockerfile health directive naming each other, so the fifteen-second margin between them stops being an untied coupling between two files.

The comment justifying the macOS DNS upstream choice guarantees only that it never weakens deny. Add a sentence naming the availability cost it accepted - that internal names became permanently unresolvable on that platform and policy expressiveness now differs across platforms. Scoped doc change, belongs with whoever next touches that path.

The chosen nftables fix carries unvalidated syntax: a rule-file check needs Linux and cannot run on this host's native toolchain. Establish before merging whether the check is a genuine parse-and-evaluate that would catch an error in the conntrack-original idiom, or whether it needs kernel state a throwaway container cannot provide - in which case a green result is a check on the wrong axis.

GatewayManager::inject_nftables has zero callers anywhere in the workspace, tests included. Decide whether to delete it or wire it up — a dead nftables-injection entry point beside a live one is a trap for the next reader.

Lite gateway containers auto-restart rule-less and are excluded from repair by construction: the Lima recovery path snapshots only Running Lima sessions, so a restarted lite gateway is never revisited. Fix the selection, not just the repair.

Record at the macOS container-backend recovery skip which platform actually loses enforcement and which does not. A skip inside a platform arm reads as a platform property and will be misremembered as covering Linux lite, which it does not.

Whenever the container-restart rule loss and the gateway VM DNS defect appear together in the working document, state that they sit on different surfaces and that the DNS fix does not touch the restart defect. They have travelled together only because they surfaced together.

The pull-policy documentation claims override environment variables control image pulling, but they do not reach the argv builders' image-tag parameters at all. Decide whether to add the plumbing or narrow the documented promise; the doc is being corrected to match reality first.

New macOS-gated code in the Lima gateway module gets no Linux CI coverage, including eighteen tests of the image-presence predicate. Decide whether the macOS half of the matrix runs anywhere automated, or accept that it is verified only on a developer host.

The gateway's CoreDNS health endpoint is declared with no bind address, so it listens on all interfaces and is only kept unreachable by the base table's trailing reject. Bind it to loopback so its reachability does not depend on a firewall rule surviving.

When the ct-state-new DNS gate rule is implemented, ship it with a comment naming the established,related baseline accept it depends on and what breaks if that accept is moved or removed: the gate silently degrades to first-packet-only and DNS breaks for any resolver reusing a source port.

Gateway health predicate cannot observe rule loss: it reads process liveness only, so a restarted gateway container with an empty ruleset reports Healthy. Fixing this alone is insufficient and arguably harmful — control then lands in a recovery arm that discards the container backend, yielding detect-warn-continue every 30s. Any remedy must address all three barriers together: an observation of netns-younger-than-last-injection, a predicate that carries it, and a lite-shaped repair arm.

The docker inspect format is a closed six-variant enum with no restart signal (no RestartCount, StartedAt, FinishedAt), and there is no docker events consumer anywhere in the tree, so the daemon cannot currently express the question 'has this container restarted since we last injected into it'. This is the barrier that must be cleared first, because the other two repairs have nothing to trigger on without it.

Rewrite the gateway health predicate's doc-comment premise as a failure condition rather than a justification: it currently states the deny-all floor is in place from t0 as a reason the probe need not read nftables, which is true only for a container the daemon created and false for a restarted one. State what voids it.

Trace whether a gateway-VM restart on macOS lite reaches the same rule-less end state via the gateway recovery path, whose selector filters on Lima only. USER-FACING BUG, container backend. The runtime's session map is populated only by register_session, which is called only on create paths, and is never rehydrated at startup. Test gap is an intersection: one e2e test restarts the daemon but never stops/starts the session, another stops/starts without a daemon restart. The startup hydration loop rehydrates the event bus, the vm-ip map and the subnet allocator from existing networks and skips this map sitting beside them, so anyone searching for the restart path finds that loop and stops at the wrong object. Likely deserves its own session.
